studi.t: Palmitic acid promotes glomerulosclerosis via TGF-β1 upregulation in podocytes
studi.s: Podocytes are terminally differentiated visceral epithelial cells of the glomerulus and play a vital role in renal filtration. Nevertheless, they are vulnerable to several insults in obesity and metabolic syndrome. Obesity-related glomerulopathy (ORG) is characterized by podocyte hypertrophy, reduced podocyte density, and secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). However, how lipid overload, particularly palmitic acid (PA), whose plasma levels are frequently elevated in obesity, injures podocytes remains incompletely understood.

studi.t: STL1267 alters HIF-1α and REV-ERBα localization and transcriptional responses in CoCl2-treated HeLa cells
studi.s: Background: REV-ERB nuclear receptors regulate gene expression and cellular metabolism, but their role in the response to hypoxia-associated stress remains unclear. We examined how the REV-ERB agonist STL1267 affects protein distribution and gene expression in HeLa cells exposed to cobalt chloride (CoCl2). Methods and Results: Immunofluorescence microscopy and RNA sequencing were used to compare vehicle-treated controls, cells exposed to CoCl2 plus vehicle, and cells exposed to CoCl2 plus STL1267. Representative images showed stronger nuclear HIF-1 staining after CoCl2 exposure.

studi.t: Revealing the platelet transcriptome using Siphon-seq: a sensitive, purity-aware method for RNA-sequencing
studi.s: Platelet transcriptomics is limited by the exceptionally low RNA content of platelets and by disproportionate contributions from contaminating cells to bulk RNA-sequencing libraries. We developed Siphon-seq, an approach that deliberately overloads independently barcoded single-cell partitions to increase aggregate platelet RNA input, then computationally identifies and removes partitions containing contaminating RNA after sequencing.

studi.t: Confocal Live-Cell Imaging Under Ultralow Irradiance Using Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensor
studi.s: Confocal laser scanning fluorescence microscopy (CLSFM) is widely used for three-dimensional live-cell imaging. However, high irradiance is required to overcome dark counts in photodetectors, often leading to observation bias. In this study, we examine whether a CLSFM system equipped with a virtually dark-count-free superconducting transition-edge sensor (TES) can enable live-cell imaging under low irradiance, thereby mitigating observation bias.

studi.t: EHMT1 and EHMT2 Control the Timing of Cortical Neurogenesis Through H3K9me2-Dependent and -Independent Mechanisms
studi.s: The precise timing of neural progenitor differentiation and cell fate specification is critical for establishing the size and cellular diversity of the cerebral cortex. However, how chromatin regulators control the temporal progression of neurogenesis remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the cooperative roles of Euchromatic Histone Lysine Methyltransferases 1 and 2 (EHMT1 and EHMT2) in mouse cortical neurogenesis. We demonstrate that EHMT1- and EHMT2-mediated H3K9me2 deposition is dispensable for H3K9me3, and that these histone marks occupy distinct chromatin regions.

studi.t: Resource enrichment and utilization underlie widely observed production and biomass scaling relationships
studi.s: Broadly observed trophic scaling patterns relate the biomass of predators to the biomass of prey, and biomass to productivity. The consistency with which these patterns are observed suggests the existence of governing principles that apply across ecosystems. We present a model for the trophic interaction between phytoplankton and zooplankton that produces the scaling patterns as an emergent property of resource enrichment without invoking the influence of phenotypic or genotypic diversity on system structure.

studi.t: Community responses outweigh species-level plasticity in shaping future marine forests
studi.s: Anthropogenic ocean warming (OW) and acidification (OA) are progressively reshaping marine ecosystems, yet ecosystem-level evidence remains limited. Marine forests are foundational ecosystems that support highly productive and diverse communities. Understanding how macroalgal communities will assemble, perform and persist in future ocean conditions requires integrated evidence capturing concurrent shifts in primary productivity, species interactions, and associated macroalgal community responses.

studi.t: A conserved dimerization motif squelches transcription
studi.s: Squelching is an indirect inhibition of transcription that results from redistribution of cofactors away from DNA. Here, we describe a class of Lis homology (LisH)-derived peptides that act as transcriptional squelchers. LisH domains are a highly conserved motif found in 10s of thousands of proteins and are composed of ~30 amino acids in a helix-turn-helix fold.

studi.t: Contrasting plasmid-host associations shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) colonization factors
studi.s: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) causes a substantial burden of diarrhoeal disease, but how its virulence plasmids spread across E. coli populations remains unclear. We generated 479 complete ETEC genomes and combined them with 56 publicly available assemblies to produce the largest plasmid-resolved ETEC collection to date. Clustering of 903 virulence plasmids identified distinct plasmid lineages associated with individual colonization factors (CFs).

studi.t: Making monkeys of caregivers: Evaluating the use of caregiver behaviour as social enrichment for lab-housed Rhesus and Cynomolgus Macaques
studi.s: Enrichment is pivotal to captive animal welfare. Social enrichment is of particular importance for social animals who, due to laboratory space or protocols, are not housed in larger groups. The objective of our study was to see if caregivers could act as an additional source of social enrichment to pair-housed research macaques. 5 adult Rhesus (Macaca Mulatta) and 3 adult Cynomolgus macaques (Macaca fascicularis) were enrolled in the study. Every day, for 3 weeks, caregivers would spend 6 minutes interacting with the monkeys during afternoon feeding.

studi.t: Wilson disease mechanisms manipulate ATP7B activity
studi.s: Copper is an essential cofactor for enzymes involved in diverse processes including mitochondrial respiration and the metabolism of neurotransmitters, collagen and melanin. However, its redox activity requires tight homeostatic control. The P-type ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B help deliver copper to cuproenzymes, and ATP7B mediates the excretion of excess copper into bile. Pathogenic ATP7B variants cause Wilson disease (WD), leading to copper accumulation in organs including the liver, kidney, and brain, and to disruption of copper-dependent processes.

studi.t: De Novo Design of Miniprotein Binders Targeting the Leptin-Binding Site of the Leptin Receptor
studi.s: The leptin receptor (LEPR) regulates appetite, energy balance, glucose homeostasis, and neuroendocrine function and is closely associated with obesity, diabetes, and neurological disorders. Activation of LEPR signaling suppresses appetite and promotes energy expenditure, whereas impaired LEPR signaling and leptin resistance are commonly associated with obesity. Accordingly, modulation of LEPR signaling is a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.

studi.t: Workflow for Assessing Mass Spectrometer Performance in Shotgun Lipidomics
studi.s: Reproducible and testable analytical performance of mass spectrometers is critical for inter-laboratory concordance of quantitative lipidomics analyses. However, common instrument readout or analyses of arbitrarily chosen lipid mixtures do not lend themselves to direct comparison between instruments independently configured and operated in different laboratories under in-house settings.

studi.t: Sterically Controlled Conformational Gating of Rhodamine Spirolactam Switches for Super-Resolution Imaging
studi.s: The reversible interconversion of rhodamines between nonfluorescent spirocyclic and fluorescent ring-open states underpins fluorogenic probes and spontaneously blinking dyes for super-resolution imaging. Existing strategies mainly tune the equilibrium between these states through electronic modification, whereas the role of conformational return in ring closure remains less explored. Here, we establish steric regulation of rhodamine spirolactams through amide N-substituents. Bulky substituents generate intramolecular repulsion with the xanthene scaffold, favoring ring opening.

studi.t: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
studi.s: Objective: Conventional microelectrode arrays (MEAs) are suboptimal for long-term electrophysiology of three-dimensional (3D) excitable tissues, as limited oxygenation, nutrient diffusion, and tissue-electrode coupling compromise recording stability. Air-liquid interface (ALI) culture mitigates these constraints, but existing ALI MEA platforms are limited in channel count, flexibility, and compatibility with commercial multichannel acquisition systems.

studi.t: Stress granule transcript contrasts between colorectal cancer compartments depend on scoring and depth
studi.s: Stress granule (SG) gene-set scores summarize transcription associated with stress-response machinery, but their stability across scoring definitions is uncertain. We compared fibroblast-epithelial expression contrasts for four fixed SG lists in two colorectal cancer single-cell cohorts containing 195,527 cells from 85 donors. Analyses used donor pairing, gene-wise standardized expression, within-cell ranks and raw-count pseudobulk summaries, with tissue and sequencing-depth sensitivities. At least 20 tumor cells per compartment were available for 15 and 29 paired donors.

studi.t: Identifying disease-associated dysbiosis in image-based spatial microbiome via MiSA
studi.s: Background: Extensive studies have revealed the associations of microbiome dysbiosis with disease through compositional analysis of 16S rRNA amplicon or shotgun metagenomic sequencing data. However, dysbiosis in spatial organization of microbiome inhabiting the body sites and its implication for diseases remain understudied.

studi.t: Averaging in gene perturbation benchmarks hides perturbation-strength variation: Consequences for model evaluation
studi.s: Perturbation-response benchmarks usually represent each genetic intervention by averaging all cells assigned that perturbation label. We inquire what perturbation-strength information is lost by this averaging, and whether current model predictions preserve enough perturbation-specific information for this perturbation-strength variation to be evaluated. Using X-Atlas/Orion CRISPRi screens, we use depth-corrected guide abundance as a cell-level proxy for perturbation strength and examine how transcriptional responses vary within a nominal perturbation.

studi.t: Flux Transformer learns intracellular metabolic fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates
studi.s: Cells convert incoming nutrients into energy and biomass via metabolic fluxes. Quantifying these fluxes involves feeding cells isotope-labeled nutrients, quantifying metabolite labeling patterns, and inverting the labeling data to retrieve the underlying flux distribution. Traditional metabolic flux analysis (MFA) is both computationally expensive and frequently requires manual refinement of the cost function to obtain plausible results. For this reason, MFA has remained inaccessible to non-experts.

studi.t: Gene set selection for classification with single-cell RNA-seq
studi.s: Marker genes are important for analyzing and interpreting single-cell RNA-seq (scRNAseq) experiments. They are used to identify and categorize cell types and can also be useful for the design of downstream experiments. We present CellSieve, which tackles the problem of finding effective gene sets rather than distilling markers one at a time.

studi.t: Theory of large-bead AFM compression of pressurized rod-shaped bacteria
studi.s: Motivated by our atomic force microscopy (AFM) experiments measuring turgor pressure in living bacteria, we develop a theoretical description of pressurized spherocylindrical cells compressed by spherical probes whose radius greatly exceeds the cell radius. In this global-loading regime, the mechanical response is governed primarily by cell geometry and turgor pressure, while the elastic properties of the cell envelope enter as higher-order corrections. The strong confinement imposed by the probe drives water efflux from the cytoplasm, thereby increasing the turgor pressure.

studi.t: ERM proteins antagonistically control cancer invasion and metastasis via mechanosensing regulation
studi.s: Metastasis requires cancer cells to overcome anchorage dependence and rewire mechanosensing pathways. Here, we identify the ERM proteins ezrin, radixin, and moesin as key but antagonistic regulators of breast cancer metastasis. Expression profiling across matched low- and high-metastatic breast cancer models revealed consistent upregulation of all three ERM proteins in highly metastatic cells. Despite this, ezrin depletion reduced colony formation, invasion, and lung metastasis, whereas radixin or moesin depletion enhanced these phenotypes.

studi.t: Ion channel-enhancing nanoparticles reprogram T cells in vivo for cancer immunotherapy
studi.s: In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), immunotherapy is frequently ineffective due to the impaired ability of tumor-infiltrating T cells to sustain calcium-dependent cytotoxic effector functions. Kv1.3 potassium channels in T cells are essential for maintaining membrane potential, which is necessary for Ca2+ influx; however, they are suppressed within the tumor microenvironment, and no pharmacologic Kv1.3 activators are currently available.

studi.t: β-catenin/TCF signaling represses GUCY2C hormone expression through a p38α-GATA2 axis in colorectal cancer
studi.s: Guanylin (GUCA2A) and uroguanylin (GUCA2B) are paracrine hormone ligands of the tumor-suppressor receptor guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C). In early colorectal tumorigenesis, expression of GUCA2A and GUCA2B is silenced through transcriptional repression by APC-regulated {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling, a pathway activated early in malignant transformation. This repression depends on a locus control region (LCR) 1,000-3,683 bp upstream of GUCA2A.

studi.t: 2-Cys peroxiredoxins facilitate phosphatidylglycerol unsaturation and contribute to PSII recovery from high-light photoinhibition
studi.s: The level of fatty acid unsaturation of chloroplast lipids is a key determinant of plant acclimation to different environmental stresses. Though the enzymes catalysing fatty acid desaturation are well known, the regulatory mechanisms linking their activity to environmental signals remain poorly understood. In this work, we have addressed the role of chloroplast 2-Cys peroxiredoxins (Prxs), thiol peroxidases that play a central role in redox regulation, in {omega}-3 fatty acid desaturation in lipids of the organelle, and their contribution to plant acclimation to environmental stress.

studi.t: CortexDecoder: Efficient fMRI-to-Image Reconstruction from Cortical Flatmaps
studi.s: Recent brain decoding work has shown the potential of Vision Transformers (ViTs) to learn mappings from neural representations to visual features. Here we present CortexDecoder, a framework that reconstructs viewed images from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) flatmaps, which are neural responses projected onto the cortical surface and unfolded into 2D images. We show that a frozen, pretrained cortical foundation model is sufficient for competitive reconstruction.

studi.t: A multimodal arrayed Perturb-seq platform for dissecting microglial state dynamics and target identification
studi.s: Microglia are highly dynamic immune cells of the central nervous system that can adopt diverse functional states in health and disease, making them both emerging therapeutic targets and challenging systems for target identification. Here, we developed TF-iMG, a human pluripotent stem cell-derived transcription factor-induced microglia model generated by inducible expression of SPI1 and CEBPA in Cas9-expressing stem cells.

studi.t: Spatial atlas of gut-draining lymph nodes reveals the developmental organization of intestinal tolerance and immunity
studi.s: Early life offers a window to establish lasting tolerance to dietary and commensal microbial antigens. How developing gut lymph nodes balance tolerance and immunity remains unclear. Using spatial transcriptomics, we map small intestine- and colon-draining nodes during weaning and adulthood, resolving rare immune and stromal populations and their niches, including Thetis cells (TCs), an antigen-presenting lineage critical for intestinal tolerance.

studi.t: Continuous generation of short-lived resident effector CD8 T cells sustains alopecia areata
studi.s: CD8 T cells mediating chronic tissue inflammation have been thought to depend on stem-like progenitors that self-renew and replenish cytotoxic effector cells or exhausted progeny. Here, we show that stem-independent, short-lived resident effector CD8 T (TRE) cells sustain alopecia areata (AA), a common autoimmune disease that destroys hair follicles. AA-TRE cells exhibit TCR-dependent cytotoxicity, undergo rapid apoptosis in the skin, and lack memory or stem-like properties.

studi.t: Cell identity and activation state determine the innate immune response to nanoplastics
studi.s: Autoimmune disease is on the rise, and while no direct connection has been made, evidence suggests environmental toxins such as nanoplastics may be contributing to the increased incidence. A key factor in the onset of autoimmunity is inflammation; yet how nanoplastics impact innate immune function is unclear. Here, we exposed primary human neutrophils, macrophages, and endothelial cells to biocorona-coated polystyrene nanoplastics at physiologically relevant concentrations. All cells internalized nanoplastics without viability loss, but functional consequences diverged.

studi.t: Host HSP90 mimicry by a parasite effector triggers mitochondrial membrane shedding
studi.s: The outer mitochondrial membrane mediates critical host defenses against intracellular pathogens. How microbes manipulate this compartment remains poorly understood. Here, we found that the human parasite Toxoplasma gondii remodels host mitochondrial membranes through molecular mimicry of HSP90 chaperones. Cryo-electron microscopy analyses showed that the parasite effector TgMAF1 binds the same specialized clamp domain of the mitochondrial import receptor TOM70 as chaperones of the HSP70/90 family.

studi.t: Compartment-associated filtering and environmental gradients shape fungal communities in arid Artemisia species
studi.s: Plant-associated fungal communities are shaped by interactions among host, environmental conditions, and compartment-specific filtering processes, yet the relative importance of these drivers remains poorly understood in arid and semi-arid ecosystems. We investigated fungal communities associated with three Artemisia species (Artemisia herba-alba Asso., Artemisia mesatlantica Maire and Artemisia negrei L.), including Moroccan endemics, across bulk soil, rhizosphere, root, and shoot compartments using ITS amplicon sequencing, culture-dependent isolation, and ecological analyses.

studi.t: CCDC81 is a conserved microtubule-binding protein that maintains centriole integrity
studi.s: Centrioles are microtubule-based organelles that exhibit a highly conserved architecture that is essential for their function. However, the molecular mechanisms maintaining their structural integrity remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterize CCDC81 as a conserved microtubule-binding protein that contributes to centriole organization. Using expansion microscopy, we localize CCDC81 to the A-C linker of Chlamydomonas basal bodies, where it associates with POC11, the homolog of human A-C linker protein CCDC77.

studi.t: pH Gradient Drives Redox Reactions in the Nucleolar Caps to Modulate Nucleolar Integrity and Function
studi.s: While enzymatic catalysis is the main driver of redox processes in cells, biomolecular condensates exhibit unique electrochemical properties that can potentiate redox reactions. Nevertheless, the regulatory mechanisms governing the electrochemical equilibrium of biomolecular condensates and their influence on the emergent physicochemical functions remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that specific nucleolar stressors induce alkaline nucleolar caps, which generate an interfacial pH gradient and electrical potential that drive spontaneous redox reactions.

studi.t: Autophagy induction by cytoplasmic Acinus requires Lrrk activity
studi.s: Autophagy is a critical pathway for maintaining cellular health in ageing and disease but mechanisms matching levels of autophagy to different stress conditions remain incompletely understood. In response to proteostasis stress, autophagy is induced upon activation of Acinus, a mostly nuclear protein previously linked to alternative splicing as a subunit of the ASAP complex. Here, we show that Acinus induces autophagy independently of its function in splicing.

studi.t: Will they survive? The critical status of Asiatic cheetahs in Iran
studi.s: The Asiatic cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus venaticus), once widespread, now survives only in Iran, with its population nearing extinction. In this study, we synthesised 13 years (2012 to 2024) of monitoring data to assess demographic and spatial patterns of this critically endangered subspecies in Iran. Using extensive camera trap surveys across eight reserves, supplemented by published records of cheetah occurrences on social media, we identified 24 adult cheetahs in the Northern and Southern Landscapes.

studi.t: Cryptic viruses shape trophic networks after biological invasions
studi.s: Biological invasions restructure ecological communities by bringing previously isolated organisms into contact, but the viral flow within the trophic network and its consequences have not been established. Here, we show viral exchange following the introduction of a parasitoid wasp released for classical biological control in citrus. Within a few years, viruses spread bidirectionally between native and exotic host-parasitoid trophic chains and reached a generalist hyperparasitoid at the fourth trophic level.

studi.t: Biased evolution of pollen size after whole genome duplication
studi.s: Cell size is an important functional attribute of single-celled organisms, and whole genome duplication (WGD) has long been hypothesized to double the volume of unicells. Pollen of flowering plants is effectively a single-celled organism, comprising the "vegetative cell" of the male gametophyte, which carries the male germline (two sperm cells or their precursor) within its cytoplasm. Instantaneous doubling of evolved pollen size is likely to be excessive, which should bias evolution in young polyploids to size reduction.

studi.t: Walking alone to the north: The origin and historical expansion of a polyploid parthenogenetic lineage in a weevil
studi.s: Background Polyploid parthenogenetic organisms are distributed nonrandomly with respect to their diploid sexual relatives, and this pattern has been well documented in plants. Comparable cases are rare in animals, and the genomic origins of such lineages have been reconstructed in only a few taxa. Additional animal examples are therefore needed to distinguish general eco-evolutionary processes from taxonomic idiosyncrasies. Results We determined the sex of 2,223 individuals of the flightless weevil Catapionus nebulosus species group from 294 localities across Japan.

studi.t: pbzarr: cohort-scale storage and analysis of per-base genomic data with Zarr
studi.s: Genomic assays now produce per-base signals for cohorts comprising thousands of samples. However, existing genomic data storage formats (e.g., D4, bigWig) were designed primarily for single samples or individual datasets. Consequently, cohort-scale analyses across samples, populations, or species require opening, reading, and merging thousands of files before proceeding to downstream computational analyses. Here, we present pbzarr, a format and toolkit that stores per-base genomic data from many samples and assays as a single Zarr store.

studi.t: Unveiling value functions in social cognition with multi-agent inverse reinforcement learning
studi.s: Social behavior requires individuals to consider not only their own goals but also those of others. Latent reward functions that encode such goals can be recovered from behavior using inverse reinforcement learning in single-agent settings. However, extending this to multi-agent interactions is challenging, as joint reward functions are defined over joint state spaces that grow exponentially with the number of agents. Existing approaches address this complexity by imposing restrictive assumptions on social interactions, limiting generality and interpretability.

studi.t: VINCIT: A virus-incorporated biomaterial niche enables spatially controlled in vivo CAR T cell engineering
studi.s: In vivo generation of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells could bypass the complex manufacturing required for conventional cell therapies, but systemic gene delivery remains limited by off target exposure and inefficient access to target immune cells. Here, we develop VINCIT (Virus Incorporated Niche for Cellular ImmunoTherapy), an injectable nanofiber hydrogel composite that establishes a localized immune-engineering niche for CAR T cell generation in vivo.

studi.t: Short-Duration Fluid Shear Stress Enhances LPS-Driven Macrophage Pro-Inflammatory Response in a Magnitude-Dependent Manner
studi.s: Macrophages are mechanosensitive cells that integrate physical and biochemical cues to shape inflammatory responses. Mechanical stimuli such as stretch, strain, and matrix stiffness have been extensively studied; however, the effects of fluid shear stress (FSS) on macrophage function remain relatively poorly understood. In this study, we investigated how mild-magnitude, short-duration FSS applied alone or in combination with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS), affects bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) phenotype and function.

studi.t: Systematic mapping of protease-substrate specificity through geometric graph learning
studi.s: Protease-substrate specificity is central to cellular regulation and disease pathogenesis, and accurately modelling its structural determinants remains challenging. Substrate recognition is governed by spatial constraints and higher-order relationships that extend beyond local sequence motifs. Most computational approaches rely predominantly on motif-centric or sequence-based representations, limiting their ability to capture the geometric and relational structure underlying enzymatic specificity.

studi.t: Saturation mutagenesis and NMR of a fold switch reveal position-dependent deep learning performance
studi.s: A predictive understanding of the properties of fold-switching or metamorphic proteins can provide insights into protein dynamics and energetics, and enable the design of complex protein functions and molecular machines. Recently developed deep learning modeling tools, including AlphaFold, have led to dramatic increases in structural modeling accuracy, but their performance for prediction of fold switching or point mutant effects is unclear.

studi.t: Periendothelial enrichment of PIEZO1 and its contribution to cisplatin tolerance in small cell lung cancer
studi.s: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) contains neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine cell states that differ in their response to chemotherapy. We asked where cells expressing the mechanosensitive channel PIEZO1 reside in SCLC and how PIEZO1 affects cisplatin response. PIEZO1 expression increased in two resistant cell models and correlated inversely with neuroendocrine programmes in patient tumours. In a primary SCLC section profiled by single-cell spatial transcriptomics, 273 of 7,101 epithelial candidates expressed detectable PIEZO1.

studi.t: Detection of Melanoma Using Deep Serum Proteome Profiling and Machine Learning
studi.s: Background Early detection is the primary determinant of melanoma survival yet screening still relies on visual inspection and no serum protein biomarkers are in clinical use for early detection We sought to identify serum protein signatures of melanoma development in a longitudinal military cohort Methods Using the Department of Defense Serum Repository we analyzed 390 serum samples from 73 melanoma cases and 73 matched controls collected at up to four timepoints spanning 4 years before to 2 years after diagnosis Samples were profiled by data independent acquisition mass spectrometry with…

studi.t: L-Phenylalanine acts as a broad-spectrum plant growth biostimulator for both dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous crops
studi.s: L-phenylalanine (Phe), an aromatic amino acid known to induce plant pathogen resistance at concentrations >4 mM, also functions as a broad-spectrum plant growth biostimulator in the total absence of biotic stress. To evaluate its biostimulatory potential, drench and foliar spray applications of Phe (1-16 mM) were tested on dicotyledonous (cucumber, tomato, lettuce) and monocotyledonous (wheat) crops grown under commercial-like net-house conditions with full NPK fertigation (150 mg/ L N).

studi.t: The Cost to Scroll: Short-form Video Use and Episodic Memory
studi.s: Short-form video platforms expose users to rapid streams of novel content; these features are posited to place heavy demands on cognitive processes. In a preregistered online study, we used device-reported screen time (TikTok and total Instagram app use) to examine whether short-form video use is associated with sustained attention and episodic memory in participants aged 18-24 yrs (N = 497).

studi.t: A toolkit to identify parameter degeneracy and solution manifolds of Hodgkin-Huxley type current models
studi.s: Countless studies have fitted Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) type models of active currents to voltage clamp data using nonlinear least squares. Yet, little is known about the uniqueness of parameter solutions and the interdependence of HH-type model parameters. Here, we show that considerable insight can be gained from the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a matrix closely related to the objective function used in the fitting procedure.

studi.t: Resistome-based machine learning source attribution of a superbug
studi.s: Many bacterial human pathogens infect not only humans but also other species, and source attribution has been very useful for studying transmission among the different sources. Yet, critical pathogens such as Acinetobacter baumannii have not been studied using source attribution approaches. Here, we conducted machine source attribution using the resistome of almost 1200 A. baumannii genomes from four sources: humans, companion animals , soil, and white storks. Of note, no other study has used the resistome as input data before.

studi.t: Simulated microgravity induces aging phenotypes in human organoids
studi.s: Simulated microgravity provides a controlled perturbation for testing how loss of mechanical load affects human tissues. After 24 hours in rotating-wall vessels, neural, cardiac and tonsil organoids developed tissue-specific transcriptional responses that overlapped published spaceflight datasets, accompanied by higher transcriptomic-age estimates in neural, cardiac, and tonsil models, altered cardiac-organoid contraction dynamics and modified tonsil-organoid antiviral gene-expression signatures.

studi.t: Extracellular vesicles from alternatively activated macrophages remodel the injured hepatic niche and promote repair
studi.s: Alternatively activated macrophages (AAMs) are in clinical development for acute liver injury, but their mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. AAM therapy remodels the injured hepatic niche, promoting reparative macrophage states, suppressing inflammatory myeloid programmes and restoring hepatocyte metabolic and biosynthetic programmes. We identify extracellular vesicles released by AAMs (AAM-EVs) as essential mediators of AAM therapeutic activity.

studi.t: Polymer type and surface functionalization determine the impact of nanoplastics on neural crest cell adhesion, migration, proliferation, and apoptosis in primary cultures.
studi.s: Nanoplastics (NP) constitutes a pervasive source of environmental pollution that contaminates all ecosystems, the atmosphere and freshwater. They are absorbed by living organisms and cross biological barriers, with increasing evidence pointing to their harmful effects both at cellular levels and in whole organisms. The impacts of NPs vary not only depending on their size and concentration, but also on the cell type, the polymer composition and surface charge, requiring a comprehensive understanding of the responses of a wide range of cells to these parameters.

studi.t: Isolate relatedness is more strongly associated with host and geography compared with phenotypic variation in a broad host range pathogen
studi.s: Determining the drivers of diversity in plant pathogen populations is a critical for developing effective management strategies. Sclerotinia sclerotiorum, a cosmopolitan fungus infecting over 400 plant species, causes considerable yield and economic losses worldwide. However, longstanding questions remain about the association between genetic and phenotypic variation in this pathogen, leaving the drivers of its diversification unresolved. Here, we characterized the diversity of S.

studi.t: Hidden but Expanding Sampling Bias Distorts Prokaryotic Genome Collections
studi.s: Public genome collections underpin our understanding of bacterial diversity and the distribution of traits such as antibiotic resistance, and increasingly serve as training data for genomic foundation models. Their growing size promises an increasingly complete view of microbial genetic variation. However, these collections combine studies with different sampling priorities, often overrepresenting subgroups of closely related strains of particular interest.

studi.t: Dynamics of somatic L1 retrotransposition in the human brain
studi.s: The sole source of genomic diversity in the human brain caused by autonomous retrotransposition is facilitated by the long interspersed nuclear element-1 (L1). However, assessing the rate, timing and source elements of this event has been challenging due to the lack of technologies that capture of L1s at sufficient scale in single cells. Here, we introduce LUSTRE, a single-cell assay that enables mapping L1 sites without whole-genome amplification, and profile ~17,600 neurons from the dentate gyrus, cortex, cerebellum of the adult human brain.

studi.t: Bivalent, Copper-Mediated Amyloid-β Binding Disruptsthe Prion Protein's Neuroprotective Conformation
studi.s: Emerging evidence shows that the cellular prion protein (PrPC) is a major receptor for Amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) and that this aberrant interaction may influence the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the molecular basis of this interaction remains poorly understood. Both proteins strongly bind Cu2+, and we previously discovered that PrPC, A{beta}30, and Cu2+ form a ternary complex at equimolar ratios.

studi.t: Ancestral sequence reconstruction enables functional expression of archaeal thermostable tungsten-containing aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductases in E. coli
studi.s: Tungsten-containing enzymes offer important opportunities in industrial biocatalysis, e.g. to convert carboxylic acids into aldehydes without requiring co-substrates ATP and NADPH. These W-enzymes operate at low reduction potentials compared to the more ubiquitous Mo-enzymes, enabling unique reactions. Their application is limited by the lack of functional expression in commonly used heterologous host organisms. Here, we show that variants of Pyrococcus furiosus aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PfAOR) obtained using ancestral sequence reconstruction can be functionally expressed in E.

studi.t: Dynamic nanocomplexes of antibiotics and biofilm-degrading enzymes overcome biofilm tolerance to treat Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections
studi.s: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms limit antibiotic penetration and protect embedded bacteria, making established infections difficult to treat. To combat the biofilm, administering tobramycin (Tob) with deoxyribonuclease I (DNase) could pair antimicrobial action with biofilm matrix degradation, but their distinct physicochemical properties hinder co-delivery and transport into the biofilm core. Taking advantage of the acidic biofilm microenvironment, we developed pH-responsive nanocomplexes (NCs) that expand, favoring local retention of the NCs and their cargo.

studi.t: Compound-specific DNA adduct profiling with nanopore sequencing and IonStats
studi.s: Covalently bound DNA adducts are mutation precursors that contribute to aging and diseases such as cancer. Accurate detection of adducts in the genome will shed light on tumorigenesis. However, commonly used detection methods are unable to pinpoint the exact genomic locations of adducts. Long-read nanopore sequencing has the potential to accurately detect multiple types of DNA adducts at single-nucleotide precision. In this study, we developed a novel statistical toolkit, IonStats, to profile DNA adducts in nanopore sequencing data.

studi.t: CATEomics: model selection and ensembling for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation from high-dimensional omics data
studi.s: CATEomics addresses the lack of a standardized and reproducible process for choosing among conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimators in high-dimensional omics studies, where their estimation errors cannot be evaluated directly from observed outcomes. The R package accepts a SummarizedExperiment, applies common preprocessing and data partitions across R and Python estimators, compares their out-of-fold estimates using proxy losses, supports model selection and ensembling, and returns the resulting CATE estimates to the original object for downstream omics analysis.

studi.t: Neural processing of linguistic speech features and their modulation by selective attention in users of hearing aids and cochlear implants
studi.s: Understanding speech relies on the neural processing of acoustic and linguistic features, which can both be analyzed using Temporal Response Functions (TRFs). While both types of features have been the focus of numerous studies in typical-hearing individuals, much less is known about the neural processing of continuous speech for people with hearing loss, particularly how hearing-impaired listeners process word-level features in noisy environments, where they typically struggle.

studi.t: Depletion of LKB1 in cerebellar granule cells affects parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synaptic organization and causes progressive locomotion deficits
studi.s: integrates sensory and motor information and transmits signals to the muscles via motor neurons. The sole cerebellar output neurons, Purkinje cells (PCs), receive two main inputs from climbing fibers (CFs) and parallel fibers (PFs), which are the axons of granule cells (GCs). The serine/threonine kinase liver kinase B1 (LKB1) regulates GC migration; however, its role in PF synapses remains unclear. We generated a novel strain of mice with a LKB1 conditional knockout (cKO) in GCs during the postnatal period to investigate the presynaptic function of LKB1.

studi.t: A plasma proteomic atlas of rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorders reveals convergent molecular signatures, neurodegenerative overlap, and a cross-disorder severity index
studi.s: Rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorders are individually too small for well-powered biomarker studies, and each is typically studied alone. We present a harmonized plasma proteomic resource that treats them together: over 10,000 proteins measured across 27 rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorders and unaffected family members, 26 of them with enough participants for differential abundance analysis, paired with standardized adaptive behaviour phenotypes and released with the full analysis pipeline.

studi.t: Functional specialization of TAF4b governs early prophase I entry and recombination frequency in Brassica rapa
studi.s: While the core transcription factor TAF4b regulates meiotic transcription and recombination in the diploid model Arabidopsis thaliana, its functional specialization and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood in paleopolyploid genomes. Here, we investigated how a unique, single-copy TAF4b gene on chromosome A7 modulates early meiotic progression and reproductive success in the paleopolyploid crop Brassica rapa.

studi.t: CAS-X: A Probabilistic Multi-Tissue eQTL Framework for Prioritizing Candidate Effector Genes at Type 2 Diabetes Risk Loci
studi.s: The genetic etiology of Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) involves regulatory mechanisms operating across multiple metabolic tissues. However, candidate effector gene prioritization can be limited by approaches that focus predominantly on pancreatic transcriptomics. To address this limitation, we developed CAS-X, a computational multi-tissue functional genomics framework for prioritizing candidate effector genes at T2D susceptibility loci.

studi.t: Electrophysiological correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of pain
studi.s: Positive and negative expectations can substantially shape pain and analgesic treatment outcomes, highlighting the need to elucidate neural mechanisms underlying placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia. The primary aim of this feasibility study was to assess adaptations to an established placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm in the context of electroencephalography (EEG). The secondary aim was to assess EEG correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of experimental heat pain in healthy volunteers.

studi.t: Implication of the amyloid precursor protein expressed in GABAergic interneurons for CA3 neuronal dynamics
studi.s: The amyloid precursor protein (APP), a key player in Alzheimers' disease (AD, is ubiquitously expressed in a large majority of neurons, including GABAergic interneurons (INTs) in the hippocampus. INT dysfunction and subsequent abnormalities in neural circuits have emerged as potential mechanisms of cognitive decline in AD. How APP expressed in selective classes of hippocampal INTs controls local neuronal activity and thereby influences brain rhythms remains unclear.

studi.t: Probe-assisted Structural Topography Reveals In-tissue Lesion Heterogeneity in Alzheimer's Disease
studi.s: Disease lesions are typically defined by morphology, yet this classification often masks underlying structural heterogeneity. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) plaques appear as featureless deposits under conventional microscopy, obscuring distinct sub-regions with divergent packing, maturation, and pathological potential.

studi.t: Switch from inflammatory signaling to excessive extracellular matrix remodeling in fibrotic fibroblasts attenuates monocyte tissue infiltration
studi.s: Tissue damage induces infiltration of monocytes that differentiate into macrophages and cooperate with fibroblasts in tissue repair. If repair fails and tissue stress persists, a feedforward loop involving high contractility of activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, and TGF-{beta}1 signaling can lead to chronic fibrosis characterized by hypertrophic scarring.

studi.t: Charting the Expansive Outer Membrane β-Barrel Landscape in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
studi.s: Outer-membrane beta-barrel (OMBB) proteins are central to Gram-negative bacterial physiology, mediating nutrient acquisition and secretion while shaping host interactions and antimicrobial permeability. Yet tools to catalog the diversity and functional potential of the OMBB proteome in these bacteria remain incompletely defined. Here, we combine proteome-scale structure prediction analysis and experimental validation to systematically map the OMBB proteome of the opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

studi.t: Reconstitution in JCVI-syn3B suggests the roles of the Spiroplasma Fibril protein (Sfibril) in swimming
studi.s: Spiroplasma, wall-less helical bacteria of the class Mollicutes, swim without flagella by shifting the handedness of their helical body. This motility is driven by an internal ribbon composed of actin-superfamily MreB proteins (SMreB) and the Spiroplasma-specific Fibril protein (Sfibril), which accounts for nearly half of the ribbon mass. However, because helical shape and swimming have been reconstituted with SMreBs alone, the role of Sfibril has remained unclear.

studi.t: LuxS Inactivation Increases Antibiotic Susceptibility and Impairs Genetic Competence in Streptococcus pneumoniae
studi.s: The LuxS enzyme participates in bacterial metabolism and produces the precursor of autoinducer-2 (AI-2), a signaling molecule implicated in bacterial stress responses and genetic competence. Although LuxS/AI-2 has been associated with antibiotic responses in other streptococci, its contribution to antibiotic susceptibility in Streptococcus pneumoniae remains poorly understood.

studi.t: Domain-informed effector gene assignment exposes training-data dependence of drug target prioritisation from GWAS
studi.s: About 90% of trait-associated lead variants lie outside protein-coding regions, so nominating the effector gene at genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci remains the principal bottleneck in translating associations into biological insight. Since no experimentally resolved ground truth exists at scale, every method rests on quasi-true-positive sets dominated by a single line of evidence.

studi.t: Single-dose neonatal gene therapy preserves motor coordination and extends survival of Polg-deficient mice
studi.s: POLG mutations are the most common single nuclear gene cause of mitochondrial disease. POLG disease spans a spectrum of clinical presentations with variable age of onset and severity. Early-onset disease is often severe and fatal (e.g., Alpers syndrome, myocerebrohepatopathy), while late-onset disease can be relatively mild (e.g., progressive external ophthalmoplegia). POLG disease is incurable, with few symptomatic treatments available, none of which can prevent its progression.

studi.t: Physics-Informed Modeling of Biological Aging through DNA Methylation Entropy
studi.s: Epigenetic clocks based on DNA methylation patterns are among the most accurate molecular correlates of chronological age, yet widely used clocks are predominantly empirical models with limited explicit characterization of the underlying methylation variability, lacking a direct connection to the physical mechanisms of aging. In this work, we bridge this gap by introducing an information-theoretic framework for DNA methylation dynamics combined with nonlinear machine learning to develop a competitive and interpretable age predictor.

studi.t: QuadSeq: A duplicated-duplex DNA-synthesis technology for high-fidelity nanopore sequencing of linear DNA amplicons
studi.s: Long-read nanopore sequencing is a highly versatile technology that is currently constrained by high error-rates, which can impair accurate genotyping of complex DNA samples. Common mitigation strategies based on creating consensus sequences from tandem duplications synthesized by rolling-circle or multiple-displacement amplification are prone to create both chimeric DNA molecules and require an initial DNA-circularization.

studi.t: No detectable DNA methylation in the kelps (Laminariales): a conversion-free test of a predicted loss
studi.s: Kelps (Laminariales) dominate temperate and polar rocky coasts and support a fast-growing aquaculture sector. Breeding and restoration programs need to know whether a line's performance follows its genotype or its culture history. DNA methylation has been reported in kelps, with differences by life stage, thermal history and population of origin now underpinning a literature on conditioning and priming in seaweed breeding. Recent comparative genomics work predicts otherwise, because brown algae lack the canonical DNA methyltransferases and should therefore carry little or no DNA methylation.

studi.t: Robust Cluster Typing, a computationally accessible tool for species designation from whole genome data, exemplified with the genus Campylobacter
studi.s: Bacterial genomic analysis is a cornerstone of modern epidemiology. Many genomic typing methods exist, and most are designed to work within a given species in a hierarchical fashion. However, designation of bacterial species can be problematic, making the higher resolution level of hierarchical typing difficult. Using the universally present ribosomal proteins, we have developed a pipeline for a robust typing system which can be used to assign an unknown organism to a species-level cluster or, sometimes, a sub-species cluster.

studi.t: Accurate and interpretable protein complex stoichiometry prediction through agentic AI with StoiAgent
studi.s: Accurate protein complex structure modeling requires knowledge of complex stoichiometry, yet the copy numbers of individual subunits are often unknown. Consequently, predicting protein complex stoichiometry has emerged as a major challenge in recent years. Here, we present StoiAgent, a large language model (LLM)-powered AI agent that automates the retrieval and integration of sequence, structural, and literature evidence to predict stoichiometry while preserving interpretable reasoning traces (chain of thoughts) of its evidence assessment and ranking decision.

studi.t: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
studi.s: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility.

studi.t: scUNVEIL: Learning scRNA-seq Cell Embeddings Through Measurement Enrichment
studi.s: Large-scale pretraining can improve scRNA-seq representations through measurement enrichment: estimating what the same measurement would reveal at greater UMI depth under the same measurement process. We introduce scUNVEIL, a self-supervised model trained through next-UMI prediction. We show that the Bayes-optimal next-UMI predictor is the posterior mean of the transcriptome composition that arbitrarily deep sequencing would reveal.

studi.t: BI-SCUDO Regression - A novel algorithm to infer clinical variables from omics datasets
studi.s: Regression analysis of high-throughput omics data is often made difficult by noise, batch effects, and the loss of information resulting from the discretization of continuous variables. Existing machine learning algorithms often struggle to extract stable biological signals under these heterogeneous conditions. We introduce BI-SCUDO Regression, a rank-based regression framework designed for omics data analysis. By leveraging within-sample rankings and network-based predictions, BI-SCUDO Regression bypasses the need for complex normalization and provides robust, interpretable results.

studi.t: Elflow: Automated Quality Control and Self-Supervised Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Cytometry
studi.s: High-dimensional flow and mass cytometry are foundational technologies for clinical immunophenotyping and hematological diagnostics, yet computational data analysis remains bottlenecked by operator-subjective manual gating. While computational tools have emerged, they remain fragmented across isolated tasks such as quality control or discrete clustering, leaving an unmet need for integrated, modular workflows that resolve continuous biological variation without manual supervision.

studi.t: Vocabulary recurrence, rather than biological grounding, explains tokenization transfer in protein function prediction.
studi.s: Sequence-based protein function prediction requires a choice of tokenization. K-mers, the common default, correspond to no biological unit; enzymatic digestion offers a principled alternative, since tryptic peptides are the fragments proteases generate and mass spectrometry measures. We asked whether this grounding improves transfer to unseen proteins. Using six Gene Ontology terms and 23,723 UniProt proteins, we compared tryptic peptides, peptide topics (groups of related peptides), 3-mers, and amino- acid composition, with ESM-2 embeddings and homology transfer as reference points.

studi.t: Beyond Linear Paths: Generalized Interpolation for Flow-Based Generative Modeling
studi.s: Flow-based generative models learn to transform random noise into molecular conformations by following a prescribed interpolation path between the two. Straight-line (linear) interpolation is the usual choice, but it is only one of many possible paths. We compare four paths within a single affine framework, xt = tx+ {beta}tz : linear, trigonometric, spherical and a new operator-based path in which each degree of freedom follows its own schedule. Linear interpolation is a limiting case of both the operator-based and spherical paths.

studi.t: Genomes to Fields 2026: Genomic resources for investigating genotype-phenotype relationships in Zea mays
studi.s: Maize (Zea mays L.) is a major global crop characterized by high genetic and phenotypic diversity across accessions. To better understand this diversity, the Genomes-to-Fields initiative has produced paired genotypic and phenotypic datasets annually since 2014. Here, we present 15 genome assemblies representing 13 maize lines, including founders and testers from the 2022-2023, 2024-2025, and 2026-2027 Genomes-to-Fields evaluation cycles and additional breeding germplasm, together with gene and repeat annotations. Assemblies ranged from 2.19 to 2.38 Gb, with BUSCO completeness of 97.9-99.0%.

studi.t: Optoretinographic measurements of cone photoreceptor function in disease-affected retinas
studi.s: Optoretinography (ORG) provides a noninvasive approach for measuring stimulus-evoked photoreceptor responses in the living human retina, but its application to retinal disease using clinically translatable imaging systems remains limited. Here, we applied velocity-based ORG using a clinical-grade swept-source optical coherence tomography (OCT) system to assess photoreceptor function in disease-affected human retinas and healthy controls.

studi.t: Torsion in motion: the visual system as a three-axis gimbal
studi.s: Eye movements are usually characterized by where we look and represented using the two rotational degrees of freedom that direct the line of sight onto a target. The third, torsion about the line of sight, is often regarded as a limited response and has rarely been measured outside the laboratory. Yet the conditions producing the largest torsional responses, looking at a target straight ahead, are the ones that dominate natural walking. Here we tested whether torsion is present during this pervasive behavior and measured its impact on the visual input.

studi.t: Beyond morphometry: Adolescent brain microarchitecture reflects sex differences in pubertal timing and hormones
studi.s: Puberty is a sensitive neurodevelopmental period characterized by dramatic increases in adrenal and gonadal hormones, yet how these changes relate to human brain microarchitecture remains unclear. Here, we used restriction spectrum imaging (RSI) to link peripubertal hormone levels to individual differences in brain microarchitecture (i.e., cellular and neurite density) in 7,457 youth (ages 9 to 13 years) from the ABCD Study.

studi.t: Multistage gradient-based whole-cortex modeling for joint inference of regional circuit heterogeneity and interregional structural connectivity
studi.s: Current non-invasive neuroimaging methods cannot directly resolve regional circuit heterogeneity and interregional structural connectivity, limiting mechanistic understanding of brain structure-function relationships and accurate whole-brain modeling. Here we introduce StaGIC (Staged Gradient-based Inference of Circuitry), a method that jointly infers regional circuit heterogeneity and model-constrained structural connectivity (SC) from resting-state functional connectivity (FC) and functional connectivity dynamics (FCD).

studi.t: Stage-Dependent Requirement for SETX in Human Motor Neuron Maturation and Survival
studi.s: Senataxin (SETX) is an RNA/DNA helicase involved in transcription, RNA processing, R-loop resolution, and genome maintenance. Mutations in SETX cause neurological disorders, but its role in human motor neuron (MN) development remains unclear. Here, we examined SETX function using isogenic SETX knockout (KO) human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), shRNA-mediated knockdown, and direct conversion of fibroblasts into MNs. SETX expression increased during differentiation from hiPSCs to neural progenitor cells (NPCs) and MNs.

studi.t: Biological Embedding of Social Experience Over Genomic and Neural Time Scales
studi.s: The "Neurons for Today, Genes for Tomorrow model" (NTGT) predicts how the brain's neural and molecular control systems interact to regulate biological embedding, whereby social experience alters the brain to shape future behavior. We report here on the first test of this model, using honey bee queen retinue pheromone (QRP) and behavioral, single-nucleus transcriptomic, and electrophysiological analyses.

studi.t: Modeling CNS inflammatory demyelination using myelin-directed CAR T cells
studi.s: Multiple sclerosis therapies remain confined to immunomodulatory agents that reduce inflammatory activity; none restores lost myelin, and disability can continue to accumulate independently of relapses. Development of remyelinating therapies has been hindered by models that incompletely reproduce the persistently inflamed lesions in which remyelination fails. Here we show that chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells targeting myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) build such lesions on demand.

studi.t: Two co-occurring dynamics explain the organization of a natural movement repertoire
studi.s: Natural movements vary across multiple kinematic features, making it difficult to identify the dynamics shared across movements that generate a behavioral repertoire. Here, we provide a low-dimensional, interpretable generative account of the larval zebrafish hunting repertoire that links tail dynamics to behavioral outcomes.

studi.t: Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridging Network for Motor Execution to Motor Imagery EEG Transfer in Brain-Computer Interfaces
studi.s: Motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) hold promising application prospects in the fields of limb motor rehabilitation and human-computer interaction. However, the reliability of MI calibration data is limited by the difficulty of verifying participants' engagement during motor imagerywhereas motor execution (ME) provides a more readily supervised source of motor-related information.To investigate the potential of ME-derived knowledge for assisting MI decoding, we propose a Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridge Network (SE-RTBNet) to achieve accurate intra-subject cross-task…

studi.t: TDP2 couples PKA-CREB signalling to genome stability in human cerebellar development
studi.s: Transcription and neuronal activity in the central nervous system generate abundant DNA damage, particularly DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), rendering neural cells - and cerebellar neurons especially - vulnerable to genome instability. Tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase 2 (TDP2, also known as TTRAP) resolves topoisomerase-2-linked DSBs, and biallelic TDP2 mutations cause spinocerebellar ataxia autosomal recessive 23 (SCAR23), yet how DNA repair shapes human cerebellar development is unknown.

studi.t: Measuring the information budget of cross-target antibody affinity generalization: a robust cross-target wall, and why structure reaches developability but not affinity
studi.s: Structure-based machine learning is widely expected to advance antibody engineering, yet it is unclear how far affinity predictions transfer to new targets, and why. We introduce a noise-corrected, censoring-aware estimator of the cross-target transfer ceiling, {rho}max = {surd}(T/(T+I)), which separates a transferable antibody-intrinsic component (T) from a non-transferable target-specific interaction (I). On deterministic synthetic ground truth the estimator recovers the noise-free ceiling to {+/-} 0.0003, whereas the naive sum-of-squares estimator is biased downward by measurement noise.

studi.t: A metacommunity of complex microbial communities shows high spatial synchrony, ecological memory, gradual succession and invasion resistance
studi.s: Complex microbial communities are increasingly applied in biotechnological and health-related environments, yet maintaining their diversity and relative community composition over extended periods remains challenging. While dispersal can counteract the divergence of spatially separated communities, it remains unclear whether controlled mass transfer can sustain compositional synchrony in highly diverse communities over extended periods, whether this synchrony persist after dispersal is interrupted, and how robust such communities are to invasion.

studi.t: Effect of neuB deletion on biofilm formation and extracellular electron transfer in Geobacter sulfurreducens
studi.s: The extracellular matrix of Geobacter sulfurreducens biofilms is primarily composed of proteins and exopolysaccharides. The extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) matrix provides the structural scaffold necessary to facilitate extracellular electron transfer (EET); however, the specific role of its carbohydrate components remains unexplored. Sialic acids are a class of carbohydrate derivates that can modulate extracellular matrix stability in bacteria. N-acetylneuraminic acid (Neu5Ac), the most common sialic acid, is primarily synthesized by NeuB.

studi.t: SARS-CoV-2 saltational events are recurrent and trace to persistent human infections
studi.s: SARS-CoV-2 evolution is characterized by gradual mutation accumulation but has been punctuated by rare yet impactful highly mutated variants. Whether such saltational jumps are a broad feature of SARS-CoV-2 evolution or rare anomalies remains unclear. We systematically investigate SARS-CoV-2 saltational evolution by developing a scalable framework to detect saltational events from 4.4 million high-quality viral genomes. Saltational events occurred at low but detectable rates during the pandemic and post-pandemic periods and across geographies.

studi.t: De novo Genome Assembly and Annotation of the Seep Tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma using Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
studi.s: The tubeworm Lamelllibrachia satsuma inhabits seep region by forming a mutualistic symbiotic relationship with chemosynthetic bacteria residing in its trophosome. Genomic and symbiotic studies have been extensively conducted, primarily from a bacterial perspective. But rarely vice versa. Here we present a high-quality draft genome assembly of L. satsuma and its tissue-specific transcriptome data. This genome will be valuable for further understanding the mechanisms of adaptation in cold seep environments, host-microbe interactions, as well as genome variation among tubeworms.

studi.t: FULL-seq reveals isoform-specific regulatory architecture in single cells
studi.s: Gene regulation is commonly modeled at the gene level, yet genes express multiple isoforms from distinct transcription start sites whose regulatory architecture is not resolved by current approaches. Here we introduce FULL-seq, a scalable single-cell multiomic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcript coverage from the same cell, enabling direct coupling of regulatory elements to alternative first exon (AFE) usage.

studi.t: Fine-tuned DNA sequence language models for predicting gene expression in admixed population: A comparison with variant-based methods
studi.s: Predicting gene expression from whole genome sequencing data is essential for elucidating regulatory mechanisms and interpreting functional consequences of non-coding variants to complex diseases. While traditional approaches rely on variant-based linear models, DNA sequence-based language models have gained increasing popularity for their ability to learn regulatory features directly from whole genome sequence data.

studi.t: DRAFT: graph-recurrent learning of dynamic gene regulatory networks along single-cell multi-omics trajectories
studi.s: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness.

studi.t: Sc-HistoMorphomics: A General Framework for High-throughput, Multimodal Profiling of Nuclear Morphology in Tissues.
studi.s: Quantitative cellular morphology provides a rich but underutilized window into cell identity and state. We introduce sc-HistoMorphomics, a scalable framework for profiling nuclear morphology in whole-slide H&E images and correlating these measurements with spatial transcriptomics data. Our pipeline combines deep-learning based segmentation with 194 interpretable morphometric features capturing nuclear shape, eosin and hematoxylin texture, and neighbourhood architecture, enabling high-throughput, multimodal characterization of tissue organization.

studi.t: Differential routing of spectral light inputs redistributes circadian phase sensitivity
studi.s: Shared sensory channels create a routing problem when biological functions require different combinations of the same environmental inputs. In phototrophic systems, spectral light signals can influence both circadian entrainment and irradiance-dependent physiology. We formulate a two-channel framework that separates common changes in channel activity from differential changes in their relative balance and asks how a locked oscillator represents these directions.

studi.t: Innate development of cognitive functions and motor programs by chemoaffinity
studi.s: Humans and animals possess a rich repertoire of innate cognitive and behavioral abilities, yet the developmental mechanisms that establish the underlying neural circuitry remain unclear. Here, we show that a simple chemoaffinity-based connectivity rule, combined with stochastic cell-autonomous expression of cell adhesion molecules, can establish neural networks for a broad range of cognitive functions.

studi.t: Robustness of cortical distortion metrics to unmodelled OPM errors
studi.s: The estimate of cortical current flow from magnetic fields measured outside the head is an ill-posed problem. Recent work using head casts to minimise co-registration errors in conventional cryogenic magnetoencephalography (MEG) has shown that ground truth anatomy can be used to judge between different inversion schemes and metrics. Inversion algorithms or metrics that are insensitive to anatomical distortion are unlikely to reflect correct assumptions about the underlying current distribution.

studi.t: False-negative assessment of NanoNewron's NewroBus blood-brain barrier delivery platform in the JAX apical-domain-humanized TfR1 mouse
studi.s: Humanized transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) mice are frequently used to evaluate blood-brain barrier (BBB) delivery, yet available strains differ in the extent and design of receptor humanization. We compared two NanoNewron NewroBus-based anti-TNF constructs, NN-841 (D3 TfR1-binding module) and NN-843 (A2 module), in JAX #038212 (humanized apical domain), Cyagen C001584 (human extracellular-domain CDS model), Cyagen C001860 (human extracellular-domain genomic replacement model), and wild-type controls. Thirty mice received intravenous injections and were evaluated 24 h later.

studi.t: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
studi.s: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges.

studi.t: Heterogeneous short-term plasticity reformats latent temporal information into an explicit population clock
studi.s: Short-term plasticity (STP) supports diverse synaptic-level computations, but how its organization across a circuit shapes emergent, network-level dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we first characterize STP across sparse inputs to Kenyon cells in the Drosophila mushroom body, revealing an unstructured and near-random organization that could not be explained by either pre- or postsynaptic cell identity.

studi.t: Intracellular spirochete integrates into a chemosynthetic micro-consortium of a deep-sea vent mussel
studi.s: Animal-microbe interactions comprise a diverse functional landscape, spanning pathogenic to mutualistic outcomes across extracellular and intracellular niches. Within this context, spirochetes are predominantly documented as extracellular associates or transient pathogens, leaving stable, functional endosymbiosis within animal cells unverified. Here, we report the discovery of an intracellular consortium comprising a spirochete and a primary sulfur-oxidizing bacterium within gill bacteriocytes of the deep-sea hydrothermal vent mussel Gigantidas horikoshii.

studi.t: How good a predictor the in vitro antibiogram is, of in vivo antibiotic efficacy? An in vitro - in vivo integrated approach
studi.s: Conventional antimicrobial susceptibility testing, particularly the disc diffusion assay (DDA), provides a convenient means of assessing bacterial susceptibility to antibiotics. However, its ability to predict antibiotic efficacy in an infected host remains uncertain. This study investigated the relationship between DDA-derived inhibition zones and host-protective antibiotic activity using Caenorhabditis elegans infection models involving three bacterial pathogens: methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Clostridioides difficile.

studi.t: Rapidly and reproducibly building a comprehensive catalogue of resistance-associated variants for M. tuberculosis surveillance
studi.s: Background: Catalogues of genetic variants associated with resistance underpin whole-genome sequencing (WGS)-based predictions of drug susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, and are essential for molecular diagnostics and surveillance. The current gold standard catalogues are those released by the WHO but the underlying data are not fully released and they are difficult to interpret. Open and reproducible methods would help address these problems, extending the important work already done.

studi.t: Altered age-dependent somatic mutational trajectories in ALS motor cortex neurons
studi.s: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease in which disease onset is influenced by genetic, age-associated and environmental factors. Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life and may provide a molecular link between aging and neuronal vulnerability. Here, we investigated neuronal somatic mutational patterns in ALS and control motor cortex using three previously generated 10X single-nucleus RNA and ATAC sequencing datasets.

studi.t: Regulatory grammar design of tissue-specific enhancers across species
studi.s: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles.

studi.t: A de novo reference genome of the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis
studi.s: Furcellaria lumbricalis is a red seaweed that occurs across a broad salinity gradient, ranging from the saline waters of the NE Atlantic to the brackish Baltic Sea. In the Baltic Sea, natural populations of F. lumbricalis are harvested commercially, primarily for furcellaran extraction, a sulphated polysaccharide used as a stabilizing, thickening, and gelling agent. Genomic resources for this species remain absent, constraining evolutionary, ecological, and applied research.

studi.t: Structural basis of end processing in the nucleosome by polynucleotide kinase-phosphatase
studi.s: Genomic DNA is packaged into chromatin through a fundamental repeating unit known as the nucleosome core particle. Chromatinized DNA is under constant assault from endogenous and exogenous sources of damage, which must be effectively repaired to preserve genome stability. Single-strand breaks (SSBs) with chemically heterogeneous DNA ends are one of the most prevalent forms of genomic DNA damage. These SSBs must be enzymatically processed prior to downstream gap-filling DNA synthesis and/or nick ligation during single-strand break repair (SSBR).

studi.t: Biomaterial preservation of mesenchymal stem/stromal cell fitness improves haematopoietic support in a post-leukaemic bone marrow niche model
studi.s: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are promising regenerative partners to haematopoietic stem cell (HSC) transplantation used for treatment of blood cancers. However, prolonged ex vivo expansion induces senescence and phenotypic drift that may compromise therapeutic efficacy. Here, we engineered a poly(ethyl acrylate)-laminin interface to preserve MSC fitness during expansion and investigated whether this biomaterial-controlled state influences function in a bioengineered post-leukaemic bone marrow niche model.

studi.t: BiomedCAT: Biomedical Context Analysis Tool for Supporting Mechanistic Hypothesis Generation via User-defined Contextual Subgraph Extraction
studi.s: Researchers formulate mechanistic hypotheses in slides and figures long before they write them as text, yet knowledge-graph (KG) tools expect a query in the vocabulary of the graph. We present BiomedCAT, an open-source workflow that turns biomedical slides into a subgraph of the RTX-KG2c knowledge graph shaped by the user's research profile, on a laptop and without sending the documents out.

studi.t: Systematic evaluation using SigMatch reveals how sample tissues shape transcriptomic disease relationships
studi.s: Motivation Diseases often share underlying molecular characteristics captured by transcriptional responses. Leveraging this knowledge transfer can aid in uncovering novel disease biology and drug repurposing. Large-scale transcriptomic datasets and disease signatures provide an opportunity to computationally identify these shared disease relationships based on shared genome-wide gene expression changes. However, disease signatures are strongly influenced by sample tissue, making it difficult to distinguish shared disease biology from shared tissue origin.

studi.t: XAMPGen: An Interpretable Super Intelligence Pipeline For Novel Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery
studi.s: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are short peptides with a broad spectrum of activity against bacterial pathogens, representing a promising avenue for combating the growing threat of antibiotic resistance. This study focuses on two main components: 1) generative super intelligence (GenSI) and 2) utilizing explainable super intelligence (XSI). We fine-tuned ProGen, a decoder-only protein language model, on known AMPs to generate novel peptide sequences with strong antimicrobial properties.

studi.t: ARGeement: sequence-based, versioned mapping of antimicrobial resistance gene databases
studi.s: Genomic studies of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rely on several independently curated reference databases, which describe the same genes under different names, in different structures and with different classifications. This makes results obtained with different databases difficult to compare. ARGeement maps the entries of AMRFinderPlus, the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and ResFinder/DisinFinder to each other by protein sequence, independently of their names.

studi.t: Most substitutions need more than one base change and an exact test tells which deposited scans measure the route
studi.s: Design methods that reach a target through an intermediate take two substitutions at one position, and no deep mutational scan built from a single parental sequence reports the second. The detour is common, since 230 of the 380 ordered pairs of amino acids are more than one base change apart. Both substitutions are nevertheless present in the public record wherever one protein has been scanned on two parental backgrounds that differ at a position. We assemble every such comparison in MaveDB, 102,421 complete two-step routes over 65 protein clusters.

studi.t: Spinal Recurrent Inhibition Shapes the Dynamics of TMS-induced Motor-Evoked Potentials
studi.s: Background: Motor-evoked potentials (MEPs) elicited by TMS reflect the integrity of the corticospinal pathway, yet the contributions of spinal and peripheral mechanisms to the shape of individual MEP waveforms remain poorly understood. Objective: To develop a biologically grounded model of the spinal and peripheral motor pathway that can be fitted to individual MEP waveforms across TMS intensities, and to test whether Renshaw cell (RC) recurrent inhibition is required to reproduce them.

studi.t: Persistent light-induced reduction of neuronal excitability in cortical neurons
studi.s: Visible light is widely used in neuroscience, yet its direct effects on neuronal activity in the absence of optogenetic manipulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether light stimulation can induce sustained changes in neuronal excitability. Using electrophysiological recordings in brain slices, we show that repeated pulses of blue light (5 s, 430 to 495 nm, 19 mW) produce a robust and persistent reduction in evoked firing activity in cortical neurons from both male and female mice, with an average decrease of ~60% relative to baseline.

studi.t: Overcoming subtype-specific immune resistance in small cell lung cancer through RNA-based immunotherapy
