studi.s: As financial institutions increasingly interact with blockchain ecosystems through decentralized finance, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and distributed ledger infrastructure, they come to depend on systems governed wholly or partly by decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). This paper examines how DAO governance differs from traditional corporate governance and what this implies for risk management in regulated financial institutions.

studi.t: "I Just Don't Want to Be a Burden": Investigating AI Chatbot Emotional Support Among People with Suicidal Ideation and Other Mental Health Concerns
studi.s: People experiencing high-acuity mental health concerns are turning to AI chatbots for emotional support, but little is known about what drives this use, their experiences, and their preferences. In a sequential mixed-methods study, we inductively analyzed Reddit posts and used the findings to develop a survey. We surveyed 202 adults with recent mental health concerns who had used AI for emotional support. Most participants were already receiving clinical care and reported turning to AI, most commonly because they did not want to burden others, rather than being driven by barriers to care.

studi.t: AI Companions for Young Adult Caregivers: Practical Advice, Emotional Depth, and the Limits of Metric Evaluation
studi.s: Young adult caregivers (YACs) are individuals aged 18 to 25 currently taking care of a family member, partner, or friend facing chronic illness. AI companions designed specifically for YACs remain underexplored in prior works. We present Carebot, it uses an open-weight LLM (Gemma 3-27B) as its base model, on which we compared fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a combination of both. The fine-tuning was performed based on an existing dataset of conversations with YACs and a psychologist.

studi.t: A Unified Choice Model of News Selection: Experimental Evidence on Stance, Rank, and Engagement Cues
studi.s: Social media platforms often display visual engagement cues alongside ranked news articles, yet their influence on clicks remains poorly understood when considered jointly with ranking position and users' political preferences. We propose a unified discrete choice framework using a conditional multinomial logit model to jointly estimate and compare the influence of these factors on news selection. We evaluate the model using 1,480 choices from 370 human participants across four news topics in a controlled study with and without visual engagement cues.

studi.t: Exploring Students' Insights on Creating Videos to Learn Software Design and Engineering
studi.s: This research-to-practice study examines the use of student-created instructional videos as an active learning strategy in a large undergraduate Software Design and Engineering (SWE) course. Supporting engagement and understanding in large-scale computer science (CS) courses remains a challenge, as instruction often relies on automated activities and summative assessments that prioritize grading over meaningful learning. This can make the learning experience feel impersonal, leading to frustration, anxiety, and confusion, especially when students face complex topics or new programming tools.

studi.t: WIP: Exploring Student-Created AI Agents and Instructional Videos to Foster Engagement in Computing Education
studi.s: This work-in-progress (WIP) research-to-practice study examines the use of student-created artifacts to promote active learning in a large undergraduate Software Design and Engineering (SWE) course. Active learning strategies have been shown to significantly enhance student engagement, comprehension, and motivation, particularly in computing education. In this work, we explore the use of student-created artifacts to foster student engagement in higher-level Computer Science (CS) courses.

studi.t: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
studi.s: Web research agents gather information online and write cited reports, including financial analysis. Users can state a priority to guide this research, but a priority may not say how to judge the options, leaving the agent to choose the criteria. We examine how two such agents, built on OpenAI and Anthropic models, interpret a stated priority. In 36 runs, the agents compared Microsoft and Alphabet as businesses. Prompts asked for special attention to growth or resilience, or gave no priority. We analyzed reports, searches, returned sources and cited sources.

studi.t: Longitudinal Multi-Dimensional Analysis of India-Pakistan Conflict Discourse on Reddit (2019-2025)
studi.s: Six India--Pakistan crises between 2019 and 2025, from the Pulwama attack to Operation Sindoor, have each been argued out on Reddit in India-aligned communities such as \texttt{r/india}, in Pakistan-aligned communities such as \texttt{r/pakistan}, and in general-audience ones such as \texttt{r/worldnews}. A strike can be a security issue in one community and a question of who was harmed in another.

studi.t: Milk yield responses to heat stress in tropical dairy cattle
studi.s: Context: Rising temperatures and warm tropical nights threaten dairy productivity and resilience across tropical landscapes. Objective: This study characterises multi-scale interactions among thermal regimes, nighttime cooling, metabolic heat load, and crossbred genetics on daily milk yield in Brazilian dairy systems. Methods: A 24-year panel (2001--2024) of 788,528 test-day records from 87,809 Girolando (Holstein $\times$ Gyr) cows across 408 municipalities was linked to weather data.

studi.t: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
studi.s: The emergence of large language models (LLMs) in late 2022 has raised questions about the future of science, but assessing their impact requires understanding how scientific practices were already evolving. We analyze 2.5 million full-text papers across five disciplines from 2015 to 2025, tracing trends over a broad spectrum of lexical, structural, epistemological, and social dimensions. Aside from frequency shifts in some words, most pre-2023 trends continued with limited detectable breaks.

studi.t: JALE: A new Python toolbox for coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation
studi.s: Coordinate-based neuroimaging meta-analysis using activation likelihood estimation (ALE) is commonly used to synthesize reported results of functional or structural magnetic resonance imaging studies. We here present JALE, a new, open-source Python package for conducting ALE meta-analyses. Besides computing standard ALE main effects and contrast analyses, this toolbox implements several novel analytical approaches including new options for thresholding (threshold-free cluster enhancement statistics, significance threshold prediction) as well as sensitivity and cluster analyses that were only…

studi.t: Action-outcome coupling: a pre-investment feasibility audit for offline reinforcement learning in supply chain operations
studi.s: Prescriptive analytics initiatives in logistics, such as offline reinforcement learning and next-best-action systems, are often funded before anyone verifies that the available historical logs can support an improved decision policy. We formalise this pre-investment feasibility question via action-outcome coupling: a total-effect variance index measuring how much expected outcomes change with the logged action.

studi.t: The Whole Warps the Parts: Attentional Certainty Modulates Ensemble-Induced Bias in Visualizations
studi.s: Data visualizations often require viewers to extract both ensemble statistics and individual values from collections of graphical marks. Yet individual items embedded within an ensemble can be systematically biased by that context. Prior studies have reported both repulsion away from and attraction toward ensemble statistics, but these effects have been observed across different conditions. We test whether task or attentional certainty explains these opposing forms of ensemble-induced bias.

studi.t: Copula-Based Synthetic Data Generation: A Use-Inspired Perspective on Trade-offs
studi.s: The generation of synthetic data offers a promising way to address challenges related to data scarcity and privacy concerns. While many approaches have been developed, tabular synthetic data generation methods often require complex models and extensive training data, while lacking interpretability. In this work, we investigate versatile probabilistic approaches using copulas, and leverage in particular the Gaussian Mixture Copula Model, to model the joint distribution of multivariate data, with a main focus on moderate-dimensional data sets.

studi.t: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
studi.s: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames…

studi.t: Does the AI Reviewer Alleviate or Aggravate the Maintenance Burden? Evidence from GitHub Copilot Reviewer
studi.s: This study examines how AI-based code reviewers reshape contribution behavior and maintenance dynamics in open-source software (OSS) communities. AI reviewers provide scalable, fast, and standardized evaluations. They reshape contributions as well as maintainers' workload. Leveraging the introduction of GitHub Copilot Reviewer on GitHub as a natural experiment in 2025, we investigate how AI review affects maintainers' workload and review efficiency as well as contribution behavior.

studi.t: AI as Anchor: How Interview Sequencing Relates to the Appropriation of Synthetic Stakeholder Voices in Design Education
studi.s: Designers increasingly use large language models to simulate stakeholder conversations. Yet it remains unclear how AI-Simulated Stakeholders (AIS) are taken up when used alongside human stakeholder engagement. We report a field study in a single-institution, single-semester design course in which 8 teams (N=21) constructed, evaluated, and peer-reviewed an initial AIS. Then, the teams interviewed both AIS and human stakeholders in two sequences: AIS-first or human-first.

studi.t: TRAIL-IRL: Crossed Reward-Temperature Mixtures for Unlabeled Trajectory Clustering
studi.s: Different paths need not imply different preferences, trajectories also differ in how randomly actions are chosen. Many multi-reward inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) methods assume common action randomness and can confound it with preference heterogeneity. We introduce TRAIL-IRL, which clusters unlabeled trajectories using rewards for preferences and temperatures for action randomness. Its crossed mixture pairs each reward with a shared set of temperature levels, allowing action regularity to vary within preference groups.

studi.t: Worldviews in Large Language Models
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) are often described in terms of personas and this framing has become central to alignment research. In this paper, we argue that there is a deeper level of description that lies in the agent's worldviews, i.e., its beliefs about what reality is and how it works. Treating LLMs as a population of subjects, we administer two worldview surveys from human psychology to eight models. We show that the models share many key worldview positions. For example, LLMs consistently describe the world as less good, safe, enticing, and alive than humans do.

studi.t: Plasma biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease reveal conserved features of age-related neurodegeneration in chimpanzees and humans
studi.s: Aging is a major risk factor for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD). Yet, the physiological relationships linking age-related changes in peripheral biomarkers and measures of brain structure have only recently begun to be explored. Nonhuman primates, whose brains naturally express some of the pathologic hallmarks of AD/ADRD, including amyloid-beta (A{beta}) plaques, vascular amyloid, and neurofibrillary tangles, represent a critical translational bridge between rodent models and humans.

studi.t: Nuclear phylogenomics illuminates deep lineage divergence and complex evolutionary histories in Dipsacales
studi.s: Relationships among the five subfamilies of Linnina within Dipsacales remain contentious. Extensive nuclear gene-tree discordance and cytonuclear discordance involving Linnaeoideae complicate reconstruction of their early evolutionary history. We analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 88 Dipsacales species representing all nine subfamilies and eight outgroups. Using Dipsacales-specific nuclear reference locus sets, we recovered 3,023 orthologous nuclear loci.

studi.t: Revisiting homoploid hybrid speciation in Australian cotton (Gossypium) species
studi.s: One of the earliest described cases of putative homoploid hybrid speciation was 35 years ago for the Australian cotton species, Gossypium bickii. This inference was based on discordance between chloroplast- and nuclear-based phylogenetic reconstructions, a type of incongruence that has become a relatively common observation in plants. Here we reevaluate evidence bearing on the evolutionary history of G.

studi.t: RAMA: a global genome size database of invasive tetrapod species
studi.s: Motivation: Rising numbers of biological invasions have triggered widespread erosion of environmental and socio-economic stability worldwide. To predict and understand the impacts of current and future invasive non-native species (INNS), invasion science has increased collective efforts to elucidate the role of functional traits as drivers of INNS establishments and impacts.

studi.t: Genotype and environment shape gene regulatory variation in switchgrass
studi.s: Local adaptation is contingent on genotype-by-environment interactions, which are often mediated by variation in gene expression. The causes and consequences of variation in gene expression are complex, and they are rarely evaluated under the multi-dimensional environmental regimes that occur in the field. Here, we investigate switchgrass gene expression variation in contrasting sites in Michigan and Texas.

studi.t: Game structure shapes normative preferences and inter-brain neural synchrony in free-allocation public goods games
studi.s: Threshold public goods games (TPGGs) are generally expected to facilitate coordination more effectively than linear public goods games (LPGGs), because an explicit provision point can support non-zero equilibria and transform a social dilemma into a coordination problem. This prediction, however, is based largely on settings in which group members contribute to a single shared pool. Whether it extends to environments in which individuals freely allocate resources across multiple partners remains unknown.

studi.t: A field-potential signature of pre-burst dynamics in human higher-order thalamic neurons
studi.s: The aperiodic (1/f) component of the local field potential (LFP), long dismissed as noise, is increasingly being recognized as physiologically meaningful. Its exponent has been proposed to index excitation:inhibition (E:I) balance, with higher exponents (steeper spectra) corresponding to greater inhibition. Yet this hypothesis remains debated and has seldom been tested against single-neuron activity. Here, we used rare concurrent single-neuron and LFP recordings from the human pulvinar during goal-directed behavior and quiet wakefulness.

studi.t: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Age-Specific Cancer Hallmark Architecture in Pediatric and Adult Brain Tumors
studi.s: Pediatric cancers are fundamentally different from their adult counterparts. Specifically, pediatric cancers carry fewer mutations, interact with developing immune systems, and have active developmental microenvironments. The tumor microenvironment (TME), which includes the surrounding stromal cells, immune cells, blood vessels, and extracellular matrix, plays a crucial role in cancer progression, metastasis, behavior, and treatment response.

studi.t: Bidirectional acetate exchange couples ethanol turnover to acetyl-CoA metabolism in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
studi.s: Overflow metabolism describes the excretion of partially oxidized metabolites into the extracellular environment during rapid sugar utilization. Although these metabolites can later be reused, it remains unclear whether reassimilation also occurs during ongoing sugar consumption, and if so, how. Here, 13C-isotope tracing and metabolic flux analysis of acetate exchange in Saccharomyces cerevisiae during hexose utilization reveal that net acetate overflow is only the small difference between order-of-magnitude larger simultaneous excretion and assimilation fluxes.

studi.t: N- and T-genes framework for pathway deregulation: Taxonomy, progression, and protection in cancer
studi.s: Background. Pathway analysis is widely used to interpret gene expression, but conventional enrichment depends on arbitrary thresholds and does not quantify deregulation magnitude. Recent reformulations based on average log-fold changes remove the threshold but still average over all annotated genes, diluting the signal from the genes that actually drive the normal-to-tumor transition.

studi.t: Scalable biophysical constraints link steady-state and kinetic metabolic modeling
studi.s: Rational metabolic engineering relies on models that connect molecular mechanisms to cellular behavior. Constraint-based metabolic models integrate stoichiometric, thermodynamic, and omics-derived information, but they do not generally constrain whether flux magnitudes are compatible with the corresponding metabolite pool sizes. Metabolite turnover rates, the ratios of total production or consumption flux to pool size, capture this relationship and quantify how rapidly pools are renewed.

studi.t: Personalized functional networks scale with brain size beyond anatomy and are reorganized in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
studi.s: Anatomically, cortical regions scale differentially with total brain size: some show disproportionate contraction in smaller brains and expansion in larger brains, while others show relative stability. Whether personalized functional networks (PFNs) follow similar areal scaling principles, and how these principles shape functional reorganization in conditions that alter brain size, remain unknown.

studi.t: Confidence in global motion discrimination is better predicted by perceptual reliability than by stimulus-based heuristics
studi.s: Decision-making requires evaluating the reliability of perceptual estimates, but whether confidence reflects perceptual reliability or stimulus-based heuristics remains debated. We used a multiple-aperture global motion stimulus in which the global direction, and therefore motion coherence, is only available after integrating locally ambiguous signals, so that no simple stimulus statistic can serve as a shortcut. Observers reported the global direction in two successive intervals and then chose which decision was more likely to be correct.

studi.t: Neurocognitive signatures of intrinsic motivation in naturalistic information seeking and memory
studi.s: Humans often seek information without direct external reward. Theories distinguish two major dimensions of this intrinsic motivation: wanting, the desire to resolve an information gap, and liking, the enjoyment of the information itself. However, how these motivational dimensions shape self-guided information-seeking behavior, neural activity, and memory formation in realworld contexts remains underexplored.

studi.t: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
studi.s: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin suppresses M2 macrophage polarization via the JAK2-STAT6-PPARγ pathway to alleviate allergic asthma
studi.s: Background: Allergic asthma (AA) is a chronic respiratory disease closely linked to immune-inflammatory responses driven by M2 macrophage polarization. PrimO-glucosylcimifugin (POG), a natural bioactive compound from Saposhnikovia divaricata (SD), alleviates inflammation in acute lung injury mice, but whether it mitigates AA by modulating M2 macrophage polarization remains unclear. Objective: This study investigated POGs effects on AA and its mechanisms in regulating M2 macrophage polarization.

studi.t: Carbon allocation strategies across Mucoromycota and the discovery of oxalic acid secretion in Absidia
studi.s: In this work, nine strains representing eight species, seven genera, and five families from the phylum Mucoromycota were studied for their production of biomolecules (lipids, saccharides, phosphates, organic acids, ethanol, and glycerol) under cultivation in media with different carbon-to-nitrogen (low, medium, and high). Although lipid accumulation was a common feature across the species, the results revealed also differences in carbon allocation strategies between families, both in magnitude and nature of the biomolecules produced.

studi.t: Unravelling bacteriochlorophyll biosynthesis in the uncultured Roseilinea
studi.s: Filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs) of the Chloroflexota phylum are abundant members of microbial mat communities. All isolated and culturable FAPs are found in a single class within this phylum, but metagenomic studies of hot spring communities from around the world have indicated that phototrophic members of an additional class may exist, which have so far eluded cultivation for study in the laboratory.

studi.t: Efficient Method for Estimating the Frequency of Plasmidless Cell Generation per Cell Division
studi.s: Plasmids are self-replicating pieces of DNA that play a major role in the evolution and spread of adaptive genes in bacteria. Plasmids tend to form stable associations with their hosts, including plasmids such as small, multicopy plasmids that typically lack specialized partition and horizontal transfer systems. Using a ColE1 plasmid model, we present a method that quantifies the frequency of plasmid loss over a short, defined time window.

studi.t: Sugar alternatives shift the evolutionary trajectory of fluoride resistance in cariogenic and non-cariogenic dental bacteria
studi.s: Dental caries result from acidogenic biofilms dissolving enamel while growing on fermentable dietary sugars. While fluoride from toothpastes and professional products is widely used for caries control, sugar alternatives with inhibitory effects on some dental microbiota (e.g., erythritol and xylitol) instead reduce the cariogenicity of foods and act as prebiotics, often in combination with of fluoride, to control caries progression. Despite their growing prevalence, we do not understand how frequent exposure to sugar alternatives impacts the evolutionary pressures faced by oral bacteria.

studi.t: From CSP7 to CSP5: Development of a soluble, truncated congener for the treatment of obstructive and restrictive lung diseases.
studi.s: Chronic obstructive and restrictive lung diseases (CLDs), represent a substantial worldwide health burden, with curative therapies remaining largely unavailable. Studies from our group and others have identified caveolin-1 (Cav1)-mediated signaling as a critical regulator of cellular processes implicated in the pathogenesis and progression of CLDs, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), silicosis and other progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PF) conditions.

studi.t: Docking and SPR identify candidate interactions between Apolipoprotein A-I and chemokine receptors
studi.s: Background: Apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1), the main protein component of high-density lipoprotein, suppresses chemokine-driven leukocyte migration. This effect is usually attributed to indirect mechanisms such as cholesterol efflux, changes in lipid rafts, and altered receptor expression. Whether ApoA1 interacts with chemokine receptors directly is not known. Methods: We combined in silico rigid-body docking of AlphaFold-predicted structures (GRAMM-X, with interface analysis by PDBePISA) and surface plasmon resonance (SPR).

studi.t: Pathogenic role of cGAS-STING pathway in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
studi.s: The cGAS-STING pathway is a critical component of the innate immune response to infection and cell stress. Chronic activation underlies human diseases such as lupus and inflammatory bowel disease, but cGAS-STING has not been implicated in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). Compared to healthy controls, macrophages from DMD patients have high levels of cytosolic DNA and low levels of the DNA exonuclease, TREX1, a scavenger of cytosolic DNA upstream of cGAS-STING. Likewise, cytosolic DNA is elevated in macrophages from dystrophin-deficient mdx mice.

studi.t: Spatial coordination of filamentous enzymes establishes a redox-balancing metabolon
studi.s: Nutrient scarcity in tumors prompts metabolic adaptations in cancer cells. Here, we identify that glutamine deprivation, a common feature of the tumor microenvironment, induces formation of a proline biosynthesis metabolon to selectively maintain intracellular proline levels. Mechanistically, filament-forming enzymes glutaminase (GLS) and pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) co-assemble with the downstream reductases PYCR1 and PYCR2 into a physically associated enzyme complex within a spatially segregated mitochondrial subset.

studi.t: Targeted siRNA screening coupled with unbiased proteomics identify potassium signaling as a critical regulator of pigmentation
studi.s: Ion channels are emerging as critical regulators of cellular signaling, influencing diverse pathophysiological processes and offering promising opportunities for therapeutic intervention. However, the contribution of ionic homeostasis to human skin pigmentation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify potassium (K+) dynamics as a critical regulator of pigmentation and uncover K+ channel Kir7.1 as a molecular link between K+ and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) signaling.

studi.t: Mechanically coupled proliferation controls notochord geometry during axis elongation
studi.s: The notochord is a central organizing structure in vertebrate development, functioning as a signaling axis that patterns surrounding tissues while undergoing rapid elongation. Despite its importance, how notochord shape is regulated to ensure robust morphogen signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we combine high-resolution 3D imaging of mouse embryos between E8.5 to E10.5 of development with a data-driven biophysical model to investigate the mechanisms underlying notochord morphogenesis.

studi.t: Taxonomic turnover with phylogenetic conservation in subaerial biofilm (SAB) communities of marble monuments
studi.s: Subaerial biofilms (SABs) colonizing exposed stone surfaces provide natural systems for investigating microbial community assembly under challenging environmental conditions. Although bacterial diversity on stone has been widely described, whether taxonomic variation reflects broader phylogenetic and ecological differences remains unclear. Here, we characterized SAB communities inhabiting two geographically separated historic urban marble monuments, Federal Hall National Memorial (New York) and the Lincoln Memorial (Washington, DC), using SSU rRNA amplicon sequencing.

studi.t: Cross-level correlation and temporal dynamics of hierarchical habitat selection
studi.s: Habitat selection is a fundamentally hierarchical process implying that choices made by animals at broad spatial scales constrain those made at finer ones. How selection for the same habitats relates across hierarchical orders remains largely untested empirically. We investigated whether selection for a given habitat at the larger scale reinforces itself, is independent of, or opposes selection for the same habitat at the finer scale.

studi.t: Environmental and particle trait controls on microbial carbon turnover on fast-sinking particles in the Iceland Basin
studi.s: Microbial remineralisation of sinking particles governs the depth and magnitude of organic carbon sequestration in the ocean. Yet, the combined influence of environmental gradients and particle morphology in regulating remineralisation remains poorly constrained. During spring in the subpolar Icelandic Basin, we estimated microbial carbon turnover, a proxy for remineralization, on fast sinking particles collected at two depths below the mixed-layer using shipboard incubations. Alongside this we used imagery to determine the morphology and complexity of the particles.

studi.t: Visual Landmarks Influence Eye-Hand Coordination in Memory-Guided Reaches
studi.s: The human visual system optimally weighs egocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to the eye) and allocentric cues (e.g., object location relative to other landmarks) to aim actions. The neural mechanisms of this process have been studied in the primate gaze system, but it is not known how these results extend to eye-hand coordination and the reach system. Here, reach and gaze (eye-in-space) data were collected from two head-unrestrained Macaca mulatta (M1, M2) trained to reach toward remembered visual targets on a touch screen.

studi.t: Repurposing a biosynthetic enzyme for imaging UDP-glucose dynamics in living systems
studi.s: Metabolite dynamics remain difficult to visualize in living systems, particularly for nucleotide sugars that link metabolism to glycosylation and signaling. Here we repurpose Helicobacter pylori UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase to develop UGluS, a genetically encoded ratiometric fluorescent sensor for its biosynthetic product, UDP-glucose (UDP-Glc). Circularly permuted GFP insertion and directed evolution yield an approximately 18-fold excitation-ratio response and an apparent dissociation constant of 32.5 M, with preferential responsiveness to UDP-Glc over related metabolites.

studi.t: Biosynthesis of serotonergic Kanna alkaloids
studi.s: Plants have repeatedly evolved to synthesize natural products that exploit serotonin signaling in animals. Although serotonin and most of its neuroactive analogs derive from tryptophan, the medicinal Kanna plant (Mesembryanthemum tortuosum) instead uses tyrosine and phenylalanine to construct a serotonin-like scaffold through unknown chemical transformations. Here, we elucidate the biosynthesis of Kanna alkaloids, including the serotonin reuptake inhibitor mesembrine.

studi.t: SMSTPred: Protein Language Model Embeddings Predict SAM-Methyltransferase Substrate Specificity and Reveal Metabolite Methyltransferasome Enrichment in Plants and Actinomycetota
studi.s: S-adenosyl-methionine (SAM)-dependent methyltransferases (MTases) are one of the largest and most ancient enzyme superfamilies in biology, transferring a methyl group from SAM to substrates as different as DNA, RNA, proteins, and small-molecule metabolites. Most SAM-MTases share a Class I Rossmann-like SAM-binding core, with substrate specificity determined by variable inserts and accessory domains rather than the conserved fold; as a result, substrate type is unknown for most MTases in sequence databases, which are dominated by unreviewed entries.

studi.t: Tetrapeptide caspase inhibitors exhibit protease- and substrate-dependent off-target specificity
studi.s: Peptide-based caspase inhibitors are widely used to define the functions of individual caspases and were developed from tetrapeptide substrate preferences identified using positional scanning peptide libraries. Their specificity is typically validated using fluorogenic tetrapeptide substrates, yet whether these assays accurately predict inhibition of endogenous protein substrates has not been systematically examined.

studi.t: Biocatalytic Asymmetric Radical Dearomatization of Electrophilic Heterocyclic and Non-Heterocyclic Arenes
studi.s: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization provides a powerful strategy for converting readily available aromatic feedstocks into valuable three-dimensional molecular scaffolds. Despite substantial advances over the past several decades, general methods for catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of electrophilic arenes, particularly non-heterocyclic substrates with high aromatic stabilization energies, remain a challenging task. Here, we report the use of a hydrogen atom transfer mechanism for biocatalytic radical dearomatization of electron-deficient arenes.

studi.t: When fibers crowd: Mesh burden and myofibroblast phenotypes in women with vaginal mesh exposure
studi.s: Polypropylene mesh improves the durability of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) repair but can cause complications, most commonly vaginal mesh exposure. Preclinical animal studies demonstrate that mesh deformation increases local mesh burden and is associated with maladaptive remodeling and macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition (MMT). Whether a similar cellular response occurs in women remains unknown. We examined mesh vagina tissue complexes excised from N=17 women with vaginal mesh exposure following sacrocolpopexy.

studi.t: WormIE: an Integrated Explorer for multi-source Caenorhabditis elegans annotations and transcriptomic data interpretation
studi.s: Interpreting gene lists and expression data from Caenorhabditis elegans experiments usually means writing scripts, searching scattered databases or uploading unpublished data to a remote server. WormIE (Worm Integrated Explorer, https://wormie.bio) is a free, open-source tool for analyzing user-provided data and exploring C. elegans annotations in one browser tab.

studi.t: Vecmatch: Balancing Covariates in Multiple Groups Using Vector Matching Algorithm and Generalized Propensity Scores
studi.s: Covariate imbalance is a major source of bias in observational studies. This issue arises when confounding variables (e.g., age, sex) are distributed unevenly across compared groups, potentially influencing estimates of between-group differences in other dependent variables. Matching techniques based on propensity scores are widely used to address covariate imbalance and improve the accuracy of causal inferences. These methods work by calculating propensity scores based on imbalanced covariates and then matching observations with the closest propensity scores across compared groups.

studi.t: Characterization of Inter-Alpha-Trypsin Inhibitor Heavy Chain 5 (ITIH5) Expression, a Prostate Basal Cell Marker.
studi.s: The prostate epithelium contains secretory luminal epithelial cells, basal epithelial cells and neuroendocrine cells. Luminal cells are secretory cells that produce prostatic secretions and basal cells are involved in regeneration and maintenance of epithelial tissue. The absence of a basal cell layer is a defining morphological feature of prostate adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemical detection of basal cells using standard markers such as p63 and high molecular weight keratin (34{beta}E12) is routinely employed to differentiate invasive carcinoma from benign architecture mimics.

studi.t: TR-107 and Capivasertib Synergistically Inhibit Pancreatic Cancer Organoid Growth In Vitro
studi.s: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality in the United States, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) has emerged as a promising therapeutic target due to metabolic reprogramming and the pro-survival role of mitochondria in PDAC. The mitochondrial ClpXP complex, composed of the AAA+ ATPase ClpX and the peptidase ClpP, regulates mitochondrial homeostasis through protein degradation. Madera Therapeutics has developed novel ClpP activators, including TR-107.

studi.t: Quasistable multiclonal carcinomas evolve through mutations with locally extended phenotypes
studi.s: The earliest stages of epithelial carcinogenesis are often considered to arise via lineal evolution, a mutation-driven process characterised by purely competitive clonal interactions. However, this conventional view cannot fully explain the persistent polyclonality observed in many cancers. We therefore investigated an alternative mechanism of cancer progression, termed interclonal cooperation, arising from mutations that cause cells to produce microenvironmental changes, enabling them to affect the behaviours of surrounding cells.

studi.t: Targeting Telomere Integrity Enhances Radiosensitivity and Reveals Adaptive DNA Damage Response Vulnerabilities in Diffuse Midline Glioma
studi.s: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG), including diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG), remains one of the most lethal pediatric malignancies, with limited durable benefit from radiotherapy (RT) due in part to adaptive DNA damage response (DDR) mechanisms. Here, we investigated whether targeting telomere integrity with the telomerase substrate analogue 6-thio-2'-deoxyguanosine (6-thio-dG; THIO) could induce therapeutically exploitable DNA damage in patient-derived DIPG models.

studi.t: Investigation into Nicotiana systemin orthologs reveals lineage specific systemin insensitivity in LAB accession N. benthamiana
studi.s: Systemin (SlSYS1) from Solanum lycopersicum was the first plant peptide hormone to be identified, and its receptor (SYR1), processing, and role in defense are all well characterized. However, studies of systemins outside of Solanum are extremely limited. Here, we identified four new bioactive systemins within the genus Nicotiana, three from N. tabacum, NtSYS4A/B/C, and one from N. benthamiana, NbSYS4. We showed that expressing the canonical systemin receptor SlSYR1 confers the ability to detect these novel systemins. In addition, we found that LAB accession N.

studi.t: Benchmarking honorific academic recognitions against citation metrics
studi.s: We examined how diverse metrics track individuals receiving major honorific recognitions and whether higher, more prestigious recognitions are associated with higher coverage among a database of top-cited scientists. We assessed with Scopus data the newly inducted (in 2026) 2,038 members of 14 major academies and honorific societies, endowed professors at Stanford University (n=773) and Michigan State University (MSU) endowed professors (n=129) and distinguished professors (n=112), and Nobel (n=166) and Turing (n=25) laureates awarded in 2010-2026 (n=191) for total publications, total…

studi.t: Exponent Polytopes for Abstracting Chemical Reaction Networks into Formal Specification Models for Compositional Design of Biomolecular Circuits
studi.s: Model based design has shown promise for synthetic biological circuits. However, many approaches remain empirical and limited in scale. Here, we develop specification models from chemical reaction network (CRN) models. These specifications encode assumptions explicitly and guarantees that must be met under those assumptions. Specifically, we show how monomial dominance relations in open CRNs induce polyhedral regime assumptions in logarithmic coordinates. These assumptions give polyhedral assume guarantee contracts that encode system behavior.

studi.t: CDK phospho-degron tags for dynamic protein regulation
studi.s: Cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) activity underpins cell cycle progression through dynamic and temporally ordered phosphorylation events. While transcriptional regulation has been extensively exploited in synthetic biology, the rational engineering of post-translational signaling circuits remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce modular CDK-responsive phospho-degron tags derived from the Far1 regulatory region and demonstrate their ability to confer tunable, cell cycle-dependent control over protein stability in budding yeast.

studi.t: Beyond the rule of seven: translating time across humans and dogs shows diverse clocks set the pace of development and aging
studi.s: Although a dog's year is often converted to human age by multiplying it by seven, there is little scientific evidence to justify this calculation. Here, we assembled 11,365 observations to generate age alignments across multiple organ systems from humans and 11 canid species and 171 dog groups. We used a range of metrics, including behavioral milestones (e.g., age of eye opening), age-related changes in blood chemistry profiles, disease occurrence, and reproductive traits to translate ages across species and breeds.

studi.t: The Ran-binding protein Mog1 sustains Spt5 C-terminal phosphorylation by counteracting Spt4 in budding yeast
studi.s: Transcription elongation by RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) requires phosphorylation of the C-terminal repeat (CTR) of the elongation factor Spt5 by the Bur1-Bur2 kinase, yet how this modification is sustained remains unclear. Here we identify the conserved Ran cofactor Mog1 as a positive determinant of Spt5 CTR phosphorylation in budding yeast. Cells lacking Mog1 show reduced Spt5 phosphorylation and chromatin association, lower RNAPII CTD Ser2 phosphorylation and a previously unreported, guanine-reversible sensitivity to nucleotide depletion.

studi.t: An extended Cks1-interacting region in Far1 modulates Cdk1 inhibition and substrate phosphorylation
studi.s: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) use multiple docking interactions to recognise their substrates and inhibitors, but how sequences between canonical interaction motifs contribute to these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we identify an auxiliary interaction element in the budding yeast CDK inhibitor Far1 and investigate its contribution to kinase inhibition and multisite phosphorylation.

studi.t: Age-dependent phosphorylation of estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) regulates homodimer formation and impairs the repression of amyloid precursor protein (APP) promoter.
studi.s: Estrogen receptor beta (ER{beta}) is a ligand-activated nuclear steroid receptor that promotes neuroprotection through its transcriptional coordination of healthy cell gene programs. However, circulating estrogens are dramatically reduced post-menopause and the administration of hormone replacement therapy is only beneficial within a narrowly restricted timeframe after the menopause transition. The molecular underpinnings for this failure of ER{beta} to evoke protection in advanced age is unknown.

studi.t: LIFE-seq: longitudinal spatial transcriptomics of living tissue
studi.s: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has deepened our understanding of cellular spatial heterogeneity, yet existing technologies are predominantly confined to fixed or frozen specimens, limiting longitudinal molecular profiling of the same living tissue. To overcome this limitation, we developed LIFE-seq (Living-tissue in situ nanoforest extraction for spatiotemporal transcriptomic mapping), a minimally invasive approach that combines high-density nanoforest arrays for molecular sampling with directed transfer onto spatially barcoded messenger RNA (mRNA) capture chips.

studi.t: Modeling Coupled Ecohydrological and Structural Responses to Forest Thinning
studi.s: Forest thinning is a silvicultural practice widely used to reduce competition among trees and enhance forest resilience. However, its long-term coupled effects on forest water balance and canopy structure remain uncertain due to competing hydrological processes, disturbances, and climatic variability. This study developed a multiyear stochastic ecohydrological model coupling soil saturation and water fluxes with canopy structure, represented by dynamic leaf area index (LAI), to examine how thinning alters soil water storage and evapotranspiration (ET) as the canopy regrows.

studi.t: Freezing seawater samples alters the community composition and richness inferred from eDNA metabarcoding
studi.s: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has become a common approach for surveying biodiversity, yet processing aquatic samples can sometimes be challenging in the field. When eDNA water sample processing is delayed during remote field collections, whole water samples can be stored frozen to minimize further eDNA degradation. However, the freezing and thawing processes may influence eDNA integrity thus affecting species identification. We split bulk seawater samples to compare the marine taxa detected from water that had been filtered immediately to water that had been stored frozen for one month.

studi.t: Additive Channels in Curved Fitness Landscapes
studi.s: Fitness variation within a population depends both on how genetic differences affect reproduction and on how common those differences are. We examine this dependence using breeding values, which sum the average effects of an individual's alleles on traits in that population. We average reproductive output at each breeding value before taking its logarithm, then ask how much of the resulting variation a straight line can describe. For normally distributed breeding values, a quadratic approximation separates variation due to slope from variation due to curvature.

studi.t: LAMP sheds light on how sequence to function models learn variant effects during post-training
studi.s: Genomic sequence-to-function (S2F) models show promise for interpreting noncoding genetic variation, yet they currently underestimate the effects of most causal variants. This leads to fine-mapping failures that are reflected in their underperformance relative to linear baselines at predicting gene expression across individuals from personal genome sequences. Improving personal genome predictions, which reflect this underestimation, is therefore critical.

studi.t: IMPRESS: AI-coupled HPC workflows for protein design
studi.s: Protein design campaigns are often run as multi-stage pipelines with a generative backbone model, an inverse-folding model, and a structure predictor chained together in that order. The stages differ by one to two orders of magnitude in cost per candidate, and the allocation of sampling effort across them is fixed before a campaign begins. Such a filter cascade can only discard candidates.

studi.t: Long-term low-intensity vibration attenuates age-associated adipogenic bias and enhances osteogenic potential in mesenchymal stem cells
studi.s: Aging impairs mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) function and regenerative potential, contributing to a shift in MSCs differentiation away from osteogenesis and toward adipogenesis. This study investigated the effects of in vivo low-intensity vibration (LIV) on bone characteristics, exercise performance, and the functional, mechanical, and molecular phenotypes of bone marrow-derived MSCs from 24-month-old mice. LIV (90 Hz, 0.7 g) was initiated at 5 months and administered twice daily until 24 months. Outcomes were compared with age-matched, non-vibrated controls.

studi.t: Mathematical genomics of hidden signatures in NCF1: implications for chronic granulomatous disease
studi.s: Inborn errors of immunity (IEIs), such as Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD), impose a disproportionately severe clinical burden in populations with high rates of consanguinity. CGD is caused by defects in the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex, frequently due to mutations in the NCF1 gene encoding the p47phox protein. While the functional domains of NCF1 are well characterized, the quantitative architectural constraints governing its structural stability remain elusive.

studi.t: Contrasting Effects of Potassium Glutamate and Potassium Chloride on the Oligomerization Equilibrium and Kinetics of the PCNA Sliding Clamp
studi.s: While salt and osmolyte effects on protein folding have been extensively characterized, their effects on the dissociation equilibria of protein complexes are less well understood. These effects arise from preferential solute interactions with functional groups exposed during unfolding or dissociation, as described quantitatively by the solute partitioning model (SPM). The surface exposed upon unfolding has a remarkably similar functional group composition among globular proteins, leading to broadly similar effects of a given solute on the unfolding free energy.

studi.t: Optimal combined chemotherapeutic and antibiotic treatment for cancer in the presence of saboteur bacteria
studi.s: We consider a mathematical model of cancer dynamics under chemotherapeutic treatment in the presence of bacteria capable of metabolizing the chemotherapeutic agent, thereby compromising therapeutic efficacy. To counteract this effect, we investigate the introduction of antibiotic co-therapy aimed at eradicating the bacterial population or at least mitigating its negative impact on treatment outcomes. The underlying dynamics are formulated as a system of four non-linear ordinary differential equations, with the time-varying dosages of both drugs treated as control variables.

studi.t: Metabolic rewiring of sugar alcohols drives lichen symbiosis in Trebouxiophyceae microalgae
studi.s: Lichen symbioses are among the most successful mutualisms in extreme environments, yet the biochemical traits that enable algal partners to thrive within them remain poorly defined. We used untargeted GC-MS to uncover metabolic rules underlying symbiotic compatibility. Comparing 21 Trebouxiophyceae species, including free-living microalgae and lichen photobionts, we identified 260 metabolites, concluding that sugar alcohol metabolism emerged as the principal axis of differentiation, with ribitol-rich taxa consistently dominating lichen partnerships.

studi.t: Human tau compromises neuronal structural integrity in C. elegans independently of disease-associated modifications
studi.s: Tauopathies are a group of progressive neurodegenerative diseases amongst which Alzheimer's disease is the most prevalent. They typically have a late age of onset and lead to cognitive decline. Tau is a highly soluble, intrinsically disordered microtubule binding protein that aggregates in these diseases. The mechanisms by which age-associated changes alter tau functionality and compromise neuronal structural integrity remain poorly understood.

studi.t: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
studi.s: Attentional control is a core cognitive function, yet there is still a significant debate revolving around its definition, factorial structure and underlying neural mechanisms. Research in this domain has largely developed along two largely disconnected traditions. Psychometric approaches assess individual differences using latent-variable models (e.g., structural equation modeling, confirmatory factor analysis), while cognitive neuroscience focuses on group-level behavioral and neural effects.

studi.t: In vitro and in vivo validation of recombinant Syrian hamster interferon-α
studi.s: The Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) is an important model for the study of viral pathogenesis and the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines, yet species-specific reagents remain scarce. Here, we validate the potent and specific activity of recombinantly expressed Syrian hamster maIFN-12-like protein (maIFN) in vitro and in vivo. MaIFN expressed in E. coli induced MX2 and ISG15 expression in both BHK21 hamster kidney cells as well as in primary hamster fibroblasts in a dose-dependent manner and EC50 values in low pg/mL range.

studi.t: Periodic spatial patterning of gene expression via a natural quorum-synchronized oscillator
studi.s: In many biological systems, genetic oscillators that function in growing tissues can establish spatially repetitive patterns of gene expression. However, few mechanisms for generating such patterns are known in bacteria. Here, we describe an oscillator within the quorum sensing circuit of Streptomyces coelicolor. Through modeling and genetic experiments, we demonstrate that this quorum oscillator controls periodic expression of a gene involved in antibiotic biosynthesis at the periphery of expanding colonies.

studi.t: An Optimized ChIP-sequencing protocol for transcription factors in embryonic mouse brains
studi.s: Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-Seq) is widely used to identify genome-wide protein-chromatin interactions. However, obtaining reliable ChIP-seq data for transcription factors has been challenging for several reasons, including their low abundance, transient or weak DNA binding, and poor antibody performance. Here, we present an improved ChIP-Seq protocol for mapping transcription factor occupancy in embryonic mouse brains.

studi.t: Interconnections with and within the trypanosomal respiratory chain revealed by complexome profiling
studi.s: Proteins are frequently integrated into multicomponent complexes that execute the elaborate processes supporting life. Thus, a protein's function can only be defined by the company it keeps within a complex. Proteomes provide informative protein inventories but lack information about protein quaternary structures. Complexome profiling (CP) has been transformative in capturing the comprehensive population structure of complexes at a given moment within a cell. We have employed CP to chart the multiprotein complex landscape of two life cycle stages of Trypanosoma brucei.

studi.t: Evaluating the effectiveness of raised beds in alleviating heavy metal contaminants
studi.s: Structural policy and social practices, including redlining and white flight, have driven disinvestment and heightened exposure to persistent environmental pollutants resulting from residual impacts of industrial activity. Urban agriculture, meant to empower and feed communities, are frequently established on vacant lots that may contain these contaminants and pose a threat to human health. To circumvent the legacy of contaminations on bare soil, Chicago growers are using raised beds to create a barrier between contaminated soil and healthier imported compost.

studi.t: Validating regional insect pest phenology forecasts using published developmental data
studi.s: BACKGROUND: Crop losses caused by insect pests are expected to increase under global warming, highlighting the need for accurate phenology forecasts to support integrated pest management (IPM). Arthropod pests, as ectotherms, exhibit temperature-dependent development and phenology that can be described by thermal performance curves (TPCs).

studi.t: Land use intensification favours fitness similarity as plant diversity declines
studi.s: Land use intensification reduces plant diversity, but we know little about how it changes coexistence mechanisms. Niche and fitness differences, together with indirect interactions, can respond non-linearly to intensification and influence which species combinations are feasible, meaning that all members have positive equilibrium abundances. We analysed nine annual vegetation surveys (2008-2016) of 50 common plant species across 150 German grasslands, using a composite land use intensity (LUI) index summarising fertilisation, mowing and grazing.

studi.t: Emergent frequency-dependent selection predicts mutation outcomes in complex ecological communities
studi.s: Ecological interactions can dramatically alter evolutionary outcomes in complex communities. Yet, most population genetics models neglect how interactions within complex communities shape evolutionary dynamics. Here, we bridge this gap by using dynamical mean-field theory to integrate community ecology into classical population genetics models. We show that near an ecological steady state, interactions generate emergent negative frequency-dependent selection between parents and phenotypically similar mutants.

studi.t: Acoustic phenotyping reveals sublethal pesticide effects in bees using BEEhaviourLab
studi.s: Behavioural changes can provide early indicators of physiological stress, yet remain difficult to quantify at scale. Acoustic behaviours such as buzzing are widespread in insects but are rarely incorporated into automated ecotoxicological assays. We developed BEEhaviourLab, a multimodal platform combining tag-free video tracking with automated acoustic phenotyping, and validated it across four insect pollinator species (honey bee, Apis mellifera; bumble bee, Bombus terrestris; ivy bee, Colletes hederae; and hoverfly, Eristalis tenax).

studi.t: Sample preparation for mass spectrometry-based tissue (phospho)proteomics
studi.s: This protocol describes the workflow for the preparation of tissue samples for proteome and phosphoproteome analyses using mass spectrometry. The tissue samples are cryogenically pulverized and homogenized in a sucrose-based buffer to ensure proper tissue disruption. For depletion of lipid contaminants, proteins are purified using chloroform-methanol precipitation, followed by a resuspension in a urea-based buffer for enzymatic digestion. Peptides are desalted and enriched for phosphopeptides prior LC-MS/MS analysis.

studi.t: Osmotic niche changes as multifaceted trigger of cellular regenerative processes in organ injury
studi.s: Tissue compartments can maintain distinct osmotic environments that are separated by physical barriers. Whether injury-induced osmotic niche changes associated with the disruption of these barriers contribute to the onset of regeneration remains unknown. Here we present analyses of human tissue samples indicating that fracture-induced barrier disruption likely exposes the marrow niche to a sudden hypo-osmotic shift, which enhances extracellular matrix (ECM) stress relaxation.

studi.t: What a running template needs: leg damping and a hip torque
studi.s: A template, the simplest model that reproduces a behaviour, is a hypothesis about what the body must do. For running, the spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) captures the bounce of the centre of mass but not the force behind it: its ground reaction force (GRF) is symmetric in time and always points along the leg. Its many extensions have never faced a common test.

studi.t: Diffusion geometry and topology reveal Alzheimer's proteomic states
studi.s: ABSTRACT INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity. Identifying biologically distinct proteomic states may improve understanding of disease heterogeneity and support precision diagnostics. METHODS: Cerebrospinal fluid proteomic data from ADNI were analyzed. Among 6,361proteins tested between cognitively normal and AD groups, 407 remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (FDR < 0.05), with 404 retained after missingness filtering. Following preprocessing and outlier removal, 130 individuals were included.

studi.t: Characterization of heterogeneous bioinformatics training needs in the AI era
studi.s: Bioinformatics training providers serve heterogeneous audiences, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing what learners need. Training-needs surveys are typically analyzed question by question or split by demographics such as career stage. This assumes that people in the same demographic group need the same training, whereas needs may depend more on the data people work with. We present a protocol that groups survey respondents by the similarity of their topic ratings rather than by demographics.

studi.t: ModkitOpt: Accurate RNA modification site calling from nanopore sequencing
studi.s: ModkitOpt is a pipeline for the systematic optimisation of modkit filtering thresholds and stoichiometry cutoffs using orthogonally validated modification sites. It substantially improves site-calling accuracy across modification types, even when the nanopore sample and validation sites are from different biological contexts. We report optimal site-calling parameters for m6A and pseU and provide practical recommendations for applying ModkitOpt.

studi.t: Molecular simulation of ion-mediated phase separation and structural organization in RNA condensates
studi.s: Phase separation of RNA is strongly influenced by ions, yet the molecular mechanisms by which ion-RNA interactions affect RNA condensation and internal organization remain poorly understood. Here, we use coarse-grained molecular simulations to investigate how temperature, ions and RNA sequence collectively regulate condensate formation and organization. We find that RNA condensates selectively enrich Mg2+ through dynamic multidentate phosphate coordination, producing ion concentrations several orders of magnitude higher than in surrounding solution.

studi.t: Loss of metabolic resilience underlies maladaptive responses to lipid overload in TDP-43 proteinopathy
studi.s: INTRODUCTION Altered eating behaviour is a hallmark feature of behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). These changes may represent a compensatory response to an underlying metabolic disturbance. However, whether increased lipid availability restores metabolic homeostasis or instead accelerates disease progression remains unknown. TDP-43 proteinopathies, which account for approximately half of FTD cases, are associated with alterations in lipid metabolism, providing a mechanistic framework to investigate the cerebral response to lipid overload.

studi.t: Correlated but distinct: VIP and NDNF interneurons implement dissociable inhibitory motifs for state-dependent gain control in visual cortex
studi.s: VIP and NDNF positive interneurons are both found in layers 1 and 2/3 of the cortex, but have distinct patterns of gene expression, morphology, and connectivity. Despite this, their functional roles in the sensory cortices seem remarkably similar; their activity correlates with behavioral state, and they gate behaviorally driven increases in excitatory activity and sensory-driven responses.

studi.t: Drug Repurposing of Rapamycin Mitigates Amyloid-β-Associated Proteotoxicity in Caenorhabditis elegans Models of Alzheimer's Disease
studi.s: Background: Alzheimers disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, affecting an estimated 55 million people and projected to exceed 130 million by 2050. AD is defined pathologically by extracellular accumulation of amyloid-beta (A{beta}) and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles. Currently no therapy halts the underlying neurodegeneration in AD patients. Proteotoxic accumulation of A{beta} is a central pathogenic event therefore, strategies that enhance its clearance represent a compelling therapeutic avenue.

studi.t: Slow but not fast theta tACS modulation of hippocampal-cortical connectivity compresses temporal distance judgments
studi.s: The temporal organization of episodic memory is thought to depend critically on the hippocampus, potentially coordinated by theta-band oscillations. Here, we used concurrent transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to examine whether slow theta stimulation (3 Hz) applied over the left parietal cortex modulates hippocampal-cortical functional connectivity during memory encoding, and how this relates to subsequent temporal memory performance.

studi.t: Subtractive and Divisive Methods for Isolating Neural Oscillations From Broadband Activity Yield Different, Even Conflicting, Power Estimates
studi.s: Understanding the role of oscillatory brain activity in cognition is a key objective in cognitive neuroscience. However, quantifying the power of narrowband neural oscillations is made challenging by the presence of non-oscillatory broadband activity in the signal. Recently, there has been a proliferation of methods designed to separate oscillatory from non-oscillatory (aperiodic) signals. To perform this separation, these methods must model the relationship between oscillatory and aperiodic components.

studi.t: Switches in single-neuron excitability class can induce rich dynamical states in balanced networks
studi.s: Network states with rich dynamics and highly variable firing rates of individual neurons are prominent in experimental observations and thought to benefit complex information processing and learning. Such states have been proposed to arise from properties of network coupling, like a strong connectivity or slow synaptic dynamics. Here, we identify an alternative mechanism based on weak synaptic coupling and intrinsic cellular dynamics.

studi.t: Characterising semantic prioritisation in visual working memory
studi.s: Visual working memory preserves multiple features of recently encountered information, but these features are not necessarily equally available to guide upcoming behaviour. In particular, categorical semantic content can be prioritised over perceptual content when objects are retrieved from memory. Here, we asked what drives this semantic prioritisation in visual working memory, and whether it depends on the attentional state of the remembered information.

studi.t: Development of an Enclosed Microbial Co-culture Device and GCXGC-TOFMS Workflow to Investigate Volatile Organic Compound Exchange
studi.s: Microbial volatile organic compounds (mVOCs) can mediate interactions between microorganisms without direct physical contact. However, co-culture systems to examine these interactions are limited, and volatilomic data interpretation is challenging. Here, we developed enclosed microbial co-culture platforms compatible with diverse microbial systems, headspace solid-phase microextraction (HS-SPME), and comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography time-of-flight mass spectrometry (GCXGC-TOFMS) for mVOC sampling and characterization.

studi.t: Differential modulation of host cell Serine and Arginine-Rich (SR) protein and apoptotic factor BCL-2 gene expressions during Chandipura and Dengue virus infections
studi.s: Regulation of alternative splicing (AS) is important in controlling cellular functions. More than 95% human genes are alternatively spliced and AS is regulated by close to 100 splicing factors. Line of evidences suggest that virus infections alter the AS pattern of numerous host genes. In this study we have investigated Chandipura virus (CHPV) induced alteration of host cell SR protein gene expressions and determined if these changes have any effect on apoptotic factor BCL-2 levels.

studi.t: Progerin Expression in Alveolar Epithelial Cells Exacerbates Inflammatory Responses to SARS-CoV-2 Infection
studi.s: Age is a major determinant of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), yet the cell-intrinsic consequences of ageing for SARS-CoV-2 infection remain difficult to examine in human experimental systems. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived tissues provide accessible models of infection but generally lack hallmarks of ageing. Here, we employed an iPSC line containing an inducible progerin cassette and differentiated these cells towards an alveolar type II-like epithelial fate.

studi.t: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting regulates tissue-specific pioneer activity
studi.s: Pioneer transcription factors bind nucleosomal DNA and establish accessible chromatin, yet their binding is tissue specific. While studies have largely focused on protein-extrinsic features, like chromatin structure and cofactor expression, the mechanisms governing the tissue-specific binding remain poorly understood. We used the Drosophila pioneer transcription factor Zelda as a paradigm to investigate the mechanisms controlling tissue-specific binding. Zelda promotes the undifferentiated state in both the embryo and in neural stem cells of the larval brain.

studi.t: Expanding the human T cell receptor germline reference through population-scale pangenome analysis using the gAIRR Suite version 2
studi.s: The germline gene set encoding the adaptive immune receptor repertoire (gAIRR) defines the allele space from which the expressed repertoire (exprAIRR) is assembled, so an incomplete gAIRR reference propagates errors into T cell receptor (TR) annotation and genotyping and is also a barrier to studying inherited TR variation in its own right. Human TR gAIRR diversity remains incompletely characterized because the loci resist short-read resolution and because locus-resolved cohorts have been small.

studi.t: A Molecular Glue that Regulates Processing of Non-Coding RNAs in Human Cells
studi.s: Small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs) are a major class of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) and essential components of the spliceosome. Chemical tools for perturbing snRNA structure and function are lacking, and ncRNAs have more generally been considered undruggable. Here we use chemical proteomics and cryo-electron microscopy to identify a covalent molecular glue HL-1B that stabilizes binding of the 3'-exonuclease TOE1 to the spliceosome in a catalytically competent state.

studi.t: GatorAnchor: Cross-Modal Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Reliable Cell Neighborhoods in Single-Cell Multi-Omics
studi.s: Cross-modal uncertainty challenges single-cell multi-omics integration because molecular modalities differ in sparsity, technical noise, and context-dependent biological informativeness, producing discordant cell-cell relationships. Treating conflicting evidence as equally reliable can propagate uncertain relationships and obscure biologically meaningful cellular heterogeneity.

studi.t: Machine Learning Prediction of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Performance, Interpretability, and Cross-Database Redundancy
studi.s: Antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) classifiers are typically developed and evaluated within a single curated database, leaving open how much two independently curated databases agree and what that implies for apparent cross-database generalization. We trained an XGBoost classifier on amino acid trigram frequencies and physicochemical descriptors using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD), the field's largest curated ARG resource.

studi.t: Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG) for Antiviral and Antibacterial Drug Discovery.
studi.s: Infectious diseases remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, while therapeutic discovery is hindered by fragmented biomedical data and antimicrobial resistance. To address this challenge, we developed the Infectious Disease Knowledge Graph (IDKG), a queryable platform that integrates curated chemical, biological, pharmacological, and clinical information relevant to infectious-disease drug discovery.

studi.t: Super-resolved mass photometry reveals the dissociation pathways of individual protein complexes
studi.s: Mass photometry (MP) measures the mass of single unlabelled molecules as they adsorb to a glass surface, but conventional analysis captures each molecule only momentarily, as it binds, and neglects its subsequent fate. Here we correct for coverslip drift and use mass-dependent localisation precision to link successive events at one site to a single molecule and enables two workflows for studying protein assemblies.

studi.t: Striking Differences in Tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) Deconjugation by Human Fecal Microbiota: The Pilot-10 Human Donor Study
studi.s: Tetrabromobisphenol A (TBBPA) is a widely used brominated flame retardant with multiple adverse health effects. Although TBBPA undergoes phase II conjugation to facilitate elimination, gut microbial deconjugation may regenerate unconjugated TBBPA, increasing intestinal re-exposure. However, the extent of interindividual variability and its underlying microbial determinants remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Distinct calcium, sodium, and water programs characterize mouse and human connecting tubule
studi.s: The kidney connecting tubule lies between the distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct. Even though short, it plays a key role in regulating calcium, sodium, and potassium excretion and water balance in health and disease. In rodents and humans, transitions between distal segments are gradual, making the assignment of functional properties to cell types difficult. To address this, we enriched mouse kidney distal tubule cells prior to performing single nucleus RNA-sequencing.

studi.t: Attenuated, Not Absent. Trusting Autonomous Systems Tracks Reliability More Closely, With Less Neural Engagement, Than Trusting Humans
studi.s: Users of autonomous systems and AI assistants decide whether to accept a system's output, yet whether such active trust decisions engage the same evaluative architecture as trust between people remains unknown. Forty-four participants made trial-by-trial decisions to trust or distrust a human or autonomous system partner during fMRI, with identical prescripted accuracy for both partners across five difficulty levels. Despite equivalent performance, trust in humans exceeded their reliability.

studi.t: A multiscale map of the descending sympathetic innervation of the spleen
studi.s: Brain regulation of visceral organ function depends on descending neural circuits. The spleen is the largest secondary lymphoid organ, and studies indicate that descending neural activity can alter splenic immune responses. Here, we combined retrograde tracing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spinal cord and brain reconstruction, and glycoprotein-complemented rabies tracing to map the sympathetic circuits associated with these organs in mice.

studi.t: A neuronal atlas of neurexin isoform expression in Caenorhabditis elegans
studi.s: The Caenorhabditis elegans neurexin gene nrx-1 encodes both long () and short ({gamma}) isoforms, but how their expression varies across individual neurons remains unclear. Using NeuroPAL and endogenous transcriptional reporters, we generated a nervous system-wide atlas of nrx-1 expression in L4 hermaphrodites. We assessed reporters for one and two {gamma} transcript groups in 267 identified neurons. The two {gamma} reporters collectively marked a broader set of neurons than the reporter, and most neurons expressing the reporter also expressed at least one {gamma} reporter.

studi.t: Near-threshold somatosensory perception revisited: Pre- and post-stimulus neural processes during electrical and naturalistic mechanical stimulation
studi.s: Near-threshold somatosensory stimulation is traditionally applied to investigate the post-stimulus neural correlates of conscious perception as well as ongoing brain activity like alpha oscillations that precede stimulation and modulate perception. Recent findings showed that applying more natural mechanical stimulation instead of the frequently used electric stimulation reveals differences in early post-stimulus perceptual correlates.

studi.t: In silico designed small molecule targets misfolded TDP-43 to rescue function and ALS pathology
studi.s: The DNA/RNA binding protein TARDBP or TDP-43 is a key driver of pathology in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), a motor neuron disease with no known cure. In >97% of sporadic ALS patients, nuclear TDP-43 in motor neurons mislocalizes and aggregates in the cellular cytoplasm (gain-of-function). A parallel reduction in nuclear TDP-43 in ALS patients leads to a loss-of-function in mRNA binding and splicing regulation. Using our machine learning platform, we discovered ACE-339, a novel, orally bioavailable small molecule that disrupts insoluble TDP-43 aggregates.

studi.t: Dance experience shapes local brain dynamics and shared responses during naturalistic action observation
studi.s: Skilled action observation unfolds over time: viewers follow changing movements, coordinate what they see with prior experience, and form a response to the performance as a whole. Dance expertise is known to alter action-related activation and the similarity of spectators' responses, but its association with local BOLD dynamics during an extended performance remains unclear. We reanalyzed fMRI from 14 professional dancers and 11 novices watching the same 33-minute dance film; one choreographer provided a separate reference.

studi.t: From Adalimumab to orally administered secretory IgA: preclinical characterization of ABC-301
studi.s: Reformatting therapeutic immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies into secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) may provide an alternative architecture for mucosal drug delivery. We characterized ABC-301, a recombinant human sIgA1 incorporating the antigen-binding regions of Adalimumab, and evaluated its human tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF) neutralization, oral activity in experimental colitis, tissue biodistribution, and susceptibility to patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibodies. ABC-301 retained human TNF binding and functional neutralization in vitro.

studi.t: Treponema pallidum eight-stranded beta-barrels: an evolving, versatile family of outer membrane proteins in the service of stealth pathogenicity.
studi.s: Syphilis is a multistage sexually transmitted infection caused by the highly invasive and immunoevasive spirochete Treponema pallidum (TPA). TPA depends on the import of many host-derived nutrients to sustain its auxotrophic lifestyle. Moreover, its invasive nature requires interactions with diverse host molecules to successfully disseminate and persist. The outer membrane proteins (OMPs) mediating these processes remain largely uncharacterized. In other bacteria, 8-stranded {beta}-barrels (8S{beta}Bs) perform such functions, including nutrient uptake and host interactions.

studi.t: Capsular surveillance-guided phage cocktails against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae
studi.s: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is among the most urgent antimicrobial-resistance threats, yet its extraordinary capsular diversity has kept phage therapy locked in per-isolate matching-a process too slow and labor-intensive for routine use. Here we convert this specificity problem into a look-up problem.

studi.t: Intestinal epithelial differentiation factor HNF4α restrains homeostatic interferon signaling and is required for its full induction during Salmonella infection
studi.s: Intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) must interpret microbial signals to transcriptionally adapt their identity and function. Which transcription factors (TFs) mediate those adaptations, and whether competing transcriptional pathways signal within the same or in different IEC subpopulations, remains unclear. We find that microbiota colonization shifts nearly all IECs toward an interferon-driven inflammatory program at the expense of genes involved in enterocyte differentiation and metabolism.

studi.t: Nuclear blebs are rupture-prone restricted compartments of the nucleus
studi.s: Nuclear blebs are abnormal herniations of the cell nucleus that cause nuclear rupture and dysfunction. The biophysical principles underlying nuclear blebs and ruptures remain to be fully elucidated. Using nuclear localization signal green fluorescent protein (NLS-GFP) we tracked nuclear bleb rupture dynamics. Upon nuclear rupture, the nuclear bleb NLS-GFP loss rate is significantly faster than the nuclear body, whereas non-blebbed nuclei ruptures show no difference in NLS-GFP loss rates between the site of nuclear rupture and body.

studi.t: Adaptive signal evolution and gene flow drive variable speciation outcomes in bark anoles
studi.s: New species evolve in a complex and non-linear fashion, resulting in situations where genomic and phenotypic variation between diverging lineages become decoupled.
