studi.t: Learning gene co-regulation across cells with Multicellular Transformer
studi.s: Understanding how genes coordinate across cells is central to explaining tissue function and disease, yet most existing models still take a single cell as input and therefore emphasize cell-intrinsic regulation. We present the Multicellular Transformer (MCT), a foundation model built around a different assumption: cells function together within tissues, so the appropriate unit of input is not one cell in isolation but a set of cells from the same sample.

studi.t: Paired multiomic profiling defines the healthy human synovium infrapatellar fat pad stromal continuum
studi.s: The synovium and infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP) are anatomically contiguous tissues implicated in osteoarthritis, yet their cellular and molecular organization in the healthy human knee remains poorly defined. We combined bulk RNA sequencing with paired single-nucleus transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling to establish a quantitative multiomic reference of healthy human synovium and IPFP.

studi.t: Expanded ME-model analysis capabilities enable genetic recoding, proteostasis, RNA decay, and cofactor essentiality in bacterial models
studi.s: Genome-scale metabolic models (M-models) are widely used to understand and manipulate microbial metabolism in silico, and are characterized by an extensive availability of automated reconstruction, analysis tools, and simulation software. The scope and accuracy of M-models was greatly improved by the development of metabolic and gene expression models (ME-models) aimed to infer the optimal allocation of individual macromolecules such as proteins, RNA, and enzymatic complexes which constrain metabolic fluxes to their availability and abundance.

studi.t: Genomic tessellations
studi.s: Periodicity is ubiquitous in genomic data. Assembled sequences are dense with homopolymers, microsatellites, and large satellite arrays, which contribute to phenotype, variation, and disease. Third-generation sequencing technologies, such as Oxford Nanopore (ONT) and PacBio HiFi, has enabled longer and increasingly accurate reads, but have brought with them systematic error biases in repetitive regions, where insertions and deletions can distort array lengths and mimic or obscure biological variation.

studi.t: Ion selectivity as a biophysical determinant of action-potential dynamics
studi.s: Ion selectivity is a fundamental property of voltage-gated ion channels, yet its contribution to action-potential dynamics has received less attention than channel conductance and gating kinetics. Here, we investigate how Na+/K+ permeability ratios influence membrane excitability, extending a multiscale framework that connects molecular properties of ion channels to neuronal electrical activity.

studi.t: N-terminal mutations R5L and R5H share a common mechanism in disrupting tau condensates on microtubule surfaces
studi.s: Tau, an intrinsically disordered protein abundant in neuronal axons, forms cooperative condensates on microtubule (MT) surfaces that regulate motor proteins and protect MTs from severing enzymes. Disease-associated mutations at residue 5 in the N-terminal projection domain of tau, far from the MT-tau binding interface, have been linked to progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) (R5L) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) (R5H). While R5L was previously shown to disrupt tau condensate formation on MT surfaces, it remained unclear whether R5H shares this phenotype.

studi.t: Neuroprotective Effects of the Purine-Derived Compound ITH15004 Against Nigericin- and Mitochondria-Induced Toxicity in NSC-34 Motor Neuron-like Cells
studi.s: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the progressive degeneration of motor neurons. Most patients die within 3 to 5 years of diagnosis, primarily due to respiratory failure, and effective therapeutic options remain limited. Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, calcium dysregulation, and neuroinflammation are key contributors to ALS pathogenesis.

studi.t: Long-Acting GLP-1 Receptor Agonism Ameliorates Sinoatrial Node Dysfunction by Attenuating Electrophysiological and Structural Remodeling
studi.s: Background: Sinoatrial node dysfunction (SND) causes bradyarrhythmia, while pacemaker therapy does not reverse injury to the sinoatrial node (SAN). Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) raise heart rate, but whether they can repair an injured SAN in SND remains unknown. Methods: In streptozotocin-induced SND rats, we studied an acute phase (SND, GLP-1RA treatment, glycemic control, and GLP-1R antagonist groups) and a chronic phase (SND, GLP-1RA treatment, and glycemic control groups).

studi.t: Quantitative analysis of HDAC inhibition using the TGx-HDACi transcriptomic biomarker in human TK6 cells
studi.s: Transcriptomic biomarkers provide an objective approach for extracting mechanistic information from complex gene expression datasets and may support quantitative applications in chemical assessment. TGx-HDACi is an 81-gene transcriptomic biomarker designed to identify histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) in human TK6 cells. We evaluated whether benchmark concentrations (BMCs) derived from TGx-HDACi responses are concordant with BMCs based on reductions in HDAC enzyme activity.

studi.t: Harnessing Circadian Resilience for Demand-Flexible Controlled Environment Agriculture
studi.s: The increasing penetration of renewable electricity generation creates opportunities for flexible demand-side energy management in Total Controlled Environment Agriculture (TCEA), where artificial lighting represents a major operational cost. However, the biological consequences of demand-responsive lighting strategies remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether photoperiods can be dynamically adjusted to minimise economic costs or maximise renewable energy utilisation while maintaining crop productivity.

studi.t: Visual Illusion: A Matter Of Disorder Between Retinal And Perceived images
studi.s: Visual illusions reveal that perception is constructive rather than a faithful copy of the retinal image. This paper proposes that the brain supplements ambiguous or incomplete sensory input with virtual edges, filled-in surfaces, brightness and size cues, and illusory contours. Using gray-level Shannon entropy, we compared original and perceived images across five illusion classes: edge detection, surface filling-in, brightness perception, size perception, and the Hermann grid. In all cases, perceived-image entropy exceeded real-image entropy.

studi.t: Tracking single neurons across days reveals acute and persistent effects of psilocybin in the mouse brain
studi.s: The psychedelic psilocybin offers a novel approach to treat depression and other psychiatric disorders. A single dose of psilocybin induces rapid neuroplastic effects that persist for many weeks to months. However, psilocybin's effect on neural firing beyond its systemic presence, and the neural mechanisms linking these acute and sustained effects remain unknown. Using chronically implanted Neuropixels probes, we tracked 1,692 neurons spanning prefrontal and hippocampal regions following saline and psilocybin injections and 24 h later.

studi.t: Motor cortex facilitates visual action override through the superior colliculus
studi.s: Unexpected visual events can leave goal pursuit undisturbed or trigger visual action override - an interruption that redirects behaviour towards the stimulus. Using a visual distraction task in freely moving mice, population calcium recordings and causal perturbations identified the lateral motor-related superior colliculus (lSCm) as a key node controlling distractor engagement. Retinal inputs to the sensory-related SC signalled distractors even when mice ignored them.

studi.t: Inter-protocol reproducibility of multi-shell diffusion MRI metrics across major neuroimaging study protocols
studi.s: Diffusion MRI is a core component of large-scale neuroimaging initiatives, yet the reproducibility of quantitative dMRI metrics across different acquisition protocols remains unclear. We acquired seven multi-shell diffusion protocols representative of major consortia and clinical settings on a single scanner in 41 healthy adults, isolating protocol effects from hardware and site variability.

studi.t: State-dependent gating of sensory and cortical inputs by median raphe neurons
studi.s: The mesopontine median raphe (MnR) plays an important role in regulating brain states, hippocampal network activity, and memory processes. Recent studies have revealed that the MnR comprises three major neuronal populations: serotonergic (5-HT), glutamatergic (Vglut3-expressing), and GABAergic neurons. How these distinct neuronal populations may gate sensory and cortical inputs across different brain states remains largely unknown.

studi.t: A four-dimensional single-cell and spatial atlas of cAMP-driven repair after rat spinal cord injury
studi.s: Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) induction through photoactivatable adenylate cyclase (bPAC) in corticospinal neurons enhances locomotion after spinal cord injury (SCI); however, the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie this improvement are unknown. Here we perform single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) of spinal cord sections at the injury site of dorsal hemisected rats, to identify the pathways through which bPAC stimulation exerts its regenerative cues after SCI, along with the changes in cellular populations that occur in different parts…

studi.t: An isogenic human stem cell model reveals NGLY1-dependent control of microglial development
studi.s: NGLY1 is a cytosolic N-glycanase involved in glycoprotein quality control and proteasome-mediated protein degradation and is critical for normal brain development and function. Although neuronal alterations caused by NGLY1 deficiency have been extensively characterized in animal and human cell models, how NGLY1 deficiency affects human glial cells, particularly microglia, the brain-resident innate immune cells, remains largely unknown.

studi.t: Age-dependent changes in the putamen transcriptome and proteome of a transgenic minipig model of Huntington's disease
studi.s: Huntington's disease is an inherited neurodegenerative disorder with no disease-modifying treatment available. Preclinical trials of gene therapies rely on large animal models and the transgenic Huntington's disease (TgHD) minipig is one of them. Minipigs live more than a decade, so the effect of a single dose of gene therapy can be followed for years. The TgHD transgene carries a mixed CAG/CAA repeat that is not expected to expand somatically.

studi.t: Waveform morphology links local circuit kinetics to cortical interactions
studi.s: How does local cortical physiology shape interactions between brain regions? We combined neural mass modelling with human and macaque intracranial recordings to examine how synaptic kinetics link oscillatory waveform morphology to cortical interactions. In a modified excitatory-inhibitory Wilson-Cowan model, synaptic rise and decay kinetics shaped waveform geometry and phase-dependent responsiveness.

studi.t: Macaque Vγ4+ γδ T cells exhibit distinct IFN-γ and IL-22 effector profiles that are dysregulated during chronic SIV infection and diarrheal disease
studi.s: V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to colonic homeostasis in humans, but their biology in nonhuman primates remains poorly defined. Here, we characterized V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells in blood and intestinal tissues of healthy, diarrhea-inflicted, and SIV-infected rhesus macaques. TRG/TRD repertoire sequencing across colon, mesenteric lymph node, blood, and spleen revealed compartment-specific clonal architecture and colonic enrichment of TRGV3.

studi.t: O-antigen promotes age-dependent pathogen competition with the gut microbiota and complement evasion during natural systemic dissemination
studi.s: Bacterial pathogens employ multiple virulence factors to outcompete the gut microbiota and immune system during host colonization. Among these, O-antigen (O-ag) is a common cell-surface virulence factor in gram-negative bacteria extensively studied in vitro and in models of systemic infection. Yet, its role during bacterial enteric infection is less understood. Particularly, O-ag contributions to pathogen competition with the gut microbiota and natural establishment of diarrhea-associated bacteremia remain unclear.

studi.t: Identifying the metacommunity scale reconciles deterministic and stochastic assembly in a natural mainland-island microbial system
studi.s: Disentangling the deterministic and stochastic processes that shape microbial communities remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. The framework proposed by Vellend---selection, drift, dispersal and speciation---offers a natural conceptual scaffold, but testing these processes in natural communities is technically demanding, and analyses are often narrowed to a single process, which can lead to seemingly contradictory conclusions.

studi.t: Parasite-induced ER-PVM contacts promote CERT-dependent ceramide delivery to the apicomplexan vacuole
studi.s: Apicomplexan parasites rely on host lipids for replication, yet how host transport machinery is coupled to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) remains unresolved. Here, we uncover a host-parasite membrane contact site mechanism driving ceramide delivery to the vacuole. Host ceramide transfer protein (CERT) targets the PVM via its PH domain, cooperating with host VAP-B to promote sphingolipid accumulation and support Toxoplasma and Plasmodium development.

studi.t: Detection, Persistence, and Antimicrobial Resistance Profiles of Escherichia coli and Shiga Toxin-Producing E. coli in Nut Orchards with Integrated Grazing Animals
studi.s: Integrating grazing animals into nut orchards can introduce foodborne pathogens including Salmonella enterica and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) into crop production environments. This study investigated pathogen transfer and persistence in the soil following livestock grazing (sheep/chicken) in two organic almond orchards and one walnut orchard in California. Soil and fecal samples were collected periodically for 120 days after grazing. Enrichment, selective culture and PCR were used for STEC and Salmonella enterica detection.

studi.t: An epiphytic tissue sampling method using a cellulose acetate membrane filter facilitates phylogenomic analysis of Plasmopara viticola
studi.s: Understanding genetic backgrounds and potential migration routes of emerging pathogens is important for preventing further invasions and outbreaks. RNA-seq data from field-collected infected plant tissues are increasingly used for pathogen monitoring, particularly for pathogens that cannot be cultured on artificial media. Despite its advantages, low pathogen read proportions in such field RNA-seq data can lead to unreliable genotyping results, hindering accurate surveillance and diagnosis.

studi.t: Direct Sputum Sequencing Reveals Mycobacterium tuberculosis Diversity Underrepresented by Culture in a High TB-Burden Setting
studi.s: Background: Whole-genome sequencing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) commonly relies on culture-derived isolates, potentially altering the bacterial populations represented. Direct sputum whole-genome sequencing (dsWGS) may better capture lineage composition and within-host variant diversity. Methods: We compared targeted-enrichment dsWGS with WGS of matched culture-derived isolates from participants initiating treatment for rifampicin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis in Worcester, South Africa.

studi.t: HOG pathway modulation is a determinant of echinocandin treatment failure in Candidozyma auris
studi.s: Candidozyma auris is a rapidly emerging fungal pathogen whose drug-resistant profile poses a formidable challenge to antifungal treatment. Echinocandins are the recommended first-line therapy for invasive C. auris infections, but resistance to this drug class is on the rise. Here we show that, beyond resistance, C.

studi.t: Identifying key biodiversity areas in Mozambique for conservation planning and policy
studi.s: The world is experiencing unprecedented rates of biodiversity loss. To reverse this trend, signatories to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) have committed to conserving at least 30% of marine and terrestrial areas by 2030, with an emphasis on sites critical for biodiversity. One mechanism to support this goal is the identification of Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) to inform spatial planning and the development of conservation area networks. However, few case studies demonstrate how the KBA process can be implemented in high-biodiversity, low-income countries.

studi.t: Multimodal private information and reward value shape information use during ant foraging
studi.s: Animals use both private information acquired through experience and social information produced by conspecifics when making behavioural decisions. The combination of sensory cues and their associated reward value may influence how animals weigh private information against social information. We investigated information use during foraging in the ant Pristomyrmex punctatus using Y-maze experiments with learned visual and olfactory cues and trail pheromones. Workers learned both types of private cue and showed no significant preference between them when they were placed in conflict.

studi.t: SIRT3 preserves mitochondrial DNA integrity to restrain cGAS-STING signaling and autoimmune inflammation
studi.s: Mitochondria play critical roles beyond energy production, including regulation of innate immunity through release of damage-associated molecular patterns such as mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3), a mitochondrial deacetylase, modulates mitochondrial function, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and inflammation. Here, we investigate the role of SIRT3 in controlling Type I interferon (IFN) responses in macrophages.

studi.t: Structural basis for reprogramming group II intron target specificity
studi.s: Group II introns are mobile ribozymes that, with their intron-encoded protein (IEP), insert into duplex DNA without a double-strand break, a route to programmed gene insertion so far confined to bacteria. How class IIA complexes recognize and remodel duplex DNA was unknown. We identify group IIA intron/IEP pairs that retrohome efficiently into linear, relaxed duplex DNA, and report cryo-EM structures of one, Voyager-1, at successive stages of insertion.

studi.t: Distinct contributions of cohesin-STAG1 and cohesin-STAG2 to the pluripotent and totipotent states
studi.s: Cohesin organizes the three-dimensional genome and thereby regulates gene expression. In somatic cells, cohesin complexes carry either STAG1 or STAG2, paralogs that impart distinct chromatin binding dynamics and are both essential for mouse embryonic development. How each variant contributes to the maintenance and transitions of pluripotent cell state remains poorly understood.

studi.t: RBM15::MKL1 uncouples SPOC-dependent m6A remodeling from WTAP recruitment
studi.s: The recurrent t(1;22) translocation associated with pediatric acute megakaryoblastic leukemia generates the RBM15::MKL1 (RM) fusion protein that retains the RNA-binding and SPOC domains of RBM15. RBM15 recruits the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methyltransferase complex (MTC), of which WTAP is a key regulatory component. How RM engages this machinery and whether the SPOC domain is required for its leukemogenic activity remain unclear.

studi.t: Geometry shapes cytoplasmic Cdk1 waves that drive cortical dynamics
studi.s: Cell division in large embryos is coordinated by spatial waves of Cyclin B-Cdk1 activity that spread through the cytoplasm and drive cortical contractility. However, it remains unclear how cell size and nuclear enrichment of Cyclin B-Cdk1 shape these waves, and how the cytoplasmic signal is transmitted to the cortex.

studi.t: The shape of density dependence points to regulation of population growth beyond classical resource limitation
studi.s: Growth slows as population density increases, influencing species coexistence, conservation, and resource management.This slowdown is widely attributed to declining per-capita access to energy and nutrients, and standard models of resource-limited growth predict superlinear declines of growth rate with density.Contrary to this expectation, we observed sublinear declines for 90% of 3,995 bacterial and eukaryotic growth curves.

studi.t: Testing for changes in population trends from ecological count data
studi.s: 1. Accurate, up-to-date knowledge on population trends are essential for effective biodiversity conservation and for evaluating interventions. Yet, estimating trends is often limited by sparse or noisy data, and many methods require long-term monitoring, delaying timely conservation actions. 2. We present \birp{}, an R package that provides an accessible and fast Bayesian estimation framework designed to maximize power for detecting population trends.

studi.t: A Male Expressed Copulatory Plug Increases Female Fertility in Caenorhabditis Nematodes
studi.s: The genomes of self-fertilizing hermaphrodites provide an opportunity to probe why some genes with sex-specific functions are lost while others are maintained. In the androdiecious species, Caenorhabditis elegans, the presence of mate plugging is polymorphic across genetic backgrounds. The production of a mating plug is controlled by a single gene, plg-1, which has male-specific expression. Given that males are present less than 1% of the time, this gene is likely lost if mate plugging is maintained through intrasexual selection in males as is often hypothesized.

studi.t: Functional trait differences between invasive and non-invasive Lonicera (Caprifoliaceae) species
studi.s: Functional traits can influence a plant's ability to establish and spread in a new environment. Examining traits associated with resource acquisition and defense may help explain why some introduced species become invasive while others do not. This study aimed to determine whether invasive and non-invasive Lonicera species differed in growth-related, physical-defense, and chemical-defense traits at the Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University in Boston, Massachusetts.

studi.t: Conserved inhibitory mechanisms of root-associated bacteria towards Arabidopsis thaliana and Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
studi.s: Soil bacteria colonize plants without causing visible disease, yet many suppress host growth. The prevalence and evolutionary reach of this cryptic inhibition are unknown, because phenotyping hundreds of isolates in plants is prohibitively slow. Here we use the unicellular algae Chlamydomonas reinhardtii as a scalable proxy for the green lineage. We screened 148 plant-associated bacteria on Chlamydomonas lawns. Seven of eight Chlamydomonas inhibitors also inhibited the vascular model plant Arabidopsis thaliana.

studi.t: Discovery of a Novel High-Salt-Adapted Archaeal AP Endonuclease using Microfluidics-Based Cell-Free Functional Metagenomics
studi.s: We report the discovery of a novel archaeal AP endonuclease recovered from a metagenomic library constructed from environmental DNA collected in a salt-marsh ecosystem. Using an ultrahigh-throughput, cell-free functional metagenomics workflow, we screened nuclease activities in an agnostic, single-round selection format employing a DNA molecular beacon as the bait substrate. The recovered enzyme exhibits sequence and structural homology to human APE1 and displays overlapping substrate specificity toward AP sites.

studi.t: Asymmetric division and polar growth define a non-canonical cell cycle in Bradyrhizobium.
studi.s: Bradyrhizobia are widely used as plant growth promoters in agriculture, yet their cell biology remains poorly understood. Here, we described for the first time, nucleoid segregation dynamics and the cell cycle of Bradyrhizobium at the cellular level. We show that highly asymmetric polar growth generates a short daughter cell and a longer mother cell at each division. Nucleoid compaction and positioning change across growth phases, culminating in a highly compacted, asymmetrically positioned nucleoid in stationary phase. ParB presents a subpolar localization, at the nucleoid periphery.

studi.t: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the prevalence of Campylobacter and non-typhoidal Salmonella along broiler chicken production and distribution networks
studi.s: Campylobacter spp. and non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) are leading bacterial causes of gastroenteritis worldwide and can be transmitted through contaminated broiler chicken products or contact with live birds and their environment. Asymptomatic carriage of these bacteria in broiler chickens enables pathogen shedding and subsequent product contamination at any component of broiler production and distribution networks (PDNs), including broiler farms, transport, slaughter, and retail.

studi.t: From coral atolls to coal spoil heaps: two new species and two dark fungal taxa expand the monospecific genus Innospora (Paraglomerales, Glomeromycota)
studi.s: Morphological and phylogenetic analyses based on partial rDNA sequences supported the description of two new species of Innospora: Innospora atollensis sp. nov. and Innospora fodinalis sp. nov. These species expand the monospecific genus Innospora, which was formerly represented only by I. majewskii. Innospora atollensis was discovered on a coral atoll in French Polynesia, whereas I. fodinalis was recovered from a post-coal-mining spoil heap in Poland. Spores of I. atollensis and I. fodinalis are colorless, small and have a spore wall with three layers as in I. majewskii.

studi.t: DMSP modulates virus-host interactions in the coral environment
studi.s: Dimethylsulfoniopropionate (DMSP) is a ubiquitous organosulfur metabolite that plays central roles in marine ecosystems. It affects nutrient cycling, climate-relevant biogeochemical and microbial processes, including bacterial and viral infections of algal hosts, but its effect on bacteriophages has not been explored. In corals, DMSP is released under heat stress and attracts opportunistic Vibrio pathogens. Here we show that DMSP reshapes the infection dynamics of a virulent phage infecting the coral pathogen Vibrio mediterranei.

studi.t: Distinct susceptibility of masked palm civet nasal epithelium to SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2
studi.s: Masked palm civets played an important role in the emergence of SARS-CoV-1, yet physiologically relevant civet respiratory epithelial models remain limited. Here, we establish air-liquid interface cultures from primary masked palm civet nasal epithelial cells. The cultures form a differentiated, barrier-forming epithelium containing ciliated, goblet, and club cell populations and recapitulate key features of native nasal tissue. Using parallel human and civet nasal cultures, we compare infection with SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2.

studi.t: Capsidiol-inducible MFS gene BcmfsCi contributes to host-dependent virulence in the generalist fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea
studi.s: Broad-host-range plant pathogens must cope with chemical defenses that differ among host plants. This study focused on fungal genes responsive to capsidiol, a sesquiterpenoid phytoalexin produced by plants of the genera Capsicum and Nicotiana. RNA-seq analysis of the gray mold fungus Botrytis cinerea identified Bcin15g00040 as a gene strongly induced by capsidiol but not by rishitin or resveratrol. This gene was designated BcmfsCi and selected for functional characterization. The gene was predicted to encode a major facilitator superfamily (MFS) protein with 12 transmembrane helices.

studi.t: Design and analysis of synthetic carbon fixation pathways based on novel enzymatic reactions
studi.s: Biological carbon fixation is currently limited to seven naturally occurring pathways, each with its own limitations and constraints. In recent years, computational analyses of known biochemical reaction networks have identified dozens of theoretical carbon fixation pathways, some of which may have the potential to outperform their natural counterparts. This mix-and-match approach, however, cannot account for those reactions that have not been reported to occur in nature, which heavily limits the possible solution space.

studi.t: Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Improved Brain Tumor Detection
studi.s: Precise demarcation of brain tumor boundaries is critical for optimizing treatment strategies and improving patient outcomes. In vivo characterization of tumors using PET/CT and MRI is a clinical standard. PET/CT highlights metabolic processes, while MRI provides information on functional, metabolic, and structural changes. Even with technological advancements in both PET/CT and MRI, a method that can precisely delineate infiltrative tumor boundaries from normal-appearing brain regions (NABR) in vivo is still lacking.

studi.t: Binding Entropy Can Be Predicted by Crystallographic Ensembles
studi.s: Protein-ligand binding is governed by free energy, comprising both enthalpic and entropic contributions. Yet structural interpretations of binding thermodynamics have predominantly focused on enthalpic interactions, largely neglecting entropy because it is difficult to quantify from static structural models. Here, we developed multiconformer ensemble models to analyze high-resolution X-ray crystallography structures and estimate both protein and solvent conformational entropies.

studi.t: Responses of Muscle Volume, Strength, and Motor Unit Properties to Bed Rest and Retraining in Young Males and Females
studi.s: Sex differences in motor unit (MU) properties to simulated microgravity are unknown. Young males and females completed a 21-day head-down bed rest followed by a 21-day retraining. Bed rest reduced knee extensor strength and volume without sex differences. MU firing rate decreased in both groups, more in females, alongside increased serum C-terminal agrin fragment. After retraining, these measures returned to baseline, whereas strength only partially recovered, remaining below baseline.

studi.t: Genetic Variation, Iron Status, and FGF23 Signaling Converge to Regulate Renal Calcium Buffering in Sickle Cell Disease
studi.s: Sickle cell disease (SCD) causes heterogeneous mineral imbalances including variable degrees of hypocalcemia. The kidney controls systemic calcium by reabsorbing calcium from the glomerular filtrate via paracellular transport and transcellular transport in the nephron tubules, yet it is unknown whether these processes are modulated by genetic or environmental factors or disrupted in SCD.

studi.t: A xylem-specific transcriptional atlas identifies ZHD transcription factors as central transmitters of protoxylem morphology
studi.s: Xylem cell development is characterized by deposition of a rigid secondary cell wall followed by programmed cell death leading to reinforced hollow tubes enabling water transport and providing physical strength. The molecular network controlling this differentiation pathway is well established, but the early events remain poorly understood. Here, we generated and extensively validated a high resolution, xylem-specific single cell RNA-sequencing atlas of the developing xylem.

studi.t: Expansin couples salinity sensing to plant cell growth regulation
studi.s: In living plant cells, salt affects cell wall architecture directly and triggers diverse cellular responses that, in turn, feed back on wall organization and deposition. These intertwined effects obscure whether salt directly alters wall mechanical properties and thereby influences turgor-driven wall enlargement, the process underlying cell growth. In this study, we studied the tensile mechanical behavior of isolated cell wall materials at physiologically relevant salt concentrations.

studi.t: Haplotype-resolved long-read transcriptomics uncovers allele-specific heat stress induction and a nucleus-targeted chaperone isoform in potato
studi.s: Tetraploid potato is highly heterozygous, and its four haplotypes differ in gene content and regulation of gene and isoform expression, yet responses of individual haplotypes to environmental stresses remain poorly characterized. Here, we used long-read RNA sequencing to profile the haplotype-resolved leaf transcriptome of potato cv. Desiree under prolonged heat. Long-read RNA-seq gene counts correlated with short-read RNA-seq at the gene level but assigned far more reads uniquely to individual haplotypes.

studi.t: Effects of Florivore Type and Plant Chemotype on Metabolic Responses in Flowers and Leaves of an Aromatic Plant Species
studi.s: Florivory is an important biotic challenge in plant-insect interactions, evoking induced responses in plant specialised metabolism, the extent of which depends on phenotypic plasticity. While responses to leaf herbivores are well studied, floral responses to florivores with different feeding modes, their systemic effects on leaves and the role of intraspecific chemodiversity remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Dissecting rice nonhost resistance to the wheat blast fungus
studi.s: The pandemic wheat blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae destroys wheat but cannot infect rice, a form of resistance so uniform that it does not segregate in genetic crosses and cannot be mapped. We broke this nonhost resistance into single-gene phenotypes by expressing individual effectors from the wheat-infecting pathotype, one at a time, in a rice-infecting isolate. Screening 35 effectors across 20 rice cultivars (700 combinations) identified six that trigger resistance.

studi.t: Minimal, synthetic arginine deiminase pathway provides full ATP demand for cellular growth
studi.s: Bottom-up construction of synthetic cells requires a simple, yet robust ATP-generating system. The arginine deiminase (ADI) pathway offers a minimal, enzyme-based alternative to more complex ATP-producing systems such as glycolytic routes, respiratory chains or photosystems. Here, we implement the ADI pathway in Escherichia coli and test its capacity to fully replace native ATP generation. First, we designed and tested synthetic ADI operons through combinatorial library screening and selected high-performing variants.

studi.t: Hybrid virtual reality object lifting matches real-world object lifting
studi.s: Object manipulation requires anticipatory force control and online force adjustments to accommodate variability in digit position. Appropriate force scaling is learned rapidly, but repeated manipulation can interfere with updating control when object dynamics change. Sensory feedback and prior experience support object manipulation, yet how proprioception contributes remains poorly understood.

studi.t: Extracting large-scale neural activity with Suite2p
studi.s: Neural recordings using optical methods have been steadily improving. For example, we demonstrate here recordings of over 100,000 neurons from the mouse cortex obtained with a standard commercial microscope. To process such large datasets, we developed Suite2p, a collection of efficient algorithms for motion correction, cell detection, activity extraction and quality control. We also developed new approaches to benchmark performance on these tasks. Our GPU-accelerated non-rigid motion correction outperforms alternative methods, while running over five times faster.

studi.t: MRI-Based Glymphatic Markers and Their Associations with Polysomnographic Sleep in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis
studi.s: Background and Objectives: The glymphatic system is the brain waste clearance pathway. Although its dysfunction has been associated with several neurological disorders, its role in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains poorly understood. Glymphatic activity is thought to peak during sleep, yet its relationship with objectively measured sleep has scarcely been explored in humans. We assessed two MRI glymphatic proxies in patients with relapsing-remitting MS (PwMS) and healthy controls (HCs) and their associations with polysomnographic measures, structural MRI, and, in PwMS, disease burden.

studi.t: Successful retrieval is its own reward
studi.s: The ability to successfully remember past events is critical to our daily lives, yet the neural mechanisms underlying the motivation to retrieve is unclear. Although reward-system activity and feedback-related signals have been observed during memory retrieval, whether this signal reflects intrinsic reward or goal-attainment is unknown. Adjudicating between these two alternatives is crucial for understanding how individuals are motivated to engage in retrieval and how retrieval supports later remembering.

studi.t: Growth-supporting reductive defluorination by an amino acid-fermenting bacterial isolate
studi.s: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), also known as "forever chemicals", are ubiquitous environmental pollutants, highly persistent and toxic to humans and ecosystems. In addition to legacy PFAS, largely alkanoic acids, perfluorinated olefins and their corresponding enoic acids are emerging PFAS of concern. However, reported PFAS biodegradation is typically not growth-supporting, hindering the selection for effective defluorinating bacteria. Here, we report a new amino acid-fermenting bacterial isolate, Sedimentibacter sp.

studi.t: Grape branch substrates promote adaptive glycerophospholipid metabolism and lipid-synthesis gene expression in Stropharia rugosoannulata under moderate nitrogen limitation
studi.s: This study investigated the use of lignified grape plant materials (branches, stems, and roots) as cultivation substrates for Stropharia rugosoannulata and their effects on fruiting-body lipid metabolism. Metabolomic profiling identified glycerophospholipid metabolism as the primary pathway showing differential responses among substrates. While overall lipid composition remained largely unchanged, intermediate Lyso-GPL metabolites (LPA, LPC, LPI, and LPS) were more active under grape-branch substrates, indicating enhanced membrane-lipid metabolic remodeling.

studi.t: A de novo FtsA binder blocks late divisome recruitment, unmasking a hidden constriction mechanism
studi.s: Bacterial cytokinesis requires assembly of a multiprotein divisome complex, but the molecular event triggering its midcell recruitment and activity remains unclear. Recent work suggests a transition in the oligomeric structure of the conserved actin homolog FtsA may activate the divisome complex in Escherichia coli. Here, we test this model using a de novo designed protein binder, L125, predicted to block longitudinal FtsA oligomerization.

studi.t: MYC coordinates tRNA pool expansion during re-entry into proliferation by promoting pre-tRNA maturation
studi.s: Re-entry into proliferation requires rapid expansion of the translational machinery to support cell growth. How cells replenish abundant, long-lived tRNAs remains unclear. Increased RNA polymerase III activity can lead to accumulation of pre-tRNAs without proportional expansion of mature pools, suggesting that transcription alone may be insufficient. Using differentiated HepaRG cells undergoing re-entry into proliferation, we quantified precursor and mature tRNA dynamics.

studi.t: Intensive pine plantation management shapes infectious agent communities in the generalist rodent Apodemus sylvaticus, with consequences for zoonotic hazard
studi.s: Land use change is widely recognized as a major driver of emerging zoonotic diseases. Yet, while forest plantations are expanding worldwide, their consequences on the circulation of infectious agents in wildlife remain poorly understood. We investigated how native pine plantations and broadleaved habitats shape rodent-associated infectious hazard in the generalist wood mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus), in southwestern France.

studi.t: Cerebral Organization in the trilobite Yunnanocephalus yunnanensis
studi.s: TThe clade Trilobita is recognized for its extraordinary morphological diversifications amidst a highly constrained body plan. This raises the question of whether trilobite nervous systems were conservative or comparably diverse. However, despite the identification of thousands of trilobite species and increasing evidence for neural preservation in other Paleozoic euarthropods, the recognition of a fossilized trilobite brain has remained elusive. Here we describe the identification of a trilobite brain and its spatially constrained position within its cranidium.

studi.t: The Genomic Basis of Electric Signal Diversity
studi.s: Behavioral diversity is a striking result of species diversity, shaped by intertwinedmechanisms, developmental pathways, and evolutionary histories. Yet the genetic underpinnings of behavioral evolution remain obscure, even though they are key to understanding how organisms adapt and diversify. Weakly electric African elephantfishes provide a rare opportunity to dissect the genetics of behavior because their electric communication signals are quantifiable, stereotyped, and directly tied to identifiable cellular mechanisms.

studi.t: Histone H3 lysine methyltransferase activities control compartmentalization of human centromeres.
studi.s: Centromeres are essential chromosomal regions that ensure accurate genome segregation during cell division. They are organized into epigenetically discrete compartments: a Centromere Protein A (CENP-A)-rich core for microtubule attachment and surrounding heterochromatic pericentromeres that promote cohesion. Despite their importance, the mechanisms that define, enforce and partition these chromatin domains remain poorly understood. To address this, we disrupted key H3K9 methyltransferases, SUV39H1, SUV39H2, and SETDB1, that establish heterochromatin in humans.

studi.t: GHOSTs reveal a GFP-family lineage beyond marine animals that lacks Tyr66 but preserves a buried charge network
studi.s: Every characterized wild-type fluorescent protein (GFP family, Pfam PF01353) comes from a marine animal, and every one builds its chromophore with a central tyrosine, Tyr66 in Aequorea victoria GFP (avGFP). A structure-based search of the AlphaFold database for the GFP fold, followed by sequence searches, revealed a previously unrecognized lineage in bacteria, fungi, a lichen-forming fungus and corals. They carry methionine, valine, threonine or phenylalanine at the position equivalent to Tyr66. We call them GHOSTs, for GFP Homologs Omitting the Signature Tyrosine.

studi.t: A second-sphere threonine residue directs iron-oxygen species in a Fe(II)/α-ketoglutarate-dependent isonitrile synthase
studi.s: The Fe(II)/-ketoglutarate (KG)-dependent dioxygenase Rv0097 represents one of the only two isonitrile biosynthetic strategies in nature. Rv0097 synthesizes the isonitrile functional group from a glycyl-fatty acid adduct, with both the isonitrile nitrogen and carbon coming from the same glycyl moiety. To afford this challenging transformation, nature has broken it down into two half-reactions, each relying on a highly reactive Fe(IV)-oxo intermediate for hydrogen atom transfer/abstraction (HAT).

studi.t: PSMtags improve peptide sequencing and throughput in sensitive proteomics
studi.s: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics enables comprehensive characterization of proteins, but label-free approaches are challenging to scale to thousands of samples per day (SPD). Multiplexed data-independent approaches (plexDIA) can increase throughput but lack the mass tags to enable it. Here, we systematically screened a library of 576 compounds and identified several small molecules that, when conjugated to peptides, improve their detection and sequence identification.

studi.t: Large language models recover archival pathology data and identify NSE as a candidate prognostic marker in Ewing sarcoma
studi.s: Background: Current risk stratification for Ewing sarcoma relies heavily on clinical factors such as metastatic status, failing to capture histologic heterogeneity as a potential prognostic indicator. Although pathology reports contain rich biological data, this information remains locked in unstructured narrative text, limiting large-scale retrospective analyses. We aimed to validate the utility of Large Language Models (LLMs) for scalable data abstraction and to identify prognostic histologic features from a large multi-institutional cohort.

studi.t: Epigenetic and 3D Genome Changes Drive Primary Trastuzumab Resistance in HER2+ Breast Cancer
studi.s: Primary trastuzumab resistance remains a major challenge in the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer, with limited therapeutic options highlighting the need for deeper mechanistic insight. Here, integrative analysis of epigenomic and three-dimensional chromatin architecture reveals widespread remodeling of the regulatory landscape in resistant cells.

studi.t: Imageomics quantifies epidermal aging of sun-protected human skin and its rejuvenation by xenografting
studi.s: Rejuvenating aging human skin is a major therapeutic goal, but objective, quantitative measures of intrinsic aging are limited. We performed a cross-sectional histological study of UV-protected buttock and abdominal skin in Caucasian females aged 20 to 81 years to identify features that reliably track age. Epidermal thickness measured between rete ridges was unchanged, but rete ridge size declined linearly with age: ridges became shorter and thinner in both sites, though ridge number decreased only in the abdomen.

studi.t: Dendrite-wide voltage and Ca2+ imaging reveals structures of dendritic excitations during behavior
studi.s: The dynamic interplay of dendritic voltage and Ca2+ shapes neuronal integration and synaptic plasticity, but the voltage-Ca2+ relationship during behavior remains poorly defined. Using dual-color Patterned Illumination Spinning disk COnfocal (PISCO) microscopy, we simultaneously mapped voltage and Ca2+ dynamics throughout the dendritic arbors of hippocampal CA2 pyramidal neurons during spatial navigation. Fast Na+ spikes usually initiated near the soma and back-propagated throughout the dendritic tree.

studi.t: Lysosomal Glycosaminoglycan Catabolism Regulates Microglial Cell State in the Developing CNS
studi.s: Microglia acquire their adult homeostatic identity during postnatal CNS development, a period of extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, through mechanisms not fully understood. Here we show that lysosomal catabolism of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major ECM components, is a microglial function required to establish homeostatic identity. Using mouse models of Mucopolysaccharidosis VII, we examined the consequences of deleting {beta}-glucuronidase (GUSB), a lysosomal enzyme required for GAG degradation.

studi.t: Linking in situ activity to fitness reveals that clinically-relevant factors underpin pathogen survival in environmental reservoirs
studi.s: Natural environments are a key reservoir for many opportunistic pathogens, yet mechanisms enabling survival within complex microbial communities remain poorly defined. Current approaches do not adequately link molecular understanding of bacterial survival to the activities of bacteria within natural microbial communities. Here we combine in situ community profiling with isolate-level functional genomics studies to understand how opportunistic pathogens from the genera Escherichia, Klebsiella and Enterococcus survive in urban-adjacent freshwater ecosystems.

studi.t: SLFN11 restrains alternative lengthening of telomeres
studi.s: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (ALT) is a homologous recombination-dependent mechanism maintaining telomere length in approximately 10-15% of all cancers that are telomerase (TERT) negative. ALT is most prominent in osteosarcoma. Although many ALT cells feature loss of the ATRX/DAXX chromatin remodeling complex, ATRX/DAXX deficiency alone is insufficient to trigger ALT. Here, we provide evidence that Schlafen 11 (SLFN11) acts as a suppressor of the ALT pathway.

studi.t: Summary Statistics and Approximate Bayesian Computation are comparable to a Common Convolutional Neural Network Design for Inferring Fixation Times
studi.s: Detecting signatures of positive selection in genomes is a common application of population genetics and one of the most influential models for this task is the hard selective sweep where a de novo mutation rapidly fixes. Many statistics aim to detect hard sweeps by summarizing signatures left behind in the site frequency spectrum, linkage disequilibrium, and haplotype frequencies. However, potentially undiscovered signals could still exist.

studi.t: reconcILS: A gene tree-species tree reconciliation algorithm that allows for incomplete lineage sorting
studi.s: Reconciliation algorithms provide an accounting of the evolutionary history of individual gene trees given a species tree. Many reconciliation algorithms consider only duplication and loss events (and sometimes horizontal transfer), ignoring effects of the coalescent process, including incomplete lineage sorting (ILS). Here, we present a new algorithm for carrying out reconciliation that accurately accounts for incomplete lineage sorting by treating ILS as a series of nearest neighbor interchange (NNI) events.

studi.t: Lacuna: Cryptic Binding Pocket Discovery via Conformational Ensemble Analysis
studi.s: Lacuna, an open-source Python tool for discovering cryptic binding pockets: sites that are absent or too small to detect in the unbound structure of a protein, RNA or DNA and open only during conformational fluctuation. Most binding-site predictors score a single static structure, the very structure in which a cryptic site is invisible. Lacuna generates a conformational ensemble from any input structure, detects pockets independently in every conformer, clusters the detections into persistent sites, and ranks those sites with a model fitted on within-structure pairs.

studi.t: Much stronger coarse-to-fine visual processing in primate superior colliculus than primary visual cortex neurons
studi.s: The visual system optimizes its signal processing properties to efficiently encode natural scenes. The superior colliculus (SC) and primary visual cortex (V1) both play important roles in visual-motor processing, and they both exhibit qualitatively similar visual responses. However, it is not clear whether the SC simply inherits V1's efficient coding image processing optimizations or not, especially given that the SC receives a substantial amount of direct anatomical inputs from V1.

studi.t: Interference Between Pavlovian Cues and Instrumental Control: A Stratified Comparison Across Alcohol Use Disorder and Smoking
studi.s: Pavlovian cues can interfere with goal-directed behavior, particularly when they conflict with the required instrumental response. Previous research linked an increased susceptibility to such Pavlovian-to-instrumental transfer (PIT) interference to risky drinking and alcohol dependence. However, it remained unclear whether the observed behavioral and neural alterations generalize to non-treatment-seeking individuals with mild-to-moderate alcohol use disorder (AUD) and to other substances like tobacco.

studi.t: Computing coalescence rates for complex demographies and sampling configurations
studi.s: Inference of population history from genetic data relies, implicitly or explicitly, on the distribution of coalescence times, because population size changes, migration, and admixture all leave characteristic signatures in genealogies. The distribution of pairwise coalescent rates in particular has emerged as a popular target for demographic inference methods. However, pairwise coalescent rates have limited power to resolve recent history, because recent coalescences in samples of size two are rare.

studi.t: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery
studi.s: Motivation: As biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs continue to grow in size, complexity, and heterogeneity, navigating and extracting actionable insights from them presents a major bottleneck for researchers. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation.

studi.t: RAB14-dependent tubulovesicular recycling directs MET to invadopodia promoting TNBC cell invasion
studi.s: Metastasis is one of the primary causes of cancer-related death in TNBC patients. During metastasis, stromal infiltration requires the cancer cells to form invadopodia, a membraneprotrusion with proteolytic activity. Cues from growth factors via the cognate RTKs promote invadopodia formation and cancer cell invasion. This study demonstrated the role of the HGFMET axis in invadopodia formation and associated protease trafficking. MET interacts with MT1-MMP and is co-transported to the cell surface.

studi.t: Attenuated gaze synchrony in autism and its non-additive modification by co-occurring ADHD: a transdiagnostic eye-tracking study of naturalistic viewing
studi.s: Background. Autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder co-occur frequently, but whether co-occurrence compounds or alters the visual-attentional differences associated with autism remains unresolved. Inter-subject correlation (ISC) during naturalistic viewing provides a model-free index of how closely an individual's gaze and pupillary responses track those of typically developing peers. Methods.

studi.t: Cell-state mapping reveals a reversible neuroblast accumulation in the aging mouse hippocampus
studi.s: Hippocampal neurogenesis supports learning and memory by generating new granule cells throughout life. However, both the rate and speed of this process have been shown to decline with age in mice. Currently, the molecular determinants underlying the effects of aging on neuronal development and differentiation remain unknown. To elucidate these mechanisms, we combined lineage tracing with single-nucleus RNA sequencing of adult-born granule cells (aGCs) in the aging mouse hippocampus.

studi.t: Folate metabolism in tumor-associated macrophages drives immunosuppressive function to promote tumor growth
studi.s: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) promote tumor progression, inhibit anti-tumor immunity, and induce resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). Metabolism is a primary determinant of TAM polarization, suggesting therapies that selectively modulate TAM metabolic state may hold therapeutic benefit. Here we demonstrate folate uptake and metabolism sustained by the myeloid-restricted folate receptor beta (FR{beta}) are critical for TAM immunosuppressive function.

studi.t: The SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain has evolved decreased inherent antigenicity in humans
studi.s: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein has evolved rapidly since the virus began circulating in the human population. This evolution has been strongly driven by pressure to escape neutralizing antibodies, which predominantly target the spike's receptor-binding domain (RBD). Many studies have shown that mutations to the RBD during SARS- CoV-2 evolution have abrogated binding by neutralizing antibodies elicited by prior infections and vaccinations.

studi.t: Development of an Ethylenediaminetetraacetic Acid-Enhanced Deep Proteomic Profiling Method for Dried Blood Spots and Its Application in Mouse Disease Models
studi.s: Dried blood spots (DBS) are well-established microsamples used in clinical testing and newborn screening. However, their use in deep proteomics is hindered by highly abundant blood proteins and inefficient protein recovery from filter paper matrices. Notably, the non-targeted analysis of non-specifically DBS-absorbed proteins (NANDA) workflow partially overcomes the impact of abundant blood proteins and has enabled the identification of over 5,000 proteins from DBS. Nonetheless, residual abundant proteins, including hemoglobin and fibrinogen, constrain deep proteomic analysis.

studi.t: Language-guided domain adaptation improves protein sequence representations for antimicrobial resistance analysis
studi.s: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in bacterial pathogens complicates infectious disease management. Protein sequences encode molecular features underlying resistance functions such as antibiotic inactivation and drug efflux, providing a basis for investigating bacterial AMR. Protein language models can extract transferable representations from these sequences. However, general purpose protein language models have limited capacity to represent AMR-associated sequences, while task-specific tools often address individual prediction problems.

studi.t: Ribosomes are covered by a coat of flexible tails of ribosomal proteins
studi.s: The three dimensional architecture of ribosomes is known to atomic detail thanks to X-ray crystallography or cryogenic electron microscopy. However, many ribosomal proteins contain terminal regions that are averaged out during electron density reconstructions, rendering them absent from experimental models. These flexible protein tails (FPTs) collectively form an invisible coat on the ribosome surface that has been systematically overlooked.

studi.t: An Extended Clade Framework for Annotated Trees in the Context of Phylogeography and Transmission Tree Inference
studi.s: Bayesian phylogenetic inference produces large samples from a posterior distribution over phylogenetic trees that represents uncertainty in both tree topology and associated variables. Such a collection of trees is hard to interpret and it is common practice to summarize such samples into a single representative tree.Methods for constructing representative trees have largely been restricted to plain tree topologies, encoding only relationships among taxa. Inference with more sophisticated models produce annotated tree objects.

studi.t: DHHC7 palmitoylates KRAS4A and promotes mutant KRAS-driven pancreatic cancers
studi.s: KRAS mutations underlie many human cancers. While inhibitors such as Sotorasib and Adagrasib targeting KRAS mutants have shown promise, additional strategies are required to address the broader spectrum of KRAS-driven cancers, particularly those displaying drug resistance. Thus, there is a need to better understand KRAS signaling and develop new therapeutic strategies. Here we show that KRAS4A is palmitoylated on Cys180 by a palmitoyl transferase, DHHC7 (gene name ZDHHC7). Palmitoylation promotes KRAS4A plasma membrane localization and importantly nanoclustering.

studi.t: Ecology of Chagas disease vector Triatoma sanguisuga in Delaware: distribution, habitat, host use and Trypanosoma cruzi infection
studi.s: Chagas disease is a vector-borne disease caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi and transmitted by triatomine bugs. The disease is increasingly recognized as an emerging public health threat in the United States (US). Little is known about the Chagas disease system in the Mid-Atlantic US despite the presence of a native T. cruzi vector species, Triatoma sanguisuga. The species is widespread throughout the eastern US, and the Mid-Atlantic comprises the northernmost portion of its geographic range. Triatoma sanguisuga has been implicated in autochthonous T.

studi.t: Local GEBVs and additive variance in maize heterotic groups across low- and high-stress environments
studi.s: Hybrid maize (Zea mays L.) parents are chosen within heterotic groups. Drought and heat stress are expected to become more frequent, but little is known about how they change the additive variance of each group and where in the genome it lies. We analyzed testcross grain yield from 62 Genomes to Fields environments, classified as low or high stress by climate. For 1,362 parents from three heterotic groups and two doubled-haploid families, we fitted a genomic model with group deviations and calculated local genomic estimated breeding values in 164-kb segments.

studi.t: Unlocking Programmable and Creative RNA Sequence Design with RDiffusion
studi.s: RNA, a pillar of the central dogma, has shaped three billion years of evolution. Despite cataloging tens of millions of non-coding RNAs and annotating millions, we have barely scratched the surface of the vast, unexplored RNA sequence space. Here, we introduce RDiffusion, a discrete-diffusion-based generative transformer model for RNA sequence design. Conditioned on diverse biological features, such as desired function, family type, secondary and tertiary structure, or binding protein partners, it can guide the generation of novel RNA sequences tailored to specific design specifications.

studi.t: Neutrophil extracellular traps and thrombotic components across human coronary plaque progression: Association of intraplaque hemorrhage with NET formation
studi.s: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), fibrin, and von Willebrand factor (VWF) are present in acute coronary thrombotic plaques. This study aimed to investigate their distribution among the coronary atherosclerotic progression and the potential association between intraplaque hemorrhage and NET formation. Coronary artery sections from autopsy cases of non-cardiac death (n = 5, 37 sections) and ischemic heart disease (n = 11, 65 sections) were classified into six morphological groups and examined immunohistochemically.

studi.t: Prediction Dynamically Modulates Gain and Width of Population Frequency Tuning in Human Auditory Cortex
studi.s: During perception, the brain must veridically portray sensory representations while simultaneously highlighting unexpected events. According to two-process theory of predictive perception, this balance is achieved via complementary mechanisms: precision-weighted predictions sharpen sensory tuning around expected features, while momentary surprisal scales response gain, dampening expected inputs and amplifying unexpected violations.

studi.t: Functional Conservation Amid Extreme Divergence in Freshwater SAR11 Hypervariable Region 2
studi.s: The Ca. Pelagibacterales order (SAR11) is a ubiquitous bacterioplankton in aquatic ecosystems. The genomes of SAR11 bacteria contain hypervariable region 2 (HVR2), the largest HVR with extreme diversity. Previous studies collectively indicated the enrichment of cell-surface modification genes on HVR2, which have been hypothesized to facilitate phage evasion. However, characterisation of HVR2 has primarily targeted marine clades and been limited for freshwater SAR11 (aka. Fontibacterium).

studi.t: PerturbBridge: Conditional Latent Schr dinger Bridge for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
studi.s: \textbf{Motivation:}Single-cell perturbation prediction seeks to recover transcriptional responses to unseen interventions from unpaired control and perturbed populations. The Schr\"odinger Bridge provides a principled framework for modeling these transitions as stochastic transport, but learning bridge dynamics directly from high-dimensional, sparse gene-expression profiles remains challenging. \textbf{Results:} We present PerturbBridge, a conditional latent Schr\"odinger Bridge framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

studi.t: Advancing Cognitive Pairwise Comparisons for Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
studi.s: Human-centric artificial intelligence and data science (HCAD) systems increasingly involve human-in-the-loop (HITL) interventions to overcome the limitations of fully automated machine learning algorithms, such as automation bias and the inability to incorporate tacit domain knowledge, and continuously improve predictive performance.

studi.t: Auditing a Moving Target: Evidence Anchoring and the Expiry of Fairness Audits of Provider-Served Language Models
studi.s: Organizations increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for decisions about people, such as hiring, investment and employee evaluation, and rely on them over long periods of time. Fairness audits of such systems, however, are conducted only once. We examine how the biases of LLMs change over time. In a venture screening setting, models from five providers decided whether and how much to invest in startups whose founders differed only in gender, origin and university. We repeated this audit three times over 13 months (248,400 API calls).

studi.t: Lived Experiences of Power and Agency: Achieving Voice Sovereignty in Assistive Speech Technology for Nonbinary Users
studi.s: Speech-generating devices (SGDs) are essential tools for many speech-disabled individuals, yet current systems often reinforce normative assumptions about identity and communication. Prior research on gender expansive SGD users has largely focused on gendered voice options, with less attention to broader identity alignment and the technological conditions that shape users' agency. This study examines how gender expansive SGD users experience power over their voices using thematic analysis of qualitative survey data.

studi.t: What Do Digital Traces Predict? Task Effects, Student Differences, and Critical Online Reasoning
studi.s: Digital assessment traces are increasingly used to predict student performance, often evaluated by correlating predicted and observed scores pooled across tasks. However, such correlations may reflect between-task differences rather than performance differences among students within tasks. To investigate this, we analyzed up to 527 browsing sessions from 424 university students completing open-Internet Critical Online Reasoning tasks and assessed the cross-task stability of their ratings.

studi.t: EEGProbe: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand EEG? A Benchmark for Signal-Grounded EEG Signals Evaluation
studi.s: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong multimodal capabilities across scientific and biomedical domains, yet their ability to understand electroencephalography (EEG) signals remains unclear. We introduce EEGProbe, a signal-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether general-purpose VLMs can extract and reason from minimally processed, channel-wise EEG without task-specific feature engineering or EEG-specific adaptation.

studi.t: UIAnchor: Anchoring UI Perception and Action Execution for Reliable Service-Composed Mobile Task Automation with GUI Agents
studi.s: Mobile task automation aims to streamline multi-step, cross-app interactions on smartphones and in-vehicle systems. Recent LLM-based GUI agents have advanced rapidly, yet reliability remains limited because modern mobile workflows are increasingly service-composed (app switching, forms, pop-ups/permissions, copy-paste), requiring fine-grained operations on dense, dynamic, and heterogeneous UIs, often in distraction-sensitive contexts (e.g., hands-busy or attention-limited use).

studi.t: Injectra: Retrofitting Extensibility into Web-Based Desktop Applications
studi.s: Large language models can generate code based on natural language prompts, opening up new possibilities for users to customize software and extend its functionality. This paper proposes and implements Injectra, a general-purpose code injection and feature enhancement system for existing desktop clients, suitable for applications whose user interfaces are built using embedded browser engines (such as Electron) or system WebViews (such as Tauri). Injectra decouples the host integration logic from the upper-layer enhancement code.

studi.t: UbiHearo: Bringing Scenario-Aware Sound Guidance to DHH Users with Mobile Agents
studi.s: For Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) users, effective sound awareness goes beyond detecting \emph{what} sound occurs; it requires understanding \emph{what it means}, \emph{how urgent it is}, and \emph{what to do}. However, existing mobile assistants largely reduce acoustic scenes to isolated labels or generic alerts, failing to provide contextual guidance when the same sound implies different risks across scenarios. We present \sysname, a mobile hearing assistant agent that closes the sensing--reasoning--action loop for \textit{scenario-aware} and \textit{personalized} DHH assistance.

studi.t: Who Bears the Excess? Imputing the Acts of AI Agents to Those Who Delegate
studi.s: When an AI agent acts outside the authority conferred on it, the actor is not a legal subject and the legal subjects did not act. The literature of 2026 agrees that the agent cannot bear responsibility and that the burden falls on those who deploy it, but it leaves open where that duty sits in positive law and how it is proved. This paper proposes a rule of imputation. The excess is imputed to whoever conferred the delegation, to the extent of the perimeter it documented and of the control it actually exercised.

studi.t: Two-Stage Staffing with Random Arrival Rate: A Simulation Optimization Approach
studi.s: In service systems, the arrival rate in the same time period and day of the week exhibits randomness, yet can be more accurately estimated or forecast right before that period, which motivates a two-stage staffing scheme with advance base staffing and pre-shift surge staffing. Existing approaches usually impose strong assumptions on the arrival process and service systems' operational logic and other further approximations (i.e., stylized models) to derive explicit staffing policies.

studi.t: Learning Design Taste through Verifiable Synthetic Environments and Agentic Reinforcement Learning
studi.s: Code-generating language models produce user interfaces that build and run, but the pages are often weak in hierarchy, spacing, typography and composition. We study whether a small code model can learn design taste through reinforcement learning in verifiable synthetic environments. The method has three components. First, a layered verification framework splits design quality into hard gates, render-grounded metrics, rubric judges, within-group relative preference and a blinded expert panel.

studi.t: Same Papers, Different Verdicts: Tracing Version Drift in LLM Peer Review
studi.s: Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them.

studi.t: Necessary for What? Auditing Demographic Disclosure to LLM Synthetic Respondents
studi.s: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly answer surveys on behalf of real panelists, and each panelist's recorded demographic attributes (e.g., age, education, ethnicity) are often placed in the prompt on the premise that richer profiles make more faithful synthetic respondents. While data minimization limits personal data to what a purpose requires, a synthetic survey serves several purposes at once, from predicting individual answers to estimating how opinions are distributed and comparing groups.

studi.t: Effective and Efficient Rumor Assertion Over Large-Scale Social Networks (Technical Report)
studi.s: Nowadays, social networks, like Facebook, X, Reddit, YouTube, and so on, have become essential online platforms for users to connect with friends daily, post/share news, and express their opinions/comments. Meanwhile, however, the rapid and widespread dissemination of rumors and misinformation across social networks has become a serious concern. Such misleading information can distort public opinion and potentially cause significant social and economic consequences in real-world scenarios, including product promotion, elections and voting, and even cyberbullying.

studi.t: AI Tool Adoption and Loyalty among Product, Industrial, and UX/UI Designers across the Double Diamond
studi.s: Designers share many AI tools, yet their roles produce different work. This survey compared 337 Product, Industrial and UX/UI Designers from 40 countries and regions across the four phases of the Double Diamond. It measured AI adoption, breadth and frequency, tool function and the number of tools named per phase. A tool was loyal when a role picked it in all four phases. Industrial Designers adopted AI less often (73.9% against 88.2% and 87.9%), a gap that went with physical projects once project type and country were held constant.

studi.t: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
studi.s: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss.

studi.t: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
studi.s: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues.

studi.t: N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid Triggers Systemic Acquired Resistance Against Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) in Wheat
studi.s: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) represents a conserved immune strategy enabling plants to mount long-lasting, whole-plant protection following localized pathogen challenge. In Arabidopsis thaliana, SAR is orchestrated by the mobile immune regulator N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP); however, the extent to which NHP defines systemic immune states in polyploid crops remains unclear. Here, we establish NHP as an inducer of systemic immunity in hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) during infection by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia triticina.

studi.t: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
studi.s: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank.

studi.t: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
studi.s: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro.

studi.t: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
studi.s: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants.

studi.t: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
studi.s: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species.

studi.t: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
studi.s: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood.

studi.t: Do altered neural responses during self-reflection converge across psychiatric disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies
studi.s: Altered neural responses during self-reflection have been reported across psychiatric disorders, but it is unknown whether there exist common brain regions across studies. To fill the gap, we conducted a systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies. Through systematic literature search and article screening, we identified 36 studies across 8 diagnostic categories, of which 25 studies were eligible for the ALE meta-analysis.

studi.t: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
studi.s: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner.

studi.t: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
studi.s: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008).
