It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species.

studi.t: Centromere divergence and allopolyploidy reshape carnivorous sundew genomes
studi.s: Centromeres are essential for chromosome function, yet how contrasting centromere architectures shape polyploid genome evolution and plant diversification remains unresolved. In monocentric chromosomes, centromeric activity is restricted to one chromosomal region; in holocentric chromosomes, it is distributed along the chromosome length. Hybridization followed by genome doubling can place chromosome sets with different centromeres, repeat complements, and rearrangement histories in the same nucleus.

studi.t: CLASSIFICATION OF PROKARYOTIC DNA METHYLTRANSFERASES BY CATALYTIC DOMAIN TOPOLOGY
studi.s: Prokaryotic DNA methyltransferases (MTases) are essential enzymes that play a crucial role in restriction-modification systems, preventing the degradation of self DNA by restriction enzymes. In addition, they contribute to the regulation of gene expression, DNA repair, DNA replication, and other processes. Here, we propose a novel classification of prokaryotic MTases based on the 3D topology of the catalytic domain, which addresses the limitations of the previous scheme developed by Malone and Bujnicki.

studi.t: Restriction Enzyme activity under Force determined with autonomous DNA Origami Force Clamps via Gel Electrophoresis
studi.s: Investigating force-depending behaviour in biological systems is a challenging task, with most techniques requiring complex experimental equipment while also often being limited in scalability. We designed a facile force spectroscopy technique using DNA origami-based force clamps that apply forces up to ~40 pN. We validated the approach by using type II endonucleases that have been previously studied quantitatively by single-molecule measurements.

studi.t: Biomolecular design through latent reasoning with RFD4-Proteina
studi.s: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space.

studi.t: ISdetector: precise mapping of insertion sequences and associated structural variations from short-read sequencing data
studi.s: Motivation. Repetitive insertion sequences (ISs) and adjacent structural variants (SVs) complicate precise mapping from bacte-rial short reads. Accurate insertion coordinates are important for studying genome evolution and tracking transmission. Results. ISdetector constructs IS-specific references with target copies removed and clusters soft-clipped reads to pinpoint insertion sites. On simulated genomes, it had higher recall and F1 score than ISMapper and MGEFinder. On 19 Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes, it achieved the highest high-confidence F1 score (0.86).

studi.t: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
studi.s: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression.

studi.t: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
studi.s: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform.

studi.t: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
studi.s: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods.

studi.t: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
studi.s: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes.

studi.t: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
studi.s: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.

studi.t: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
studi.s: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively.

studi.t: Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
studi.s: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS).

studi.t: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
studi.s: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture.

studi.t: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
studi.s: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation.

studi.t: Combination of in vitro and ex vivo infection models highlights the role of NAD-dependent ADP-ribosylation in Influenza A virus infection.
studi.s: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a major public health concern, causing an estimated 650 000 deaths annually. Although vaccines are available, vaccination coverage is limited and must be repeated annually due to the genetic variability of these viruses. Furthermore, although direct acting antivirals are available, they must be administered as early as possible after infection to be effective.

studi.t: Azospirillum brasilense and cytidine as combination treatment to enhance drought resilience of peas
studi.s: Aims: This study tested the efficacy of two combination treatments on drought resilience of peas; Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 with the chemoattractant seedling exudate compound cytidine or pea seedling exudate. Methods and Results: Phenotypic characterization revealed that drought tolerance of peas treated with ACyt was 68.9% higher than that of peas treated with the inoculant alone (A). Dry shoot weight of ACyt Drought plants was 30.7% higher than that of plants from the untreated control group NB Drought, drought recovery of ACyt plants was 21.6% better.

studi.t: Highly multiplexed fluorescent imaging via fluidic-free, rapid sequential plasmonic heating activated signal exchange of DNA probes
studi.s: Fluorescence microscopic methods are critical for spatial profiling of multiple biological targets in cells and tissues to study cell and tissue functions, but their multiplexity was limited to 3~5 targets under a conventional setup using different fluorescent channels because of spectra overlap. Here, we introduce a simple, rapid, wash-free multiplexed fluorescence imaging method in cells and tissues, termed DNA based plasmonic heating activated signal exchange reaction (PHASER).

studi.t: Transcription factor activities as a shared representation for drug repurposing hypotheses in breast cancer
studi.s: Drug repurposing could expand the limited targeted options for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). PRECISION trains a heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) over prior-knowledge edges on the PRISM screen, describing cell lines mostly by transcription factor (TF) activities. On held-out cell lines the GNN fell below a drug-mean reference and a TF-based Random Forest. Integrated Gradients attributions define ten core TFs, shared by the drugs examined and partly stable across seeds.

studi.t: Biological network topology is a structural prior for data-efficient sparse learning
studi.s: Biological networks, from gene co-expression circuits to cortical connectomes and animal societies, share sparse, modular, small-world topologies thought to reflect optimization for efficient infor-mation routing under resource constraints. Whether these structural signatures can act as inductive biases for artificial learning is unknown. We initialized sparse multilayer perceptrons with adjacen-cy matrices inferred by mutual information from molecular, structural, functional, and behavioral networks.

studi.t: Elementary Dynamics of Neural Microcircuits
studi.s: In neural circuits with multiple excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) cell types, qualitatively new dynamics arise when one population is silenced by the others, an effect linear theories cannot capture. Using threshold-linear networks, the simplest nonlinear population model, we derive closed-form conditions for multistability, oscillations, and paradoxical responses across microcircuits. In E-I circuits, strengthening E$\rightarrow$I rather than I$\rightarrow$E connections controls runaway excitation without silencing E cells.

studi.t: Categorical Bayes Filtering for Computational Phenotyping in Adaptive Learning
studi.s: Adaptive learning depends on inferring the sources of uncertainty in the environment. Simultaneous estimation of two such sources, volatility and stochasticity, is difficult, but critical for adaptive learning. The two require opposite adjustments of the learning rate, yet both inflate the variance of experienced outcomes, and no closed-form solution exists for dissociating them. Particle filters are the standard method for this joint inference, but their likelihood is stochastic and their objective is not differentiable, so fitting requires derivative-free methods that add estimator noise.

studi.t: SroA links SigS-dependent stress signaling to metabolic remodeling in Staphylococcus aureus
studi.s: Staphylococcus aureus encounters diverse environmental conditions during colonization and infection, including fluctuations in nutrient availability, oxidative stress, and oxygen limitation. Adaptation to these environments requires regulatory systems that coordinate stress responses with metabolic physiology. The extracytoplasmic function sigma factor SigS contributes to stress adaptation and virulence in S. aureus and directly activates expression of the sroAB operon, which encodes the small proteins SroA and SroB.

studi.t: Is sediment porosity a confounder in sedimentary DNA records? A test in a temperate semi-enclosed bay
studi.s: Sedimentary environmental DNA (eDNA) has recently been widely used to reconstruct biological communities and to clarify ecosystem dynamics in natural environments. Sediment porosity is thought to influence DNA preservation, but whether it explains variation in sedimentary eDNA beyond depositional setting and burial depth has rarely been tested in natural environments. We analysed metabarcoding data of 18S rRNA and cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) together with porosity profiles from eight cores (to 6 m depth) collected from the inner and mouth regions of Uranouchi Bay, Japan.

studi.t: A large but weakened soil carbon sink in resampled forests and grasslands
studi.s: The land carbon sink is composed of vegetation and soil carbon change, but only vegetation change has been quantified by observations at global scale (1-6). Recent changes in soil organic carbon (SOC) remain highly uncertain, with process models disagreeing even on its direction (7, 8). Repeated soil sampling is the most direct measure of SOC change, but these measurements have not been synthesized. Here, we compiled repeated SOC measurements from 4,883 sites, representing environmental conditions across 30% of the world's forests and grasslands without land-use change.

studi.t: Substitution rate variation, not hidden paralogy, drives false hybridization signal in phylogenetic network inference
studi.s: Phylogenetic network inference methods are increasingly used to detect hybridization and gene [fl]ow from genomic data, but their robustness to common sources of model violation remains poorly characterized. We conducted a simulation study to evaluate the e[ff]ects of hidden paralogy and substitution rate variation on three commonly used network inference methods: find_graphs from ADMIXTOOLS 2, SNaQ and PhyNEST.

studi.t: Regulating Light-Harvesting Protein Assembly through Engineered Trimers of Phycocyanin and Allophycocyanin
studi.s: Phycobilisome-associated phycobiliproteins naturally assemble into trimeric and hexameric architectures, making it difficult to isolate stable trimeric species for structural and functional studies. Here, we establish a rational strategy to generate stable trimers of phycocyanin (TeCPC) and allophycocyanin (TeAPC) from Thermosynechococcus elongatus by destabilizing the hexamerization interface. We introduce structure-guided glycine-to-arginine substitutions, G29R in TeCPC and G21R in TeAPC, to suppress hexamer formation.

studi.t: Expanding Therapeutic Target Space from Genes to Disease-Relevant Molecular Forms with 3DisoTarget
studi.s: Therapeutic targets are commonly defined at the gene or canonical protein level, yet therapeutic effects are ultimately exerted through specific molecular states operating in specific biological contexts. Alternative splicing generates diverse RNA and translated protein forms whose functional consequences, disease relevance, and therapeutic vulnerabilities can differ substantially within the same gene.

studi.t: Listening to the room: disrupting activity of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex impairs learning of room acoustics in human listeners
studi.s: Navigating complex sensory environments is critical to survival, and brain mechanisms have evolved to cope with the wide range of surroundings we encounter. To determine how listeners learn the statistical properties of acoustic spaces, we assessed their ability to perceive speech in a range of noisy and reverberant rooms. Listeners were also exposed to repetitive transcranial stimulation (rTMS) to disrupt the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) activity, a region believed to play a role in statistical learning.

studi.t: Ventromedial striatal dopamine dynamically integrates motivated action and reward proximity
studi.s: Dopamine release in the ventromedial striatum (VMS) both invigorates actions and encodes reward-related information, yet how these functions are integrated remains under active debate. To investigate this further, we designed four different versions of a rat Go/No-go task, where we systematically manipulated response requirements, temporal task demands, and controllability of reward pursuit. Dopamine release increased reliably during action initiation (Go) but was delayed during action suppression (No-go), and this difference was insensitive to augmented response demands or controllability.

studi.t: 2'-O-Methylated ncRNA condensates form a recombination center for IgH synapsis
studi.s: While FBL-mediated RNA 2'-O-methylation has been linked to class switch recombination (CSR), how this epitranscriptomic mark orchestrates higher-order genomic architecture remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that FBL selectively promotes switch (S)-S DNA synapsis at the IgH locus during CSR, without affecting DNA cleavage. Both RNA-binding and catalytic activities of FBL were essential for CSR. Moreover, MED19 supported DNA cleavage and synapsis by regulating snoRNAs that guide 2'-O-methylation.

studi.t: Statin-Induced Mitochondrial Coenzyme Q Deficiency Alters Mitochondrial Redox Homeostasis and Bioenergetic Function in Astrocytes
studi.s: Statins, widely used cholesterol-lowering drugs, inhibit the mevalonate pathway and reduce coenzyme Q (CoQ) biosynthesis, potentially impairing mitochondrial function. Because astrocytes are essential for maintaining brain redox homeostasis, statin-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in these cells may contribute to central nervous system pathology. Therefore, this study examined the effects of a 6-day statin exposure on mitochondrial bioenergetics in rat astrocytes, focusing on mitochondrial CoQ (mtCoQ) deficiency.

studi.t: Systematic benchmarking of small variant calling pipelines for long-read RNA sequencing data
studi.s: Background: Long-read RNA sequencing (lrRNA-seq) enables transcript-resolved variant detection, but systematic and neutral evaluations of small variants calling pipelines remain limited. The performance of existing tools across sequencing technologies, alignment strategies, variant caller choice, genomic contexts and downstream haplotype phasing is not fully understood.

studi.t: Harnessing Contextual Embeddings: A Deep Learning Framework for Predicting PCR Amplification Using BERT Tokenization
studi.s: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is a widely used molecular biology technique to amplify DNA sequences. PCR amplification is affected by factors such as binding dynamics and primer-template interactions. This study aims to reduce the time and cost of the experiment by predicting PCR outcomes based on these factors. To achieve this, we first identify the most stable binding sites for each primer-template pair by calculating the Gibbs free energy.

studi.t: SWELL1 channel-mediated D-2HG export promotes immune evasion and metabolic fitness in IDH-mutant gliomas
studi.s: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) is the most frequently mutated metabolic enzyme in human cancers. Mutant IDH produces D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2HG), which promotes tumorigenesis through epigenetic alterations. Beyond cell-autonomous effects, tumor-derived D-2HG acts as a potent immunosuppressant that establishes an immune-cold tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the mechanism by which D-2HG is released from tumors remains largely unknown.

studi.t: A single complex V2 as an alternative hypothesis for the organization of mouse higher visual cortex
studi.s: The mouse has become a major model for studies of the visual system, creating a need for principles of areal delineation that can be compared across species. In many well-studied mammals, V1 is bordered by a single second visual area, V2, whereas the cortex immediately surrounding mouse V1 is commonly parcellated into roughly eight higher-order visual areas (HVAs), with boundaries defined in part by reversals in the progression of the visual field.

studi.t: Mass-transfer-constrained thermodynamics links fluid motion to the preferential use of hydrogen and formate in syntrophic propionate oxidation
studi.s: Syntrophic propionate oxidation in methanogenic environments depends on interspecies electron transfer via hydrogen and formate, yet the physical factors governing the relative use of these electron carriers remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how fluid flow reshapes electron-transfer energetics and pathway expression in the obligately syntrophic propionate oxidizer Pelotomaculum schinkii grown in coculture with Methanospirillum hungatei.

studi.t: Non-cognate molecular interactions impact bacterial growth
studi.s: In gene regulatory networks, appropriate gene expression is often determined through high-affinity binding of transcription factors (TFs) to their cognate DNA sequences. However, the large genomic background likely contains many DNA sequences similar to the TF target motifs, potentially allowing for ample low-affinity non-cognate TF binding. Whether and how non-cognate TF binding impacts cellular function and growth remains unclear.

studi.t: Functional Data Clustering of Filopodia Dynamics
studi.s: Notch signaling plays a significant role in tissue patterning. During patterning of the fruit fly dorsal thorax peripheral nervous system, basal filopodia extend the spatial range of cell-cell communication, yet it is still unclear how Notch is activated in long range signaling via filopodia interaction. Filopodia undergo dynamic length changes during their lifetime, which could supply the mechanical pulling force required for notch activation.

studi.t: Methane emissions from upland tree stems reflect a balance of microbial production and consumption
studi.s: Upland trees emit methane (CH4), but whether it is produced inside the wood or transported from soil remains debated. Methanogens occur in the heartwood of several species, yet their relation to co-occurring methanotrophs is poorly understood. We measured 1,200 stem and 288 soil fluxes, sampled internal stem gases including {delta}13CH4, quantified methanogens and methanotrophs via droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) in 592 samples, sequenced 16S rRNA genes, and bounded stand-scale fluxes.

studi.t: Biophysical resetting of specialization enables metabolic network diversification
studi.s: Organisms must integrate external inputs whose availability they do not control in internal functions that require precision. Birds exemplify this challenge: they cannot synthesize carotenoids, yet closely integrate diet-derived carotenoids into vision, pigmentation and yolk provisioning, raising the question of how unpredictability of external supply coevolves with precision of internal use.

studi.t: Carbon concentrating mechanisms in a small coastal diatom demonstrate sensitivity to changes in Zinc and carbonate chemistry
studi.s: The efficiency of marine diatom carbon concentrating mechanisms (CCMs) play a critical role in photosynthesis, enabling cells to maintain rapid growth rates under a variety of environmental conditions. To assess the plasticity of the model diatom P. tricornutum s CCMs, specifically carbonic anhydrase (CA) enzymes and bicarbonate transporters, we measured growth response, bulk CA activity, and corresponding shifts in the proteome under a range of Zn and pCO2 conditions in culture. CA activity increased with Zn availability and decreased with pCO2.

studi.t: STARgrid - an open end-to-end pipeline for Visium HD
studi.s: Grid-based spatial transcriptomics quantifies expression by counting reads, assigning them to genes and, from their barcodes, to capture locations on a grid, which is registered to a microscope image. For Visium HD, only the vendor's Space Ranger performs all these steps, and its licences prohibit redistributing it or software derived from it. We present STARgrid, an open-source, end-to-end, agent-ready pipeline from Visium HD FASTQ files and images to count matrices registered to the tissue.

studi.t: spearfish: ultrafast Δ-mapping of long reads to redundant transcriptomes
studi.s: In a transcriptome, isoforms share most of their sequence, and gene families add further near-copies. Yet most long-read mappers treat each isoform as a separate target and repeat seeding, chaining and alignment for each. We introduce spearfish, a long-read mapper built for this redundancy. Its delta mapping ({Delta}-mapping) computes each target's alignment-score difference from the best candidate. It skips sequence that all candidates share, which cannot change the difference, and aligns where they differ once per distinct sequence rather than once per target.

studi.t: DeepCDS: Ab initio coding sequence prediction in prokaryotic metagenomic short reads
studi.s: Accurate coding sequence prediction in short prokaryotic metagenomic sequences, such as Illumina reads, remains challenging due to sequence fragmentation, unknown sequence origins, and sequencing errors. Here we introduce DeepCDS, a deep learning-based ab initio coding sequence predictor trained on short prokaryotic sequences with and without simulated Illumina-like sequencing errors. DeepCDS integrates embeddings from the protein language model ESM-2 with nucleotide-level information to predict complete and partial coding sequences.

studi.t: Loop-Directed Cofactor Binding Enables Programmable Multico-factor Protein Design
studi.s: The emergence of respiratory, photosynthetic, and assimilatory complexes in evolution required proteins capable of binding multiple catalytic and electron-transfer cofactors while exerting fine control over their spatial arrangement. Across natural systems these cofactors are preferentially positioned in loop regions. In contrast, most protein design strategies have focused on installing cofactor-binding sites within helical elements.

studi.t: Auditory Profiles in Tinnitus are Age-Dependent: Electrophysiological and Behavioral Evidence
studi.s: Tinnitus is commonly associated with hearing loss, yet it can also occur in individuals with clinically normal audiometric thresholds. This dissociation has led to the hypothesis that hidden sensorineural hearing loss underlies tinnitus in audiometrically normal-hearing individuals. However, identifying such subclinical deficits non-invasively is challenging because audiometric measures are influenced by age-related changes and interactions among sensorineural processes.

studi.t: BenchRep-T: A Systematic Evaluation of T-Cell Repertoire-Based Disease Diagnostics
studi.s: Adaptive immune receptor repertoire sequencing data has emerged as a promising potential modality for disease diagnosis, relying on computational methods to analyze T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences from an individual's blood sample. Published methods rely on different cohorts, data preprocessing pipelines, and evaluation metrics, making direct comparison across methods challenging.

studi.t: HLF suppresses DREAM target genes and reinstates quiescence in lung squamous cell carcinoma
studi.s: Rationale: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) originates from airway basal stem cells and carries frequent TP53 mutations and RB pathway disruption, yet lacks oncogene-directed therapies. Here, using single-cell transcriptomics of healthy airway epithelium and primary LUSC tumors, we resolve four basal cell states along a quiescence-to-activation gradient and identify HLF as a transcription factor restricted to the most primitive quiescent population.

studi.t: Mural cell contractility regulates vessel diameter by controlling cell morphology and vessel coverage
studi.s: Mural cells regulate vascular architecture, but how their contractility and morphology together determine vessel diameter is unclear. Using high-resolution live imaging and single-cell morphometrics in zebrafish, we show that vSMCs and pericytes progressively retract actin-rich processes and decrease in size during development. Mural cell-specific manipulation of RhoA activity altered cell morphology and vessel coverage, revealing vessel- and stage-dependent effects on vascular calibre.

studi.t: The role of the roof plate for mesencephalic trigeminal neuron
studi.s: Abstract The mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus (MTN) contains the proprioceptive sensory neurons that innervate mechanoreceptors in the jaw closing muscles. In the chick embryo, MTN neurons are the first neurons generated in the mesencephalon. They arise bilaterally adjacent to the roof plate and then extend their axons ventrally before projecting caudally towards the rhombencephalon. MTN axons remain in a mid - dorsoventral position and pioneer the lateral longitudinal fasciculus.

studi.t: DAPHNE: A global database of pest herbivores and their natural enemies
studi.s: Anticipating and managing the impact of herbivorous pests requires evidence-based knowledge about the interactions between pests and their natural enemies. Knowledge of species' ecologies and biological interactions are typically disseminated in unstructured text across hundreds of thousands of scientific articles spanning a rapidly growing scientific literature, but manually screening this literature is time-consuming and impractical at scale.

studi.t: Fog adaptation and wind connectivity in an endangered California plant: a genomic baseline for wind energy development
studi.s: Fog buffers water stress in several arid, highly seasonal coastal ecosystems with exceptional plant endemism, yet the genomic basis of adaptation to fog remains almost entirely uncharacterized. We resequenced 842 genomes from six localities of the endangered Gaviota tarplant (Deinandra increscens subsp. villosa), endemic to the fog-swept central California coast, where a wind farm was built across the largest population.

studi.t: Conformational heterogeneity and state-dependent stability of active-site loops in Trametes versicolor laccase
studi.s: How can a single active site accept substrates that differ widely in size, shape and charge? We have addressed this question for the fungal laccase from Trametes versicolor, a promiscuous multicopper oxidase, by mapping the conformational ensemble of the substrate-free (but fully copper-loaded) enzyme.

studi.t: Interactions with lipid membrane modulate the conformational dynamics and energy landscape of Tumor Necrosis Factor
studi.s: Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) is a trimeric cytokine that exists in soluble (sTNF) and membrane-bound (mTNF) forms, both of which regulate immune responses through interactions with their cognate receptors. sTNF has been the subject of extensive biophysical investigations, leading to a prevailing mechanistic model in which a symmetric arrangement of the trimer promotes receptor signaling, whereas asymmetric conformations inhibit this function. In contrast, the structural and energetic landscape of mTNF remains largely under-explored.

studi.t: CD24 Acts as an Evolutionarily Conserved Innate Immune Checkpoint in Colorectal Cancer
studi.s: Checkpoint immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet current approaches targeting adaptive immunity benefit only a subset of patients, leaving innate immunity as a largely untapped therapeutic frontier. Here, we identify CD24 as an innate immune checkpoint that protects colorectal tumors from macrophage-mediated clearance through an evolutionarily conserved recognition mechanism. Using zebrafish xenografts of isogenic colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines, SW480 and SW620, we show that high CD24 expression in SW620 correlates with an immune-evasive, macrophage-resistant phenotype.

studi.t: Calcium: Modulator of Post-transcriptional and post-translational process in mESCs
studi.s: Calcium ions (Ca2+) are ubiquitous intracellular and extracellular messengers that regulate several cellular activities. Previous findings have reported active Ca2+ receptors in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), but the fundamental requirement for Ca2+ signalling remains unclear. We have noted high Ca2+ levels in undifferentiated mESCs and observed that its depletion induces G2/M cell cycle arrest, spontaneous differentiation of mESCs towards mesoderm-like lineage, and changes in mitochondrial morphology and number.

studi.t: A comprehensive temporal proteome and phosphoproteome dataset of Y1 adrenocortical cells under FGF2 stimulation and SOS inhibition
studi.s: The Y1 mouse adrenocortical tumor cell line is a classic model for cancer studies and ACTH mediated steroidogenesis. The KRAS gene amplification and SOS mediated activation sustain elevated ERK levels, which drive the tumor phenotype of this cell line. In addition, the mitogen FGF2 induces atypical cytotoxic stress and consequent cell death rather than proliferation in this system, imposing a strong perturbation on KRAS ERK signaling dynamics.

studi.t: Multicellular signaling in reverse cardiac remodeling revealed by integrated bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics
studi.s: Heart failure results from maladaptive multicellular remodeling triggered by sustained biomechanical stress. Although mechanical unloading can promote reverse remodeling, recovery is frequently incomplete and its mechanistic basis remains unclear. Using a reversible murine pressure-overload model combined with bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics, we demonstrate that reverse remodeling represents an actively maintained yet constrained multicellular state.

studi.t: Network modeling identifies vitamin B2 control of AIFM2 deficit-driven hepatocyte death in MASLD
studi.s: Drug discovery for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains difficult due to network effects. We developed MetaLiver, a public resource to identify druggable nodes within complex interactomes. It incorporates a MASLD-specific knowledge graph that improves bioactive compound contextualization while reducing computing time 18.8-fold. Layering progression-resolved bulk and hepatocyte-specific single-cell MASLD data onto this graph identified the vitamin B2-dependent flavoproteome (FlavProt) as an injury-sensitive network.

studi.t: A dynamic displacement mechanism drives protein import into mitochondria
studi.s: Most mitochondrial proteins are produced in the cytosol and imported through the translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane (TOM) to reach their final destination. Although this protein entry gate has been structurally characterized, it remains unclear how precursor proteins are handed off from the cytosolic receptor domains to the translocation pore. Here we show that the cytosolic domain of Tom22 - traditionally viewed as the central TOM receptor - acts not as a structured scaffold but as a largely disordered, flexible segment that plays an active role in precursor transfer.

studi.t: From Network Topology to Parameterization: An Optimized Model of Endothelial Mechanobiology
studi.s: Endothelial cells integrate biomechanical and biochemical cues to regulate vascular function, which can be modeled using signaling networks. Yet, the extent to which their signaling behavior is determined by network topology versus reaction-specific parameterization remains unclear. We developed a continuous logic-based ordinary differential equation model of endothelial signaling containing 70 species and 123 regulatory reactions assembled from the literature. Model predictions were evaluated against 79 literature-defined responses to imposed wall stress, wall shear stress, hypoxia, or TNF.

studi.t: Dynamic Hierarchical Interleaved Bloom Filter: An Updatable Index for Large-Scale Fast Sequence Search
studi.s: Motivation: A continued decrease in sequencing costs has facilitated the exponential increase in available sequencing data, with public databases like the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and Sequence Read Archive (SRA) reaching well in the order of petabases. This has been the incentive to develop more scalable tools for common bioinformatics tasks. One such task is the approximate searching of short sequence patterns like genes or reads in reference data sets. In recent years, a variety of indexing data structures have been proposed for searching large sequencing databases.

studi.t: Ribonucleotide Reductase Inhibition Overcomes FLT3 Inhibitor Resistance in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
studi.s: Internal tandem duplication mutations in FLT3 (FLT3ITD) occur in approximately 30% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and are among the most common genetic alterations in this disease. FLT3ITD is a major driver of AML and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Although FLT3 inhibitors (FLT3is) have significantly improved outcomes for patients with FLT3ITD+ AML, acquired resistance remains a major barrier to durable clinical benefit.

studi.t: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
studi.s: Across multiple timescales, neural rhythms coordinate cognitive and physiological processes. Slower rhythms are increasingly recognised as the scale at which autonomic and interoceptive processes are folded into ongoing cognition, a brain&body view of allostatic regulation that is particularly relevant to social interaction. Examining these slow components of the electroencephalogram (EEG) during real-time interaction remains challenging.

studi.t: Spatiospectral signatures of stomach-brain synchrony
studi.s: While cognitive neuroscience has increasingly recognized the brain-body connection, the temporal dynamics of how the stomach's intrinsic rhythm (~0.05 Hz) modulates human neural activity remain poorly understood. Leveraging high-resolution magneto- encephalography (MEG) and novel high-density electrogastrography (EGG), we provide the first comprehensive spatiotemporal mapping of human gastric-brain coupling at rest.

studi.t: Spreading depolarization, not seizure activity, drives immediate early gene expression in mouse cortex after electroconvulsive stimulation
studi.s: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective treatment for several psychiatric disorders, though its biological mechanisms remain unclear. ECT's therapeutic action has traditionally been attributed to the generalized seizure it induces. However, this view is challenged by the recent finding that electroconvulsive stimulation (ECS) can trigger a spreading depolarization (SD) in cortex.

studi.t: Decoding Articulatory and Phonetic Features: Somatotopic and Sensorimotor Representations in Native and Non-native Consonant Perception
studi.s: Speech perception relies on the integration of auditory and articulatory information, yet the precise role of motor regions remains debated. We combined fMRI with multivariate pattern analyses (MVPA) and behavioral measures to investigate cortical representations of native French and non-native Mandarin consonant perception under clear and noisy conditions.

studi.t: Peripheral detection of viruses shapes brain immunity and behavior in zebrafish
studi.s: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) are constantly exposed to pathogens, including viruses. However, serious brain infection via the olfactory route rarely occurs. When OSNs detect a virus, they coordinate local antiviral immune responses to stop virus progression to the brain. Despite effective immune control in the olfactory periphery, pathogen-triggered neuronal signals reach the CNS via the olfactory bulb (OB). We hypothesized that neuronal detection of a virus by OSNs initiates neuroimmune responses in the OB that prevent pathogen invasion.

studi.t: The bile acid receptor TGR5 is a modulator of the bone marrow microenvironment
studi.s: The gut is an emerging regulator of bone marrow (BM) hematopoiesis, with several molecules involved in this communication. Among them, bile acids (BAs) act as a relay between the microbiota and the rest of the body by activating specific receptors, including Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5). Although TGR5 has potent regulatory effects in immune cells, its role in the BM remains unclear. Here, we show that TGR5 is expressed across hematopoietic populations, including hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.

studi.t: Identification of a somatic H3K23me3 methyltransferase SET-19 in C. elegans
studi.s: Histone methylation plays essential roles in modulating chromatin organization and gene expression. H3K23 methylation is a conserved histone modification, yet its biological roles and the enzymes responsible for its deposition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the loss of set-19 leads to a pronounced reduction in H3K23 methylation in C. elegans, as revealed by quantitative mass spectrometry, western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. In vitro biochemical assays show that recombinant SET-19 proteins purified from E. coli directly catalyze H3K23 methylation.

studi.t: Can Folding Models Tell Binders from Bluffers? Evidence from POISK: The Patent-Derived Antibody Dataset
studi.s: Structure prediction models are increasingly deployed as zero-shot digital screens in antibody design, operating under the assumption that high folding confidence implies true binding. However, rigorous validation of this premise has been limited by small test sets, narrow target diversity, and the risk of data leakage from training-adjacent structures.

studi.t: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
studi.s: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks.

studi.t: Combined EZH1/2 and DNMT inhibition overcomes transcriptional barriers imposed by drug-induced epigenetic plasticity in colorectal cancer cells
studi.s: Abnormal DNA methylation patterning is a defining epigenetic hallmark of human cancers and is therapeutically targetable with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors (DNMTi's). However, epigenetic plasticity involving Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)-dependent H3K27 methylation can constrain transcriptional responses to DNMTi's and may contribute to their limited activity in solid tumors.

studi.t: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
studi.s: Aim: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has - especially in the thoracic area - characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results: We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS.

studi.t: Mathematical Modeling of the Canonical Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages
studi.s: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic sensing, as well as development, immunity, and tissue homeostasis. AhR signaling proceeds through a canonical and a non-canonical branch. It remains unclear which biochemical steps of the canonical pathway are responsible for distinct ligand specific transcriptional responses. Here, we developed a mechanistic ordinary differential equation model of the canonical AhR pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages.

studi.t: Acute FMR1 reduction alters cellular and circuit properties in human cortex
studi.s: Transcriptional silencing of FMR1 results in Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the leading inherited cause of intellectual disability (ID) and autism. Although the impact of FMR1 reduction on cortical function has been studied using the Fmr1-/y mouse model, mechanistic insights from the human brain are lacking. Here we show that acute FMR1 reduction in ex vivo human cortical slices induces transcriptomic changes that are concordant with those observed in FXS patient cortex, identifying many targets not altered in the Fmr1-/y mouse model.

studi.t: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
studi.s: Meditation encompasses diverse practices that train attention inward, unlike externally oriented task states. Which brain-activity features are shared across contemplative practices, which accompany long-term training, and which are tradition-specific remains unclear. We leveraged electroencephalography data from 226 participants: advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls. We developed a neurodynamic profiling approach spanning 21 features across four feature families: oscillatory, aperiodic, complexity and timescale.

studi.t: Loss of riboflavin biosynthesis leads to accumulation of select aromatic amino acids and loss of infectivity in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
studi.s: Riboflavin biosynthesis is required for in vitro survival of the human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). However, despite the lack of a known transporter, growth can be rescued by exogenous riboflavin. The riboflavin biosynthesis pathway is also predicted essential in vivo, but whether riboflavin levels available in the host can support survival has not been directly tested.

studi.t: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
studi.s: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. We developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Across cohorts, we find lineage-associated differences in centromere and non-centromeric array length, and show that heterochromatin components vary unequally within lineages. Yruler enables population-scale studies of how Y satellite variation relates to health and disease.

studi.t: CNVSIM: an interpretable cross-study copy-number reference atlas for cancer subtyping
studi.s: Genome-wide copy-number variation (CNV) profiles provide a representation of structural changes in cancer genomes, but interpreting new profiles with respect to their underlying biology remains challenging. We developed CNVSIM, which organizes CNV profiles into root-specific reference spaces and defines subtypes with chromosome-scale and gene-level signatures. Applied to the Progenetix dataset, CNVSIM established 112 CNV-defined subtypes across 19 cancer roots, supported by 155,881 neoplastic analyses from diverse studies and assay platforms.

studi.t: pH-driven dynamics and mechanisms of LNP-mediated siRNA delivery
studi.s: We present a comprehensive analysis of a clinically relevant DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3)-based lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation that exhibits strong short interfering RNA (siRNA, ~21 nt) delivery and potent inhibition of targeted RNAs. Using a combination of coarse-grained and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we characterize the pH-dependent structure of both unloaded and siRNA-loaded LNPs, elucidate the mechanism of siRNA encapsulation, and use these models to propose a plausible mechanism of endosomal escape.

studi.t: A general method for bootstrapping dense 3D segmentations from sparse 2D annotations
studi.s: Volumetric electron microscopy (vEM) provides unparalleled insight into cellular architecture, transforming our understanding of fundamental biological processes. Precise quantification of volumetric bioimaging data requires 3D instance segmentation, but the time and cost of manual ground-truth annotation present a major bottleneck for training accurate machine learning models. Our lightweight two-stage method generates complete 3D instance segmentations from sparse 2D annotations. A 2D network predicts dense boundaries on every section from minimal 2D labels.

studi.t: Synaptic pruning, myelination and the emergence of psychiatric disorders in late adolescence
studi.s: Adolescence is an important developmental period during which there are diverse changes in the brain and behavior. Goal-directed behaviors, including working memory, response inhibition, and reinforcement learning, improve during adolescence. At the same time there is substantial pruning of excitatory connections in prefrontal cortex and ongoing myelination of axons, which likely underlie these improvements in behavior. However, psychiatric disorders also become increasingly prevalent in late adolescence.

studi.t: Assessing multi-eGO Predictions of PDZ2-Peptide Binding across Mutations
studi.s: Accurately predicting how mutations alter protein-peptide binding remains challenging for molecular simulations because both conformational sampling and binding kinetics are computationally demanding. Here, we investigate whether multi-eGO, a hybrid transferable/structure-based atomistic-resolution model previously developed and validated for protein-small molecule interactions, can be transferred to protein-peptide binding.

studi.t: Network modularity reveals context and state-dependent reorganization of time-varying functional connectivity in single-cell resolved neural activity recordings
studi.s: An important goal of neuroscience is to understand how biological neural networks organize activity at multiple scales to enable complex information processing and behavioral output. To address this challenge, large-scale neural activity datasets with increased resolution and wider coverage have become more prevalent across many model systems. However, bridging the gap in scale between changes in pairwise functional connectivity between neurons and changes in brain-wide organization of activity remains a key challenge.

studi.t: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
studi.s: Anticipatory neurophysiological activity before unpredictable emotional events has been reported for decades, but the effects are small, difficult to replicate, and obtained almost exclusively in stripped-down laboratory paradigms. Whether they reflect genuine predictive processes or methodological artifacts remains debated; one rarely tested possibility is that such settings mute it.

studi.t: Immersive display systems for simulating natural vision
studi.s: Vision is traditionally studied using simplified stimuli presented briefly near the center of a flat display while subjects maintain visual fixation. This paradigm contrasts sharply with real-world vision, which is immersive, dynamic and strongly influenced by self-initiated actions. Traditional approaches have allowed researchers to systematically study the neural encoding of visual features and the influence of cognitive operations such as attention.

studi.t: Trust Modulates Speech Entrainment: Enhanced Cortical Tracking for Low Trust Speakers
studi.s: Trust is a critical component of human communication, providing a foundation for understanding, information exchange, and social coordination. Much of the research on trust in speech communication has focused on how vocal characteristics impact perceived trustworthiness. However, little is known about how trust in a speaker affects the neural processing of speech. Here, we demonstrate a two-stage experimental framework to study that question using non-invasive EEG.

studi.t: Precocious maturation and Purkinje cell dysfunction in the mouse Chd8 haploinsufficient cerebellum
studi.s: The cerebellum plays an emerging, but understudied, role in neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Mutations in CHD8 cause a monogenic NDD (CHD8-NDD) characterized by autism and other manifestations, and prior work in Chd8 mutant mice reported cerebellar abnormalities, raising the possibility of cerebellar contribution to CHD8-NDD. To characterize the impact of Chd8 haploinsufficiency on cerebellar development and function, we profiled the postnatal day 12 (P12) cerebellum of germline Chd8+/- mice using transcriptomic, morphological, and electrophysiological approaches.

studi.t: A cross-species protocol for ultrasound-guided intrauterine injections across gestation
studi.s: This step-by-step protocol provides a cross-species, non-surgical approach that enables prenatal gene delivery to the developing nervous system in rats and marmosets. Under transabdominal ultrasound guidance, intracerebroventricular viral injection (FIVI) of recombinant adeno-associated virus vectors into the fetal brain achieves robust and long-term transduction from prenatal stages into adulthood.

studi.t: Molecular quantification of Plasmodium falciparum ookinete load reveals associations with early immune responses in Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes
studi.s: The early stages of Plasmodium falciparum development in the mosquito are critical for parasite establishment and transmission, yet accurately quantifying parasite burden during ookinete maturation and midgut invasion remains challenging. Molecular markers of ookinete development offer an opportunity to investigate early infection dynamics and their association with mosquito immune responses at the individual mosquito level. In this study, we established a molecular approach to quantify ookinete load in individual Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes during the first 36 hours post-infection (hpi).

studi.t: Re-inventing sex: A W chromosome and a path out of parthenogenesis for Bunonematidae sp. nematodes
studi.s: Separate sexes are a conserved character across the tree of life but the molecular and genetic underpinnings of sex determination are remarkably diverse. Here we describe the evolution of a novel sex chromosome system in the nematode Bunonematidae sp. JU3390. Combining deep PacBio long read sequencing, HiC chromatin capture and Illumina sequencing of individual male and female Bunonematidae sp. JU3390 we identified an autosome-derived genomic segment currently functioning as a female-limited W chromosome.

studi.t: Physiological robustness of MScanFit to simulated motor unit loss and remodelling
studi.s: Introduction: MScanFit estimates motor unit number and size from compound muscle action potential (CMAP) scans, but its accuracy may depend on the physiological processes that shape motor unit loss and remodelling. We reproduced the general dynamic remodelling framework used in the original MScanFit simulation and expanded it to test MScanFit robustness across physiologically heterogeneous conditions. Methods: Generative computational models simulated CMAP scans from motor unit pools undergoing progressive loss from 160 to 5 surviving motor units.

studi.t: Structural recognition of an immunodominant glypican-3 peptide by a potent antitumor T-cell receptor
studi.s: Glypican-3 (GPC3) is a promising target in adoptive T-cell therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). TCR-A and TCR-B are two recently identified GPC3-specific TCRs recognizing the same HLA-A*02:01-restricted epitope but displaying markedly different therapeutic efficacy. To define the determinants of productive TCR-antigen recognition, we integrated high-resolution structures of both binary pMHC and ternary TCR:pMHC complexes, biolayer interferometry, peptide mutagenesis, target-cell conjugation assays, repetitive antigen challenge (RAC) and in vivo models.

studi.t: Golgi-endosomal CATCHR complexes function as organizing hubs for vesicle tethering and fusion
studi.s: Approximately one-third of all human proteins transit through the secretory pathway, where the Golgi apparatus orchestrates protein modification, sorting, and distribution through highly selective vesicle budding and fusion events. Central to these processes are the Complexes Associated with Tethering Containing Helical Rods (CATCHR), multisubunit tethering complexes that coordinate vesicle docking and fusion through interactions with coiled-coil tethers (CCTs), Rab GTPases, SNAREs, and Sec1/Munc18 (SM) proteins and other trafficking factors.

studi.t: Kymograph classifiers predict CMT2A disease-relevant mitochondrial motility phenotypes in iPSC motor neurons
studi.s: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2A (CMT2A) is a genetic disease characterized by autosomal dominant MFN2 mutations and dysregulated mitochondrial trafficking. While there is currently no FDA-approved CMT2A therapy, the recent development of iPSC motor neuron model systems, high-throughput imaging platforms, and CRISPR-based gene editing technologies holds promise for screening new therapies at scale in vitro.

studi.t: Rete Ridge Topography Regulates Epidermal Stem Cell Differentiation Programs and Chromatin Accessibility
studi.s: Stem cell niches regulate tissue homeostasis through biochemical and physical cues. Epidermal stem cells (EpiSCs) reside preferentially in the concave bases of rete ridges, which flatten with skin aging. Whether loss of this niche geometry contributes to EpiSC dysfunction in aging is unknown. We engineered flat and curved collagen matrices by 3D-bioprinting and found that concave topography promoted EpiSC differentiation and suppressed cell-cycle programs, with chromatin accessibility changes enriched for motifs of differentiation-associated transcription factors.

studi.t: Tissue-derived Activin signaling restrains regeneration after genotoxic stress in Schmidtea mediterranea
studi.s: Regenerative capacity depends on stem cells that replace missing tissues and signals that coordinate their activity. Following damage, particularly damage that targets stem cells, regeneration often fails. Yet, whether regeneration fails after stress because surviving stem cells lack regenerative potential or because tissue signals suppress their deployment remains unclear. Here, we show that sublethal genotoxic stress reversibly inhibits whole-body regeneration in the planarian Schmidtea mediterranea.

studi.t: Thermal plasticity of virulence differs between two latitudinally distant populations of the ash dieback pathogen
studi.s: Hymenoscyphus fraxineus is an invasive fungal pathogen responsible for the ash dieback epidemic, which continues to cause severe mortality of common ash (Fraxinus excelsior L.) across Europe. Following its likely introduction in northeastern Europe, the pathogen rapidly colonized most regions where common ash is present. As it spread southward, H. fraxineus encountered warmer climates and a higher occurrence of Fraxinus ornus L., a species resistant to the disease, which may have imposed novel selective pressures on H. fraxineus at the epidemic front.

studi.t: A Rarefaction Approach to Identify Local Introgression in a Three Population Tree
studi.s: The $D$ statistic, also known as the $ABBA-BABA$ statistic, is widely used to detect the presence of archaic genome-wide introgression between two non-sister taxa. $D$ counts the imbalance between the number of biallelic sites where either the second and third taxa (ABBA site) share the derived allele or the first and third taxa (BABA site) share the derived allele in a four taxa tree. Here, the fourth taxon acts as an outgroup to determine the ancestral allele.

studi.t: A genome-guided multilocus sequence analysis scheme to detect and resolve diversity within the X-disease phytoplasma group (16SrIII)
studi.s: Phytoplasmas of the X-disease group (16SrIII) cause economically important diseases of vegetables, forage and staple crops, fruit trees and ornamentals in South America, where they are diagnosed and classified only by 16S rRNA gene RFLP. Because this gene is highly conserved, strains that differ in host range, vectors and regulatory relevance cannot be distinguished. We developed a multilocus sequence analysis (MLSA) scheme for typing 16SrIII phytoplasmas, using genome data to select the markers and to define reference lineages.

studi.t: Performance Test of the QNome Nanopore Sequencer for Arthropod DNA Barcoding
studi.s: Nanopore sequencers have the potential to liberate DNA sequencing from centralized core facilities to distributed analytical nodes. Until recently, Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) had been the sole manufacturer of a portable nanopore sequencer, but analogous platforms are in production. Nanopore sequencers from Qitan Technology (QT) are widely used in China but have been unavailable outside that nation and have not been subject to rigorous, independent performance testing.

studi.t: Pathological LSD1 mutations repress enhancer-mediated gene regulatory networks in early differentiation
studi.s: Lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1/KDM1A) demethylates both histone and non-histone substrates, recruits repressive chromatin complexes, and is increased in cancers. De novo LSD1 mutations impairing protein function lead to a rare developmental disorder, but the molecular details of the pathology remains unclear. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, reprogrammed pluripotent stem cells, and differentiated cells, we found over 4000 differentially expressed genes and 68 transcription factors (TFs) whose motif accessibilities changed upon LSD1 mutation.

studi.t: Exploration of the structural and functional diversity in the metamorphic RfaH subfamily
studi.s: RfaH, a member of the universally conserved NusG/Spt5 family, activates transcription and translation of virulence genes by bridging the transcribing RNA polymerase to the translating ribosome. Unlike its monomorphic, constitutively active paralog NusG, RfaH fold-switches from an autoinhibited state, wherein its C-terminal domain forms an -helical hairpin bound to the N-terminal domain, into an active NusG-like state through C-terminal domain dissociation and refolding into a {beta}-barrel.

studi.t: Taccalonolide AJ uncouples tubulin GTP hydrolysis from microtubule depolymerization
studi.s: Microtubules are dynamic polymers of tubulin subunits that are vital for a variety of eukaryotic cell functions, including intracellular trafficking and cell division. Microtubule-targeting drugs are among the oldest and most widely used chemotherapeutics. Despite their extensive use, the development and optimization of these drugs is hindered by our limited understanding of the molecular impacts on microtubule structure and function.

studi.t: Beyond Sequence and Structure: Pretraining PLMs on Continuous Biophysical Fields
studi.s: The Biophysical Transformer is a protein language model that adds continuous biophysical fields as a third pretraining signal beside sequence and structure. A Poisson-Boltzmann solver computes the electrostatic potential around each three-residue token, and the model learns to predict it from sequence alone. A rotationally invariant spherical-harmonic descriptor serves as the loss target, eliminating the need for frame alignment during training and for coordinates at inference.

studi.t: Unraveling the Molecular Mechanisms of ABHD5 Membrane Targeting
studi.s: ABHD5 is a master regulator of PNPLA family lipases, particularly PNPLA2 (ATGL), the rate-limiting triglyceride (TAG) hydrolase in metabolic tissues. Despite its central role in lipid metabolism, the molecular basis by which ABHD5 recognizes membranes and regulates enzymatic activity remains poorly understood. Here, we report an integrated computational-experimental study revealing how /{beta}-hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5) dynamically engages lipid droplet (LD) and endoplasmic reticulum membranes.

studi.t: J-domain proteins bridge the PKL and ATRX complex to transcription factors to fine-tune gene expression via H3.3 deposition
studi.s: Epigenetic modifications, including histone modifications and DNA methylation, direct gene expression programs during the growth and development of eukaryotic organisms. In Arabidopsis thaliana, the chromatin remodeler PICKLE (PKL), a homolog of animal CHD3, plays a critical role during these processes. Previous studies of PKL have painted a complex picture of its function, including both activating and repressive roles, however, how PKL can control both transcriptional silencing and activation is unknown.

studi.t: Dissecting the functional heterogeneity of glutamatergic synapses with high-throughput optical physiology
studi.s: Fluorescent reporters for neurotransmitter release and Ca2+ signaling are essential tools for quantifying synapse function across neurons and circuits. However, leveraging these reporters requires scalable experimental frameworks. Here, we devised a high-throughput approach to efficiently collect and analyze hundreds of optical recordings of glutamate release activity using iGluSnFR3 at synapses in cultured rat hippocampal neurons.

studi.t: Primary and Supplementary Motor cortex implement parallel control solutions for rhythmic and discrete arm movements
studi.s: Arm movements are rhythmic, discrete, or some combination of the two. Conflicting evidence supports each of two possible solutions for how motor cortex controls them: that either it uses the same strategy for controlling rhythmic and discrete movements or different strategies for distinct movement types. Using recurrent neural network modelling and multi-unit recordings during an arm-cycling task, we show that primate motor cortex uses both solutions. Primary motor cortex (M1) dynamics converge to the same limit-cycle when executing both movement types.

studi.t: Self-generated cues and learned landmarks support spatial learning in Drosophila
studi.s: The ability to return to remembered goal locations is essential for animal survival. Although animals are known to use visual landmarks, how well they can exploit non-visual cues for spatial learning remains poorly understood. Here we show that Drosophila can combine learned olfactory cues with self-motion information to return to initially unmarked goals. In feature-poor arenas, flies assign positive value to self-deposited scents near the rewarded goal and combine these cues with self-motion cues to guide their return.

studi.t: IL18 and pyroptosis-related genes show contrasting expression in human cardiac pericytes and endothelial cells
studi.s: Interleukin-18 (IL-18) contributes to cardiac inflammation, fibrosis and contractile dysfunction, and its maturation and release involve inflammatory caspases and gasdermin D (GSDMD). In two discovery cohorts (42 and 38 donors), donor-paired comparisons of public single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from human hearts showed IL18 relatively enriched in pericytes and CASP1, CASP4 and GSDMD in endothelium. We specified these four directions as predictions and tested them against prespecified confirmation criteria in 22 adult non-failing donors from two additional resources.

studi.t: Convergent and divergent patterns of holobiont evolution in co-distributed chemosynthetic symbioses
studi.s: Intraspecific variation in microbial symbioses is shaped by a variety of ecological and evolutionary processes. In geographically separated populations, divergence in genomic traits is expected due to dispersal barriers and habitat differentiation, whereas sympatric populations might exhibit functional convergence to the characteristics of a shared environment. While these two processes have been well documented in many animal and plant species, they remain understudied in symbiotic systems.

studi.t: GlyComboCLI enables command line-based FAIR workflows for glycan composition assignment in mass spectrometry data
studi.s: Glycans are integral biomolecules whose presence cannot be predicted from genomic data alone, necessitating experimental characterisation through approaches including mass spectrometry. Assignment of glycan compositions to observed mass to charge ratios is computationally challenging due to the potential monosaccharide diversity and existing tools lack the required flexibility for integration into automated bioinformatic workflows.

studi.t: From strength to stability: muscular holding capacity characterized by Adaptive Force and its potential relevance for musculoskeletal complaints and non-contact injuries
studi.s: Musculoskeletal complaints and non-contact injuries remain poorly understood; conventional strength assessments show limited predictive value. They omit the function at which injuries occur--holding or braking under load. This is addressed by muscle stability quantified by Adaptive Force (AF)--the capacity to adapt to increasing loads while maintaining position. Available AF data were synthesized to characterize stable and unstable muscle states, evaluate parameter robustness, and explore practical relevance.

studi.t: In Vitro Budding and Floatation based enrichment of Mitochondria-derived Vesicles for Proteomics Mammalian Hearts
studi.s: Mitochondria-derived vesicles (MDVs) are carriers involved in mitochondrial quality control, yet their biogenesis and trafficking remain poorly understood. We describe an in vitro protocol to generate MDVs from animal heart mitochondria. The workflow allows for isolation of distinct MDV subsets and their proteomic analyses. The protocol improves vesicle yield and purity for NTA, TEM, or western blotting-based readouts. This facilitates the identification of novel MDV cargo and regulators of MDV biogenesis in different model organisms.

studi.t: Vegetation clump size and number as indicators for alternative stable states in semi-arid ecosystems
studi.s: Semi-arid ecosystems are vulnerable to desertification, a pressing issue in the face of global climate change due to the expected increase in aridity in drylands. In these ecosystems, vegetation often grows in spatially regular patterns that differ as aridity increases (gaps, labyrinths and clumps), which has been widely documented empirically and studied theoretically aiming to understand how these patterns relate to desertification.

studi.t: Evolutionary Design of Membrane-Lytic Antimicrobial Peptides with Mixture of Experts
studi.s: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) hold great promise in combating drug-resistant pathogens, yet current design models do not explicitly account for their primary mode of action, membrane disruption. To address this gap, we propose AMPainterV2, a model that designs membrane-lytic AMPs using generative adversarial imitation learning. AMPainterV2 integrates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) policy network to support insertion, deletion, and mutation operations, thereby expanding the evolutionary design space.

studi.t: Biomolecular Resolution as a Quantification of Structural Information Content
studi.s: Resolution is a poorly defined, ad hoc concept in structural biology, and multiple, seemingly conflicting definitions exist. In part, this ambiguity is because the structural information describing a biomolecule manifests in different ways depending upon the length scale being considered, while typical approaches to resolution just consider a single length scale.

studi.t: Distinct Hippocampal Cellular Pathologies Influence Cognition Across Diagnostic Categories and Distinguish Schizophrenia from Affective Psychosis
studi.s: Cognitive deficits are core features of psychosis and strong predictors of functional outcome, but are largely refractory to pharmacological treatments. It remains unresolved whether these deficits share cellular mechanisms across the psychosis spectrum (as in transdiagnostic models) or differ across DSM-5 diagnostic boundaries, particularly those separating schizophrenia from affective psychoses.

studi.t: Spatial Trophic Dynamics Shape and are Shaped by Desertification Transitions
studi.s: Drylands, which sustain billions of people, face desertification driven by climate change and grazing pressures. From the bottom up, desertification is affected by water availability, with vegetation often self-organising into spatial patterns that vary with aridity levels. However, how these patterns and, ultimately, desertification transitions are affected by the spatial dynamics of higher trophic levels remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce a spatially explicit tri-trophic model that links vegetation pattern formation to consumer-resource interactions and foraging behaviour.

studi.t: Toxin-associated genes cluster beyond gene family size expectations in both venomous and non-venomous animals
studi.s: Tandem arrays of toxin genes are widely read as a genomic signature of venom evolution. However, large gene families cluster whatever their function, so the baseline against which toxin clustering should be judged is unclear. We compared the clustering of toxin-associated genes with random genes and with non-toxin families of the same size in 14 independent venom origins, including a new chromosome-level genome and venom-gland proteome of the centipede Scolopendra mutilans, and applied the same analysis to toxin homologues of eight non-venomous animals.

studi.t: H9N2 avian influenza virus in Bangladesh: three genetically distinct co-circulating subgroups retain a largely conserved antigenic phenotype
studi.s: Low pathogenic avian influenza (LPAI) H9N2 viruses are endemic in poultry across Bangladesh, causing substantial economic losses and posing a persistent zoonotic risk. Although genetic surveillance has documented ongoing viral evolution, the relationship between genetic diversification and antigenic change remains poorly understood. This study investigated the genetic diversity, reassortment, and antigenic characteristics of contemporary H9N2 viruses circulating in Bangladesh.

studi.t: Diabetes-associated lung physiology shapes Klebsiella pneumoniae infection dynamics
studi.s: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with increased susceptibility to bacterial pneumonia, yet the mechanisms by which diabetic host physiology influences pathogen establishment remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated how diabetes-associated changes in the lung environment influence Klebsiella pneumoniae infection using leptin receptor-deficient (db/db) mice. Following acute lung infection, db/db mice exhibited increased bacterial burdens compared to nondiabetic controls, despite mounting a robust inflammatory cytokine response.

studi.t: Accessibility-guided targeting of NRF2-responsive long noncoding RNA NMRAL2P alters a distinct gene expression program and reduces non-small cell lung cancer proliferation
studi.s: Aberrant activation of the antioxidant transcription factor NRF2 promotes non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) survival and therapy resistance, but downstream effectors beyond redox regulation remain incompletely defined. Transcriptome profiling of lung and NSCLC cells identified the pseudogene-derived long noncoding RNA LOC344887/NMRAL2P as consistently associated with NRF2 activity. The NMRAL2P locus produces three predominant, nuclear-localized isoforms whose expression depends on NRF2 across normal lung, lung adenocarcinoma, and lung squamous carcinoma cells.

studi.t: AGPAT2 Inflammatory Metabolic Reprogramming Mediates Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-associated Myocarditis via LPAR5-pyroptosis Axis
studi.s: Objectives: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), especially programmed cell death protein-1 (PD1) inhibitors, are effective onco-therapeutic agents. However, ICI-associated myocarditis (ICIAM) greatly limits their clinical utility. Imbalance between 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferases (AGPAT2) and lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) induced by inflammatory metabolic reprogramming (IMRP) might cause cardiovascular injury. This study aims to explore the link between AGPAT2 pathway and ICIAM as well as identifies diagnosis and treatment targets of ICIAM.

studi.t: Scalable recorders of cellular calcium dynamics and molecular interactions across time
studi.s: Cellular processes are mediated by dynamic biochemical events in their native context, including changes in intracellular ion concentrations and transient interactions between molecules. Studying these processes across large cell populations requires recording their dynamics across time in single cells, simultaneously and at scale. Here, we introduce split-1POK, a split protein tape monomer whose two halves reconstitute when the domains fused to them interact.

studi.t: Gain-of-function mutations in 1-phosphofructokinase (FruK) re-establish glycolysis in bacteria
studi.s: Secondary (promiscuous) activities provide enzymes with a reservoir of latent catalytic functions, which can be leveraged during selective pressure. Here we retrace the re-emergence of glycolysis from the promiscuous activity of 1-phosphofructokinase (FruK). We evolved a hexose-degradation-deficient Escherichia coli strain on glucose and recovered non-synonymous mutations in fruK. Reverse engineering, gene deletions and transcript quantification identified a modified and strongly overexpressed fruK as the determinant of the growth phenotype.

studi.t: Optimizing Avian Influenza Viral RNA Enrichment from Water: A Comparison of Concentration Methods for Low-Volume Samples
studi.s: Feed-baited water bins may provide a complementary approach for avian influenza virus (AIV) surveillance in wild waterbird populations. In a previous study, water from these bins was sampled using swabs after exposure to visiting birds, but the low sample volume limited the detection and subsequent characterization of AIV RNA (F. I. Rondi, J. Neumann-Heise, T. Harder, V. Allendorf, K. Depner, T. Homeier-Bachmann, L. Breuer, S. Knauf, S. Dreyer, and A. Globig, One Health 23:101548, 2026, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101548).

studi.t: High-Throughput Screen of Advanced Repurposing Library Identifies Compounds Active Against Acute and Chronic Stages of Toxoplasma gondii
studi.s: Toxoplasma gondii, a pathogen with a global burden impacting millions, has the capability to interconvert between the actively replicating tachyzoite form into a semidormant bradyzoite for, complicating treatment.
